title: Former military secretary alleges attempt to alter official records of Oct. 7 massacre timeline
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's former military secretary, Avi Gil, told N12 News and Israel Hayom on Thursday that Netanyahu's chief of staff allegedly tried to change the official record of the prime minister's schedule.Shortly before leaving his position, Gil made sure the entire contents of his notebooks were digitized and stored on a classified computer in the Military Intelligence Directorate. "A state commission of inquiry will receive everything I have on the day it is established, including what I have to say," he clarified.He explained in the interview that at the end of October 2023, weeks after the start of the war, several people approached him about collecting transcripts of the day. Recounting the hours leading up to the attack, Gil said intelligence reports circulated through the security establishment's systems overnight, reaching computers in the offices of the head of the Research Division and the Military Intelligence Directorate.At 3:55 a.m., an intelligence assistant received an alert about a message detailing suspicious actions near the Gaza border that were called "routine," and it said another consultation would take place later that day. Based on that, the assistant decided not to wake either the prime minister or the military secretary, believing the situation was not urgent enough to warrant doing so.'We are at war'At 6:12 a.m., Gil said he was awakened by a phone call from the office of former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) chief Ronen Bar, who asked him to return the call using the secure red telephone. When asked what the call was about, Bar replied in one word: "South."At 6:17 a.m., he called back and was briefed on suspicious indicators, including the activation of SIM cards and reports of Hamas operatives moving underground.At 6:29 a.m., he woke Netanyahu with a phone call over a non-secure line and informed him: "Hamas has launched extensive fire, a large-scale surprise attack. I am gathering information and will call you as soon as possible."Eleven minutes later, at 6:40 a.m., he called the prime minister again and told him: "We are at war.""In January, one of the stenographers approached me and told me she had been instructed to retrieve the transcript of that 6:40 a.m. phone call and had been instructed [by Netanyahu's then chief of staff, Tzachi Braverman] to change the time of the call from 6:40 to 6:29," Gil said in the interview.Asked why someone would want to change the times, Gil said, "Someone was dealing with particular narratives," adding that he quietly flagged the incident to the attorney-general during a meeting."It was important for me to document it so that if someone later came along and presented evidence of things that I had documented differently, that I remembered differently, and that contradicted the transcripts of organizations and the memoranda recorded by people in various places, we would have an example of it, the falsification," he stated.He said that aside from the change made to the time stamp of the phone call, he did not know of other changes."Nevertheless, I have one recommendation for the commission of inquiry that will be established, and for the State Comptroller, who obtained transcripts: Do not rely solely on the transcripts," he urged. "Demand the original recordings. Listen to them."Regarding the hostages, Gil stated that Israel could have returned the hostages earlier; he said, "We could have."PM's ex-military secretary: 'What the public is being told is not what actually happened'Gil also rejected claims that betrayal had led to the massacre."There was no betrayal," he clarified, warning that those spreading such allegations were undermining the resilience of Israeli society. "There were failures. The system failed utterly... Anyone who alleges betrayal without a shred of evidence is not only spreading a lie, but is also harming the resilience and strength of this wonderful thing called Israel."Gil said that he thought he would be speaking to a state commission of inquiry about the massacre, which is why he kept his accounts of the day private. He now believes that one will never be formed, which is why he felt he needed to speak about his experience on October 7. "Three years have passed since October 7, and two years since I retired from the IDF. I hoped a state commission of inquiry would be established to investigate everything. Unfortunately, that hasn't happened, and I doubt it will.”"In the past few weeks, I realized I had to come out and say what I knew. Because we saw what happened recently when there is no investigation," he said, referencing the incident of the flydubai flight.“What the public is being told is not what actually happened,” he added. “This isn't my truth. It's the country's truth.”"I think we are tearing Israeli society apart because of the lies," he said, adding that there are discrepancies between what the public has been told and what actually happened, calling for the formation of a state commission of inquiry.Gil told reporters that Netanyahu had heard several warnings before the October 7 massacre about suspicious activity in Gaza, but they were all shot down. "October 7 was Israel's failure. Netanyahu heard it all from agency heads, everything that was known. There were suggestions to do targeted strikes in Gaza from time to time, but they were all denied."He also recounted that in July 2023, while Netanyahu was hospitalized, former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) head Ronen Bar requested to speak with him and warned of the possibility of war.Touching on the recent reports of warnings given to Netanyahu from Emirati President Mohammed bin Zayed and Egypt, he stated that he had not been in the PMO during the dates of the talks between the prime minister and MZB, and had not been aware until recently of matters with Egypt.However, he said that a plane often used by Egyptian intelligence had landed in Israel for about an hour, citing recent reports. "An aircraft like that came for a purpose. I believe someone in Israel can shed light on what happened, one way or another."Gil concluded by placing the responsibility for the failures of October 7 on Netanyahu. "I do not understand in what world it is possible to separate the concept of leadership from the concept of responsibility," he said. "There is no leadership without responsibility."Walla contributed to this report.

title: UK counterterror police arrest two Latvian men under National Security Act for RAF base incursion
body: British counterterrorism police are investigating two Latvian men who were arrested near a Royal Air Force base in Cambridgeshire in the early hours of Thursday, police said in a statement.The men were initially arrested on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and criminal damage, then re-arrested on suspicion of an offense under the National Security Act 2023 - namely "entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK"."We're very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week," Helen Flanagan, Head of counterterrorism Policing London, said in a statement.She was referring to a separate incident at the Fairford airbase, which had been used by US bombers to strike Iran, in which several men were arrested over a suspected plot which the government has linked to Iran.Abandoned vehicle checked by bomb disposal unitIn relation to Thursday's arrests, police said they were also carrying out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area in connection with the investigation.An abandoned vehicle was recovered by police and later checked by bomb disposal officers; however, nothing of concern was found.

title: Netanyahu, Smotrich hold conference to rally right-wing voters, excluding Ben-Gvir
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich held a joint conference in Jerusalem on Thursday, seeking to mobilize right-wing voters and increase turnout ahead of the October 27 elections.The joint conference came after Netanyahu's ruling Likud party and Smotrich's far-right Religious Zionist Party (RZP) signed a surplus vote-sharing agreement on Tuesday. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's far-right Otzma Yehudit party – also part of Netanyahu's coalition bloc – subsequently stated that Likud had refused to sign a surplus-vote agreement with it.Ben-Gvir was not invited to the conference, titled Saving the Right, which included dozens of Religious Zionist rabbis, along with heads of yeshivas.“We are taking the energy of the communities and institutions, and with them we are going into the elections full force,” Smotrich said at the conference in Jerusalem.“They will explain, persuade, recruit, motivate, and get people out to vote. With God's help, we can bring victory to the national camp and continue all the wonderful processes in settlement, security, Torah, education, Jewish identity, and extensive social work,” he added.Netanyahu: Right coming together is 'matter of national survival'Netanyahu praised Smotrich for his work as finance minister throughout the government's term, while speaking at the conference.“I'm talking about all those crossroads over these past three years when we had to overcome, together, pressure from within and from abroad to surrender, give in, retreat, and bow our heads,” Netanyahu said.“This is not only a matter of national honor – it is a matter of national survival,” he added.RZP stated that the goal of the conference was to “create a broad network of thousands of activists with the aim of bringing tens of thousands of right-wing voters to the polls.”Recent polls have shown that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition bloc seeking to replace him can secure a majority without support from Arab parties. A Wednesday Channel 13 poll projected 55 seats for Netanyahu's bloc and 50 for the opposition bloc, excluding Arab parties.On Tuesday, Otzma Yehudit had accused Likud of seeking to form a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party and the leading candidate for prime minister in the opposition bloc in recent polling.Ben-Gvir on Thursday posted a picture of Smotrich at the joint conference on social media, alongside the message, “I love every Jew.”אני אוהב כל יהודי   https://t.co/aAWHZ1JFxW— איתמר בן גביר (@itamarbengvir) October 8, 2026Unclear if Otzma Yehudit will sign surplus-vote agreement It remains unclear whether Otzma Yehudit will sign a surplus-vote agreement before the approaching submission deadline.The RZP party platform has focused on Jewish identity, settlement expansion, and Israeli sovereignty in the West Bank.The party has recently faced criticism over its support for contentious legislation advanced by Netanyahu's coalition in the Knesset and sponsored by the haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties. Critics argued that the legislation encouraged draft evasion amid the IDF's severe manpower crisis.Smotrich has pushed to expand Israeli settlements in the West Bank, with over 100 initiated during his tenure, sparking international condemnation.In the previous election, RZP ran on a joint ticket with Otzma Yehudit, allowing both parties to cross the electoral threshold.In August, Netanyahu urged Ben-Gvir and Smotrich to join forces again in the upcoming election to strengthen the right-wing bloc, but Ben-Gvir refused.

title: Israel's defense ministry opens first ever pavilion at Marrakech Airshow 2026
body: Israel's Defense Ministry and top defense industry entities on Thursday inaugurated their first official participation in the defense exhibition held in Morocco since the signing of the Abraham Accords. It is also the first time that the ministry has debuted an Israeli national pavilion and headed a delegation of Israeli defense industries at the show.This participation took place as Israel has been banned or its participation reduced by France and various other Western allies due to their criticism of its conduct during the Gaza war.Criticism of Israel has continued even as the IDF has observed its commitment not to invade Hamas-held parts of Gaza since a general ceasefire in October 2025; while Israel and Hamas have pointed fingers over who is holding up progressing toward the later stages of the ceasefire agreement, such as disarming and rebuilding.Senior defense officials from the Kingdom of Morocco visited the Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) pavilion at Marrakech Airshow 2026, October 8, 2026.Eight Israeli defense companies exhibited advanced, combat-proven technologies at the Marrakesh show, including loitering munitions, AI-powered robotic systems, autonomous navigation capabilities for UAVs, laser guidance for FPV drones, satellite communications, and other items.Alongside the ministry paviilion, Israel's three major defense industries, Elbit Systems, Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), and Rafael, were present at the exhibit, presenting solutions across the air, land, sea, space, intelligence, cyber, and digital domains.Israel opens national pavilion in Morocco to expand defense exports and international cooperationThe opening of the Israeli national pavilion at the Marrakech Airshow is part of the ministry's strategy to increase defense exports and defense cooperation with countries worldwide.This strategy serves as a tool to strengthen the IDF's force buildup, influence foreign policy, and bolster the Israeli defense industry and economy. During the exhibition, meetings were held with delegations and government officials from various countries.Head of the Defense Ministry's International Defense Cooperation Directorate (SIBAT) Brig.-Gen. (res.) Yair Kulas said, “Israel's first-ever participation in an exhibition in Morocco marks an important milestone for the Israeli Ministry of Defense and the Israeli defense industry. The companies that exhibited at the show brought combat-proven technologies alongside innovation in autonomy, artificial intelligence, and communications. SIBAT serves as a gateway to Israel's defense ecosystem, and this exhibition served as a platform for expanding international defense cooperation and building long-term partnerships as part of advancing the Ministry of Defense's strategy.”

title: As UK consulate closes, Sa'ar vows Israel will enact consequences on hostile countries - exclusive
body: “The time of containment in the face of hostile [acts] against the State of Israel is over,” Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said Thursday, warning that Britain's Labour government risks losing its influence in the region as Jerusalem responds to a series of sanctions and diplomatic measures.Speaking in an interview with The Jerusalem Post at the newspaper's Diplomatic Conference in Jerusalem, Sa'ar defended his decision to shut down the British Consulate in Jerusalem on Thursday – the deadline for closure – saying, “Every state that works and acts against the State of Israel must understand that we will take our revenge.”The decision to close the consulate is the latest in a series of retaliatory measures following the British government's imposition of sanctions on Israel on September 8.In addition to closing the British Consulate in Jerusalem, Israel has removed British representatives from the International Gaza Support Center in Kiryat Gat, terminated British training activities for Palestinian Authority (PA) security forces in the West Bank, and barred 12 British elected officials from entering the country, along with other British citizens accused by Israel of antisemitic or anti-Israel activity.The closure also means the departure of approximately 20 British diplomats, including the consul general, from the Jerusalem mission.British consulate in east Jerusalem downgraded to limited diplomatic mission Sa'ar authorized the British government to operate a task force of only seven diplomats in the mission building with a limited scope of activity.He told the Post that Israel had deliberately targeted areas in which the United Kingdom previously maintained a diplomatic or security presence, including Jerusalem, the West Bank, and Gaza.“Any country that pursues a one-sided and unbalanced policy against Israel will lose its influence and relevance in our region, including in Gaza and Jerusalem.”“We didn't choose this path. It was the Labour government that chose that. But we had to react,” he said.Sa'ar accuses UK Labour government of increasingly hostile policies toward IsraelSa'ar accused the Labour government, which came to power in July 2024, of pursuing an increasingly “hostile” policy toward Israel, pointing to measures targeting Israeli officials, organizations, trade negotiations, and military cooperation.Despite the deterioration in relations, Sa'ar insisted that diplomatic dialogue between Jerusalem and London would continue.“I'm always for dialogue,” he said, although he expressed little optimism about a significant change in British policy under the current government.Asked whether he believed relations could recover while Labour remained in power, Sa'ar pointed to the party's recent conference, claiming that government ministers had avoided an event organized by Labour Friends of Israel while attending one hosted by Labour Friends of Palestine.“I believe this tells you the direction, and therefore I want to be realistic,” he said. “It doesn't mean we don't give [them] a chance. We always give a chance for a different path.”Sa'ar says Britain risks undermining valuable intelligence and security cooperation with IsraelThe foreign minister also stressed that Israel continued to provide the UK with valuable assistance in intelligence and security cooperation, suggesting that London was undermining a relationship from which it benefited.“We help the Brits: security, intelligence, a lot of issues. They know it,” he said. “I think they are making a mistake in their approach.”Sa'ar drew a distinction between legitimate criticism of Israeli government policy and what he described as punitive action against the Jewish state.“It's one thing to criticize, and it's a different thing to act against you,” he said.Colombia to open embassy in Jerusalem next weekTurning to Israel's wider diplomatic relations, Sa'ar announced that Colombia would inaugurate an embassy in Jerusalem on October 14, thus becoming the 10th country to establish an embassy in the Israeli capital.“Next Wednesday, we are going to inaugurate the 10th foreign embassy in Jerusalem, which will be the Colombian embassy,” he told the conference.“When I entered my ministry, it was less than two years ago, there were five [embassies in Jerusalem]. Next week, we're going to have 10.”Sa'ar also revealed that Israel had already reached an agreement with the Democratic Republic of the Congo to open an embassy in the capital, which would become the 11th foreign diplomatic mission in the city.“We already agreed about the 11th embassy with DRC. And that will be very soon,” he said.Sa'ar hopes more countries, including Brazil, will open embassies in JerusalemThe foreign minister expressed hope that additional countries, including Brazil, could eventually follow, linking the expansion of Jerusalem's diplomatic presence to Israel's efforts to strengthen its international standing.“This is a diplomatic battle over the truth,” Sa'ar said, arguing that Jerusalem's historical connection to the Jewish people remained central to Israel's diplomatic efforts.“Jerusalem was always the capital of one nation, and that's the Jewish people, from the times of King David more than 3,000 years ago, until this very day,” he said.Returning to the UK in his closing remarks, he suggested that London's refusal to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital did nothing to diminish that historical connection.“Everyone knows Jerusalem,” Sa'ar said, “even if it is not recognized by the foreign secretary of the United Kingdom.”

title: US will recognize Palestinian state after Trump's term ends in two years, Liberman claims
body: Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman warned that the United States is expected to recognize a Palestinian state within approximately two years, claiming that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is aware of the move and is working to advance it.Speaking at a recent conference at Reichman University's Shabtai Shavit World Summit on Counterterrorism, Liberman accused Netanyahu of deliberately letting the process move forward, saying that by the time it happens, “he will no longer be prime minister.”“The Netanyahu family's approach is that if Bibi is not prime minister, then let this country burn,” Liberman said. According to him, the alleged Palestinian state would encompass “all of Judea and Samaria, the Jordan Valley, Gaza, and east Jerusalem. And this is something that will be almost impossible to reverse.”Previously, The Jerusalem Post reported on Yisrael Beytenu's proposal for the West Bank and Gaza Strip, including handing Jordan the responsibility for public order and the day-to-day lives of Palestinians in Areas A and B of the West Bank, while Israel retains territorial contiguity and security responsibility.Yisrael Beytenu's plan also calls for dismantling the Palestinian Authority and canceling the Oslo Accords.Liberman stated that he had, earlier this week, spoken with US State Department and the National Security Council officials and that “everyone, across the board, supports recognition of a Palestinian state.""I am telling you with 200% certainty, the Americans will lead a resolution in the [United Nations] Security Council, and the Palestinians will become a state in every sense of the word, a full member of the UN."בעוד כשנתיים וחצי ארה"ב תכיר במדינה פלסטינית בכל שטחי יו"ש, בקעת הירדן, רצועת עזה ומזרח ירושלים. כל הפקידות הבכירה במחלקת המדינה ובמועצה לביטחון לאומי בארה"ב – כולם, ללא יוצא מן הכלל, תומכים באופן גורף בהכרה כזאת. זה לא קרה עד היום כי ישראל הצליחה לנטרל את העמדה המסוכנת הזאת בזכות מעמד חזק מאוד בדעת הקהל האמריקאית, ועקב כך זכתה גם לתמיכה פוליטית רחבה בשתי המפלגות. אבל בפוליטיקה יש כלל ברזל: ברגע שאתה מאבד את התמיכה הציבורית, אתה מאבד את התמיכה הפוליטית. היום מצבנו בדעת הקהל האמריקאית בשפל חסר תקדים. הנשיא הבא שייבחר בעוד כשנתיים, לא משנה אם יהיה רפובליקני או דמוקרטי, ילך למהלך של הכרה במדינה פלסטינית, כולל העברת החלטה במועצת הביטחון של האו"ם על הכרה כמדינה חברה מלאה באו"ם. מה שעושה היום נתניהו הוא למעשה סיוע ביודעין להקמת מדינה פלסטינית. ביבי יכנס להיסטוריה כמייסד המדינה הפלסטינית. עד הבחירות הבאות בארה"ב יש כשנתיים. עד אז מדינת ישראל חייבת להגדיר מהו האנד גיים בנוגע לרשות הפלסטינית ולשטחי יו"ש, בקעת הירדן ורצועת עזה. להתעלם מהבעיה, לתת לדברים לזרום ולחכות עד שזה יתפוצץ לנו בפנים – זה דפוס ההתנהלות של נתניהו לאורך השנים. כך הוא התעלם מהאזהרות שלי בנוגע לחמאס ברצועת עזה, ומשך זמן עד שזה התפוצץ לנו בפנים ב-7 באוקטובר. אבו מאזן התחיל במהלך מתוכנן ומחושב שיתחיל ב-28 בנובמבר בבחירות לפרלמנט הפלסטיני, ומשם לעימות רחב עם ישראל, שילווה אותנו עד הבחירות לנשיאות ארה"ב בנובמבר 2028. לנו אסור לשבת בחיבוק ידיים. היעד והאנד גיים של ישראל צריך להיות חיסול החמאס ברצועת עזה ופירוק הרשות הפלסטינית, כולל ביטול הסכמי אוסלו. אבל מכיוון שאין ואקום בעולם, ומי שעלולים לתפוס את המושכות עם פירוק הרשות, הם חמאס והג'יהאד האסלאמי, אנחנו חייבים לסכם מראש עם הקהילה הבינלאומית מי יקח את השליטה והניהול ביו"ש וברצועת עזה. אני מדגיש: אני מתנגד בתוקף לחזרה לתקופת הממשל הצבאי ולאחריות ולניהול ישראלי של חיי היומיום של הפלסטינים בשכם, טול כרם, רפיח, חאן יונס וערים אחרות. ירדן יכולה להיות המדינה שתכנס במקום הרשות ותנהל את חיי היומיום של הפלסטינים ביו"ש, כולל שמירה על הסדר הציבורי באמצעות כוח שיטור. הירדנים לא יכניסו צבא או כל כוח אחר מעבר לכוח השיטור. האחריות הביטחונית על כל שטחי יו"ש תשאר בידי צה"ל. השת"פ הביטחוני עם ירדן הוכיח את עצמו מזה עשרות שנים. אנחנו חולקים גבול ארוך של 300 ק"מ. עקבה נושקת לאילת והמרחק בין הגבול לבית שאן הוא 5 ק"מ. מי שנמצאים בעיקר לאורך הגבול, אלו חיילים ירדנים ששומרים על השקט. לגבי עזה, יש גורמים רציניים בעולם הערבי שיהיו מוכנים לקחת אחריות על חיי היומיום, אבל זה יקרה רק לאחר שישראל תשלים את המלאכה ותמגר את שלטון החמאס. זאת התוכנית שלי והאנד גיים שאני מציע לפתרון הסוגיה הפלסטינית. אני אשמח לשמוע מראשי כל המפלגות ולהבין מה הפתרונות וההצעות שלהם בסוגיה.— אביגדור ליברמן (@AvigdorLiberman) October 8, 2026He also warned that the Palestinians are preparing for an “all-out confrontation” against Israel, claiming that its first stage would take place at the Palestinian Authority elections scheduled for November.Further, he criticized Israel's lack of preparedness and accused Netanyahu of pursuing a policy of avoiding proactive measures."I am telling you that Netanyahu is acting to bring about a Palestinian state and wants one to be established,” he said. “Because through inaction and restraint, when we take no initiative whatsoever, we will have no grounds for complaint."“I am telling you, if Netanyahu thinks I am wrong, he is welcome to file a complaint against me, sue me in court, and I pledge to waive my parliamentary immunity at that very moment."He added that he does not believe that there would be a recognition of a Palestinian state under US President Donald Trump's tenure, "but we must use these two years to prevent the disaster."Netanyahu a 'burden to Trump,' dismantled US-Israel ties, Liberman tells 'Post'In July, Liberman told the Post that Netanyahu had dismantled Israel's relationship with the United States and had become a “burden” to Trump.“Trump wants to distance himself from him [Netanyahu]. The relationship has become a burden, and it is already hurting him in the upcoming US midterm elections," Liberman said at the time.Liberman told the Post that the US president has “understood that he had given too much,” and was being harmed by Netanyahu “both electorally and politically.”“This is also a severe blow to Israel's standing in American public opinion,” Liberman added. “There has never been such a negative attitude. The more Gaza declines, the more Israel's image declines as well.”When asked whether he would say no to Trump if he were prime minister, Liberman did not hesitate.“I would,” he said. “I've been involved in the leadership of this country for about 20 years, and Israel has already weathered some of its toughest disputes with the United States.”“With all due respect, we need to act. We are still a sovereign country. We are not a banana republic.”Keshet Neev contributed to this report.

title: Israel assassinated Iran's navy chief over fears he could lead a more dangerous IRGC - exclusive
body: One of the key reasons for the assassination of Iran navy chief Alireza Tangsiri by Israel on March 26 was the concern of top Israeli officials that he could emerge as the next head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, The Jerusalem Post has learned.He would have been a much tougher adversary than Ahmad Vahidi, who eventually became the new IRGC chief.Many top Israeli officials viewed Tangsiri as a highly creative and resourceful commander, whereas Vahidi was largely seen as a deputy to a deputy of top commanders, lacking the power to shape the broader security posture.These revelations come out following recent reports, first in Yediot Aharonot and later confirmed by the Post, that around March 19, Cooper made a secret call to IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir to request that Israel eliminate Tangsiri, considered a serious threat to the Strait of Hormuz and the naval conflict in general.Zamir approved, and on March 26, Israel assassinated Tangsiri.US request to eliminate Tangsiri raises questions over Iranian naval mining threatThe Post has also disclosed several other details about the assassination in recent reports, including the crucial role of the Israeli Navy in providing intelligence.This incident raised the question of why would Cooper secretly call Zamir on March 19 to ask him to remove Tangsiri as a threat, if US sources want to claim in general that Iran was not carrying out significant, real sea-mining until the conflict paused sometime in mid-April - something the Post can now also reveal.The Post has learned that the US was confused and had varying levels of confidence when they learned of Iranian discussions about what Tehran was really thinking about doing regarding miningWhatever the concerns were, both Israeli and American sources have acknowledged that they were not the same as issuing actual orders on the matter.In that sense, the Post understands that Cooper's call to Zamir was, in many senses, a call for a preemptive move to head off a possible future strategic problem.From the Israeli perspective, there were multiple reasons to assassinate Tangsiri, including concerns about his potential future role in the IRGC, and Cooper's call helped push forward an operation that already had support.

title: Houthis abduct, indoctrinate kids to believe they are fighting Jews, Yemeni journalist tells 'Post'
body: The Houthis have forcibly recruited children to fight in their war against Saudi Arabia and the Saudi-backed government, threatening families in territories they control and indoctrinating young people to believe they will be fighting against Jews and Zionists, a journalist who formerly worked in Houthi-controlled territory for a decade told The Jerusalem Post on Wednesday.“A,” who spoke on condition of anonymity, explained that he feared the Houthis would punish his friends and colleagues still working in Yemen if they became aware of his communication with the Post. He noted that the Houthis are already holding several international humanitarian workers hostage, in addition to local aid employees.Human Rights Watch (HRW) announced earlier this week that the Houthis have already sent at least eight people involved in human rights and humanitarian work for criminal prosecution on espionage-related charges punishable by death, since August 18.Though the Houthis' use of child soldiers has long been documented, A said, “The problem is escalating and increasing with the recent developments.”Houthis threaten citizens with death in order to recruit more soldiers “Whenever they control new areas, the first thing they do is force people to be recruited. Otherwise, they will be punished, they will be imprisoned, or they will be killed,” he explained.“So this is one of the most significant issues and one of the least reported issues when it comes to the war in Yemen, and Houthis also want to compensate for what they lost over the past days because they lost a lot of fighters in Mokha and in their recent fighting and battles.”On the day that A spoke to the Post, he received a call from humanitarian contacts on the ground in Houthi-controlled territory warning him that the Houthis had begun indiscriminately shelling homes and schools and that bodies of women and children were being piled high.Given that A spent years working in Houthi-controlled territory, the Post asked him how the Houthis could justify killing Yemeni civilians, particularly given that the vast majority of their victims are Muslim.Explaining that the reason the Houthis are comfortable killing their own people is the same reason that makes a peace agreement with them impossible, A said that it was “firmly” embedded in their ideology that they have the “divine right to govern... not only controlling all of Yemen, but also they want to control Mecca and Medina and Saudi Arabia.”“They believe that they have the divine right to govern the world, not only the Arabian Peninsula, and so they consider people who fight them or who try to resist them as traitors, and recently as Zionists,” he continued, adding that the issue has only worsened since October 7, 2023.Houthis use Israel-Hamas War to recruit child soldiers A said the Israel-Hamas War had been a “good excuse to recruit,” with videos of the war in Gaza regularly played to children to incite them against Israel. He added that, before October 7, there had been growing discontent with the Houthis, particularly over unpaid wages; still, many were more willing to tolerate the missed payments either because they wanted to support the Palestinian cause or because they did not want to be labeled as Zionists.Estimating that tens of thousands of children had been enlisted into the Houthis' ranks since Hamas's invasion, A noted that children aged between 12 and 15 had been captured attempting to fight government forces, proclaiming that they had traveled to the front to fight the Jews.The anti-Israel popular opinion in Yemen among the entire population, A said, had also made the indoctrination of children easier, as many didn't need to shift their thinking on the issue dramatically to align with the Houthis.“They exploited what they called the Islamic background and people's support for the Palestinian cause,” he said, adding that it has now begun to backfire and there is a growing number of Yemenis who feel resentful toward the Palestinians.“People are fed up even with the Palestinian cause because it has caused a lot of damage to the country. The sentiment of people toward the Gaza issue and the Palestinian cause has gone down sharply because they saw how the Houthis decided to kill Yemenis in the name of Gaza.“They saw how the Houthis isolated Yemen by attacking vessels in the Red Sea in the name of Gaza. They saw how the Houthis even cut the income of thousands of fishermen who went jobless because of the Houthis' ventures in the Red Sea,” A added.“So people saw the economic consequences of the Houthis' actions over the past three years and started complaining and also started realizing that the Palestinian cause is not our cause. Yemen is our cause. So this sentiment has shifted dramatically, but they continued to recruit and mobilize support inside Yemen in the name of fighting the US and Israel.”Adding to the bitterness, A said it was hard watching pro-Palestinian activists in the West celebrate the Houthis and ignore comments from Yemenis trying to tell them that the group was a terrorist organization even if it partially aligned with their viewpoint.“Gaza became a trend and profitable thing for many people, including Palestinians, and the shocking fact is how many Palestinian activists, journalists, and thinkers turn and support the Houthis at the expense of Yemenis and at the expense of Yemeni suffering,” A said.

title: Nikos Karvelas Takes Back Control: He Will Decide Who Can Sing His Songs Live
body: ‘End of an era’: Composer withdraws live-performance licensing authority from Self-Management as dispute with Anna Vissi escalates Nikos Karvelas has taken a major new step in his escalating public dispute with Anna Vissi, reclaiming personal control over the licensing of his songs for live performances. The decision means the composer will now personally decide whether, when and under what conditions third parties can receive permission to perform his musical works live. The move includes songs that have become closely associated with Vissi throughout their decades-long musical partnership. Karvelas has withdrawn the authority previously held by the collective management organisation Self-Management (OSD) to license the live public performance of his works, including concerts and live appearances at entertainment venues. According to an official announcement issued by his lawyer, Archontoula Papapanagiotou, the withdrawal took effect on September 30, 2026 , under Article 12, paragraph 2 of Greek Law 4481/2017. Karvelas will personally decide who can perform his songs The legal announcement states that Self-Management can no longer grant third parties licences for the live performance of the works covered by the withdrawal. Those rights will instead be exercised directly by Karvelas. That gives the composer control over whether a performer can use his songs in a concert, live appearance or other form of live performance. The announcement makes clear that Karvelas will decide whether, when, under what conditions and to whom such permissions are granted. It also states that he will have the final say over the circumstances under which his works are presented. The decision does not, by itself, amount to an automatic ban on Anna Vissi performing his songs. Instead, it changes who controls the licensing process for live performances. What about Anna Vissi? The development is particularly significant because Vissi has performed some of Karvelas’ biggest compositions throughout a hugely successful career. The two artists have been closely linked professionally and personally for decades, with Karvelas writing many of the songs that helped define Vissi’s career. But their relationship has now entered a very different phase. In an earlier statement, Karvelas accused Vissi of effectively removing herself from the possibility of future professional collaboration. He wrote that she had “consciously, and perhaps deliberately” placed herself outside the framework of any future collaboration between them. He also ended that statement with a pointed warning about the future of her musical repertoire. The latest legal move gives that dispute a practical dimension, placing control over live performances of his catalogue directly in Karvelas’ hands. Karvelas retains other rights with Self-Management The announcement also makes clear that Karvelas has not completely withdrawn from Self-Management. He remains a member of the organisation for the management of other economic rights relating to his copyrighted works. These include areas such as radio and television broadcasting and public performance of mechanically reproduced recordings in commercial establishments. The change specifically concerns live public performances of his music. That distinction is important because it means the latest move is not a blanket withdrawal of his entire catalogue from collective management. Instead, Karvelas has chosen to personally exercise control over one particularly important category of rights. A major turning point in the Vissi-Karvelas dispute The decision marks a significant escalation in the highly publicised dispute between two figures whose creative partnership has played a major role in Greek popular music. For years, Karvelas’ compositions and Vissi’s performances were closely intertwined. Now, the composer has taken direct control of the mechanism governing live performances of his songs. Whether the decision will affect Vissi’s future concerts or other live appearances remains to be seen. What is clear is that any future request involving the live performance of Karvelas’ works will now be subject to a new licensing arrangement, with the composer himself holding the decision-making authority. The post Nikos Karvelas Takes Back Control: He Will Decide Who Can Sing His Songs Live appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Trump Says Anyone Who Does Not Call AI ‘Super Intelligence’ Is ‘The Enemy’
body: US President Donald Trump, who has said he wants the term “super intelligence” to replace artificial intelligence, said Thursday that anyone who does not heed his wishes will be treated as “THE ENEMY,” without saying what the consequences would be. “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social network. Trump mentioned his proposed name change in a speech before the UN General Assembly last month, saying his new term “sounds much better.” Then in late September, Trump signed an executive order, imposing the use of “super intelligence” across the US government. That same obligation does not affect the private sector, but some there are already adopting it, including Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta group. Trump ally Elon Musk is using “super intelligence” in his posts on his X network. The semantic debate is primarily a political one: the US president, who has stridently defended the use of AI, is trying to put a positive spin on it in the face of mounting worries about AI security, and anger over the proliferation of data centers in the US. More generally, Trump is a fan of renaming things or creating nicknames: he now calls the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America” and converted Lake Ontario into “Lake America.” The post Trump Says Anyone Who Does Not Call AI ‘Super Intelligence’ Is ‘The Enemy’ appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Parliament, Government set key bills needed for Ukraine’s funding
body:
Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada Ruslan Stefanchuk and Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said this in a joint Facebook post, Ukrinform reports.
“The Parliament and the Government share a common task – to ensure the timely adoption of decisions needed to fulfill Ukraine’s international commitments and secure financial support from partners. Ahead of an important plenary week, we held a joint working meeting with members of the Government and Parliament. We agreed on legislative priorities and further steps toward adopting key bills,” the statement said.
The priorities primarily concern European integration initiatives and decisions under the Ukraine Facility, the IMF program and other agreements with international partners.
The adoption of the relevant bills is crucial not only for Ukraine to fulfill its commitments but also for the timely receipt of international funding.
Stefanchuk and Koretskyi noted that amid the difficult situation with public finances, adopting legislative initiatives is one of the shared priorities of the Government and Parliament.
The officials assured that the Verkhovna Rada and the Cabinet of Ministers are coordinating their work at all levels. They are working with relevant parliamentary committees, parliamentary factions and groups to ensure that the bills receive proper consideration and that the necessary explanations are provided for each of them.
“On October 12, plenary sessions of the Verkhovna Rada will begin, with priority given to considering bills needed to fulfill Ukraine’s international commitments. At the same time, the Government is accelerating implementation of its part of the commitments. By October 15, all necessary decisions at the government level must be adopted,” they said.
Koretskyi and Stefanchuk emphasized that they share a common understanding of their responsibility and the importance of every decision.
“A challenging plenary week lies ahead, but our task remains unchanged: to deliver results that will determine the country’s financial resilience, the European integration process and the trust of our international partners,” the officials concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Verkhovna Rada plans to begin its work on October 12 and consider a number of important bills, including those related to European integration and unblocking the EU accession negotiation clusters.

title: Oldest active U.S. carrier USS Nimitz completes flight deck certification after Norfolk return
body: Known as PALS, the Precision Approach Landing Systems help pilots land at night or in bad weather. They do so by guiding pilots to a good starting position for the approach. A ship needs the certification before it can conduct flight operations. On Nimitz, the systems are supported by the combat systems department and the Carrier Air Traffic Controller Center, or CATCC. The certification was not the only work done at sea. Sailors also used the underway period to prepare for future operations, running aircraft recovery, damage control, propulsion and other drills. With the certification and training behind it, Nimitz is ready for future underway periods, the Navy said. Those include time at sea in support of East Coast carrier qualifications, or CQs. CQs are an important milestone in the training of student naval aviators. They give students their first opportunity to land on the flight deck of an operational aircraft carrier. Nimitz is scheduled to conduct multiple CQs in support of Commander, Naval Air Force Atlantic. The carrier is homeported at Naval Station Norfolk as part of Carrier Strike Group 8. Nimitz is the oldest American aircraft carrier in active service and the lead ship of its class. The Navy describes the supercarrier as one of the largest warships in the world. The ship was laid down, launched and commissioned as CVAN 68. It was re-designated CVN 68, a nuclear-powered multi-mission aircraft carrier, on June 30, 1975, as part of a fleet realignment. The move in July returned Nimitz to a base it left in 1987. That year the carrier was relocated from Naval Station Norfolk to Naval Station Bremerton in Washington state, now part of Naval Base Kitsap. Following its Refueling and Complex Overhaul in 2001, the ship’s homeport was changed to Naval Air Station North Island in San Diego. It moved again in 2012 to Naval Station Everett in Washington state, and in January 2015 from Everett back to Naval Base Kitsap.

title: Russian president Vladimir Putin holds bilateral meeting with Turkmen counterpart
body:
TURKMENBASHI, Turkmenistan, October 8. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin, who arrived in Turkmenistan on a working visit, held a bilateral meeting with President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
"Following the official dinner, Putin held a bilateral meeting with President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov. The heads of state discussed key current issues concerning the dynamically developing bilateral Russian-Turkmen relations," Peskov said.
The two leaders met at the Avaza complex.
Avaza is a national tourist zone on Turkmenistan’s Caspian coast, located near the city of Turkmenbashi.
Putin and Berdimuhamedov are in regular contact. Their latest phone conversation took place just recently, when the Turkmen president personally congratulated the Russian leader on his birthday the previous day.
Despite their frequent phone contacts, Putin and Berdimuhamedov invariably take the opportunity to compare notes during in-person meetings as well.
The Russian president last visited Turkmenistan less than a year ago. Putin then took part in the major international forum "Peace and Trust: Unity of Goals for a Sustainable Future," held to mark the 30th anniversary of the republic’s permanent neutrality.

title: 19-Year-Old Daughter of Detained Doctors at Centre of Plasma Exchange Investigation
body: New questions have emerged over a plasma exchange procedure reportedly undergone by the 19-year-old daughter of the two doctors detained in connection with the investigation surrounding the death of Giorgos Mazonakis. According to a report by Live News , the young woman is understood to have undergone the same medical procedure that investigators are examining as part of the wider case. Her account could prove significant as authorities work to establish how plasma exchange procedures were being carried out at the doctors’ clinic and why the 19-year-old underwent the treatment. The teenager had been studying medicine in Germany and was also a highly accomplished karate athlete, reportedly reaching ninth place in the world rankings. A family friend told Live News that the young woman has now left her studies and returned to Greece amid the turmoil surrounding the case. She is reportedly considering returning to training, primarily as a way of coping with the intense psychological pressure rather than with an immediate goal of competing. From medical studies in Germany to elite karate People connected to the young woman’s sports club described her as a talented athlete who had achieved significant success in karate. Her parents were known at the club as doctors and were said to have followed her competitions and taken an interest in her progress. However, another relative would usually take her to training sessions. Those around the club reportedly knew that her father worked as a physician and was involved in nutrition programmes and supplements. They were also aware that the family clinic had expensive equipment used for various measurements and tests and that it attracted high-profile clients. They told Live News they were not aware that plasma exchange procedures were being carried out there. The teenager had reportedly been reluctant to move alone to Germany for her medical studies, with several of her friends instead choosing Cyprus. According to her friend, she had even considered abandoning her studies to focus more heavily on karate. She stopped competing after the Panhellenic examinations and is now back in Greece, where she is reportedly supporting her younger brother. Questions over weight, training and plasma exchange One of the most sensitive aspects of the investigation concerns the young woman’s efforts to maintain the weight required for her competitive karate category. According to a close friend, she wanted to compete at 53 kilograms, despite her usual weight reportedly being between 60 and 65 kilograms. The friend claims that the teenager sometimes followed extremely restrictive diets to reach the target weight, at times eating very little and at other times seeking assistance from a dietitian. In October 2024, she reportedly reached her target weight but was left feeling exhausted. People connected to her sports club have offered a different account, saying she did not have an ongoing eating problem and had followed a programme after gaining weight during the period of her Panhellenic examinations. The young woman also reportedly worked at the family clinic during the summer before leaving for Germany while continuing demanding training sessions. Her mother has also spoken about the family’s circumstances in a statement included in the case file. She reportedly said her daughter, who was studying medicine, worked for about a month in the clinic’s reception area during the summer of 2025. The doctor described an extremely demanding professional schedule, saying her children would sometimes complain that she did not answer their calls. According to her testimony, on one occasion she finished work at around 2am after dealing primarily with patients from abroad. She said her daughter subsequently gained a better understanding of the demands of her profession. Why did the 19-year-old undergo plasma exchange? That is now one of the key questions facing investigators. Authorities are expected to examine why the procedure was performed on the teenager, who authorised it and whether it had any connection with her efforts to reach a particular competition weight. The young woman is also expected to provide authorities with video footage of the procedure, according to Live News . The footage reportedly shows her while under sedation. Her testimony could therefore become an important part of the investigation into the operation of the clinic and the procedures allegedly performed there. Her relationship with her parents According to her close friend, the 19-year-old had a particularly strong relationship with her father and would confide in him about her studies, karate and personal life. The friend therefore believes it would be unlikely that the plasma exchange could have taken place without his knowledge. However, that remains an allegation and personal assessment from someone close to the young woman, rather than an established finding by investigators. Her relationship with her mother was reportedly more complicated, according to the same friend. The teenager’s forthcoming testimony is expected to help investigators establish what she knew, who decided that she should undergo the procedure and what role, if any, her parents played. The investigation remains ongoing and the allegations have not been established by a court. The post 19-Year-Old Daughter of Detained Doctors at Centre of Plasma Exchange Investigation appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Military Plane Crash: Air Chief sets up probe panel, assures adequate support for bereaved families
body:
The Chief of Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, an air marshal, says he has directed the constitution of a panel to investigate the recent crash of a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft at Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area, Ondo State.
Mr Aneke disclosed this on Thursday when he visited the crash site.
The aircraft crashed on Monday while on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos.
The NAF authorities said 25 persons were on board the aircraft.
However, three days after the crash, all hope of any survivor has been lost.
Apart from the deployment of heavy machinery, which cleared the bushes around and dug deep into the swamp, the main body of the plane is still trapped beneath the mud.
The air chief, who was accompanied by some senior officers of the force, described the incident as a great loss.
“I had informed my Superintendent of Safety and Evaluation to come up with a high-level delegation comprising both military and civilian safety experts, NTSB, Accident and Emergency Management Board, retired senior officers, experienced air force officers, to sit down and get to the bottom of what happened,” he said.
“This is not the time to start speculating, and I plead with you, and the general public, we’ve lost people who are fighting for the nation. The best we can do for them is to be a little bit patient and let those who are the specialists get to the bottom of what has happened.”
Mr Aneke, who did not give further details of the probe, sympathised with the families of those who have lost their loved ones in the tragic incident.
“I basically knew everyone on that flight. I’ve flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. Highly trained, professional, and intelligent officers,” he said.
“I want to assure the families of our loved ones that the Nigerian Armed Forces will keep you on guard in ensuring that you are safe.
“The Nigerian Air Force is putting everything possible to ensure that the families get the necessary support they need.”
The air chief commended the people and government of Ondo State for committing resources, time and energy in the recovery efforts.
“The locals here, the residents here, were the first responders. I’ve been briefed by the commander of the Naval base here. Words cannot describe how we Nigerians come together when things go sour,” he added.
The Ondo State Government had deployed two swamp buggies to aid access to the crash site and also assist in digging out the plane.
The state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, however, expressed concerns over the inability of the rescue teams to locate the main body of the plane after putting so much effort in over the last three days.
Only torn clothes, body parts, and pieces of the plane’s panels had been brought to shore.

USA Today Co., along with the several local newspapers it owns, is suing OpenAI over claims that the company copied “hundreds of thousands” of articles to train its AI models, as reported earlier by Reuters . In a filing on Thursday , the publisher asks for damages of more than $250 million, alleging OpenAI’s unauthorized use of its content “has done real and continuing” harm to its outlets.
This is just the latest in a string of copyright lawsuits filed against OpenAI. In addition to a copyright lawsuit filed by The New York Times , OpenAI is also facing legal action from The Intercept , CNET owner Ziff Davis , CBC/Radio-Canada , Encyclopaedia Britannica , Merriam-Webster, The Seattle Times , and a coalition of nearly 400 local newspapers .
“OpenAI’s commercial success rests on large-scale copyright infringement,” USA Today Co.’s lawsuit claims. It alleges that OpenAI never asked for permission to use its content, instead “took” USA Today ’s content to “build products worth hundreds of billions of dollars.” The Tennessean , Indy Star , The Columbus Dispatch , The Oklahoman , and several other local outlets are also included in the lawsuit.
OpenAI didn’t immediately respond to The Verge ’s request for comment.

title: Ukraine strikes a data center operated by Russian tech giant Yandex. How vulnerable is Russia’s internet to further drone attacks?
body: What happened? Overnight on October 8, Ukrainian forces struck Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, with drones, causing a fire. No one was injured, but the data center temporarily shut down completely. This disrupted some of Yandex’s own services, as well as those of companies that used the tech giant’s infrastructure in Sasovo. In the morning, users complained of problems accessing Yandex Disk and Yandex Documents. Disruptions then spread to Yandex Mail, the Yandex-owned Cian, Avito, IVI, MegaFon, Russian Railways, T-Bank, and several property developers and media outlets. The cascading disruptions across the Russian internet throughout the day may have been linked to an attempt to redistribute server capacity after the fire in Sasovo. The data center occupies part of the former Sasta machine tool factory and houses two of Yandex’s three supercomputers , Lyapunov and Chervonenkis, which are used to train neural networks. Whether these systems were damaged is not yet known. The overall extent of the damage is also unclear. Yandex shares have already fallen by more than 3% following the attack, according to Moscow Exchange data . So it got hit. They’ll fix it, right? We don’t know. Much depends on how badly the fire damaged the equipment. Even if restoring the data center is technically possible, it might simply not make sense, partly because of the threat of further attacks. After a series of successful Ukrainian strikes on large Wildberries warehouses, for example, the online retailer’s management decided to spread its inventory across smaller facilities. Yandex may take the same approach. Some of the data stored at the Ryazan data center, however, may be recoverable. If Yandex customers uploaded their data to the cloud, those files were stored simultaneously at different company data centers — more precisely, in four “availability zones.” Yandex said in 2019: All of this data is replicated: When an object is edited, created, or deleted, every copy is updated. Things are a little more complicated for other companies’ virtual machines hosted there. Customers are responsible for backing up that data themselves. They could have used the separate paid service Yandex Cloud Backup, which would also have stored their data at several data centers. Or they could have chosen another solution — or made no backups at all. Related reading Russia keeps attacking Ukrainian data centers, calling it a ‘mandatory digital detox’ Why do services stop working when data centers are hit? Because these facilities store user data and house the servers that companies and organizations rent to run their websites or internal infrastructure. Data centers can withstand a temporary power outage thanks to their own diesel generators, the loss of an individual communications link thanks to connections to multiple telecom providers, and even a small fire thanks to automatic fire suppression systems. But, like online retailers’ warehouses, they have proved defenseless against drone strikes. Unless, of course, they are housed in former Cold War shelters — Europe has several such data centers. Should we expect more attacks like these — as with oil refineries, Wildberries, and Ozon? Nothing can be predicted with certainty during a war. But the context matters. The strike on Yandex’s data center looks like a logical Ukrainian response to systematic Russian military attacks on Ukrainian digital hubs, including Cosmonova and Datagroup facilities. Since late September, Russian forces have damaged or destroyed the data centers of at least eight companies . Russia’s Defense Ministry officially called these strikes a “forced digital detox.” Today, a few hours after the attack on Yandex’s data center, Andriy Kovalenko, the former head of the Center for Countering Disinformation at Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council, wrote : Two can play that game. Which other data centers in Russia could be targeted? And could strikes on them bring down the entire Russian internet? Any technology hub could be at risk, but a nationwide digital blackout is unlikely. Sarkis Darbinyan , a lawyer specializing in digital rights and an expert with RKS.global, told Meduza that a single strike on a regional data center cannot take down a major service entirely. Modern IT companies have infrastructure spread across the country, so when equipment fails, user traffic is automatically rerouted to backup systems. Russia’s main data centers are concentrated in Moscow and the surrounding region and are very well protected. Disabling them all would be an extremely ambitious undertaking, Darbinyan said. Russia has close to 200 data centers in total. Darbinyan believes further targeted attacks on regional facilities belonging to Rostelecom, Sber, VK, or Selectel are possible in theory: They could cause local disruptions, but would affect local residents more than the country as a whole: Regional government systems, online school gradebooks, medical customer relationship management systems, and internet-connected cash registers would temporarily stop working. These services could be down for anywhere from a few hours to a day while administrators reconfigure the systems. Another potential target for Ukrainian forces is MSK-IX, Russia’s largest internet exchange point. It has become a “symbol of the centralization of the Russian internet,” Darbinyan said. If MSK-IX is hit, he told Meduza, internet access across the country could slow dramatically, alternative communications links could become overloaded, and the websites of small companies and local providers could temporarily become inaccessible. Even then, however, the internet would not shut down entirely, Darbinyan said: This is a fundamental feature of the network, built into it back in the days of ARPANET so that it could withstand even a nuclear strike. So attacks like these only impair services temporarily, for a few hours — they certainly don’t cause a complete digital collapse. Related reading Ukraine strikes Yandex data center housing two of the company’s supercomputers Are these strikes legal? And why attack internet infrastructure at all? After all, it’s civilians, not the military, who suffer the most… Indeed, if we accept that this is primarily civilian infrastructure, neither army’s strikes on data centers appear justified. The Geneva Conventions explicitly state that a facility is a military objective if it makes an “effective contribution to military action” and its neutralization “offers a definite military advantage” to the attacking side. In cases of doubt, it is presumed to be civilian — meaning this infrastructure cannot be attacked without clear evidence. Unfortunately, when it comes to data centers, Russian forces — and, following their lead, Ukrainian forces — are clearly ignoring the question of legality. For example, Russia’s Defense Ministry justified its strikes on Ukrainian data centers by saying that the grounds of one facility “were used by units of Ukraine’s Defense Ministry and other security agencies to store dual-use goods.” Another data center allegedly handled “the processing and transmission of intelligence for the Ukrainian armed forces.” The ministry provided no evidence for these claims. As for the military rationale, at least some data centers meet the criteria for targets in long-range strike campaigns. Meduza’s Explainers desk previously set out these criteria : The facilities are poorly protected and can be destroyed with just a few drones carrying small warheads Their coordinates are well known They contain large quantities of valuable goods Systematically destroying these businesses can damage the enemy’s economy Disrupting internet infrastructure can also make civilians feel just how much the war is costing their country and, in theory, fuel public discontent with the government’s actions. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. title: Colby approves Pentagon policy for ‘cyber operations-peculiar’ monetary awards
body: Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby approved a departmentwide instruction that went into effect this week and details how the Pentagon will award action-based financial bonuses to innovative cyber warriors. The directive , approved on Sept. 30 and effective Oct. 5, establishes policy, assigns responsibilities, and provides procedures for the “Cyber Operations-Peculiar Awards” program authorized by Section 1124a of Title 10 U.S.C. The COPA initiative allows for the issuance of cash bonuses up to $2,500 to eligible troops to “recognize exceptional contributions rooted in novel actions, inventions, or technical achievements that significantly enhance DoW cyberspace operations capabilities,” the instruction noted, using an acronym to refer to the Department of War, the Trump administration’s preferred name for the Department of Defense. “The basis for an award must be a specific, observable outcome, not sustained performance, which other awards already recognize.” Per the guidance, award nominations can be made for innovative efforts that boost “offensive cyberspace operations against adversary systems or networks” in support of combatant commander objectives or national security goals; defend “friendly cyberspace” from malicious activity; harden, extend, or improve the security and resilience of the department’s information network; or find and “neutralize” a previously unknown “advanced persistent threat” via a clever “threat hunting” technique or procedure. Notably, the pool of potential awardees is not restricted to personnel assigned to U.S. Cyber Command. It includes “covered” service members who are part of the military’s “cyberspace operations forces” and whose achievements meet the criteria laid out in the policy edict. Troops must have been on “active duty, in active status, in active service, in active Guard and Reserve Duty, or on full-time National Guard duty” when their exceptional action, invention, or technical achievement occurred. According to the instruction, a service member’s military grade or rank won’t affect their program eligibility or the dollar value of the award that they may receive. The COPA program is “separate from (and in addition to) other military decorations, ribbons, or civilian awards for which the Service member may be eligible,” the guidance noted. The assistant secretary of defense for cyber policy, a role currently held by Katie Sutton, will oversee the COPA initiative. DOD component heads are tasked with developing component-specific procedures for award nomination and processing. The civilian leaders of the military departments are authorized to designate “appropriate approval authorities” within their respective departments. “Awards may be paid from funds or appropriations available to the activity primarily benefiting from the novel action, invention, or technical achievement, or from several funds of various benefiting activities as determined by the paying authority,” per the directive. The COPA policy aims to avoid double dipping. “Consistent with Volume 451 of DoDI 1400.25, awards under this section are not authorized if a monetary award under that volume has already been paid for the same contribution, and approving officials must ensure that the same invention is not paid twice under both authorities,” the instruction noted, adding that only one award is authorized for a qualifying achievement, regardless of the number of individuals who contributed. The bonuses will also be subject to applicable IRS tax rules. The post Colby approves Pentagon policy for ‘cyber operations-peculiar’ monetary awards appeared first on DefenseScoop .

1Password previously found itself in hot water for contributing to Omarchy, as has Cloudflare.
