title: Tinubu’s 30-Day Fuel Discount A Panic-Driven Publicity Stunt — Atiku
body: Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day fuel discount, describing it as a desperate and temporary gesture that cannot address the hardship caused by high fuel prices. In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku accused the President Bola Tinubu administration of attempting to use a temporary fuel discount as a political response to the worsening cost-of-living crisis. The former Vice President’s reaction followed the Federal Government’s announcement on Thursday that it would offer a discount on petrol dispensed by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) for an initial 30 days. The measure is part of a fresh package of interventions announced by the government to cushion the impact of high fuel prices on Nigerians and stabilise pump prices. Announcing the measure at a press briefing in Abuja, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the discount was not a subsidy but an arrangement by the government to sell the petrol at cost. But Atiku said the government had watched Nigerians endure severe hardship without providing meaningful relief, accusing the administration of offering temporary relief as the 2027 elections approach. “Atiku totally rejects this calendar-scheduled, election-laced subsidy package. Nigerians are not fools to be offered a month of discounted fuel after years of punishing prices and then expected to forget the hardship when the discount expires. This is shameless and heartless,” he said. He described the 30-day discount as “not an economic plan but a political bandage on a wound the government had helped create.” “What happens on Day 31? Nigerians wake up to the same brutal prices, the same punishing transport fares and the same rising cost of food. The government cannot manufacture relief for one month and expect Nigerians to applaud while the hardship remains,” he said. Atiku also questioned the scope of the intervention, noting that it is limited to NNPC stations. He said the government had yet to state how much motorists would save per litre or guarantee that savings for transport operators would be passed on to passengers through lower fares. The ADC presidential candidate further described the government’s move as a reversal of its previous position on relief measures, saying it amounted to an admission of the severity of the hardship Nigerians had endured. “This volte-face proves that the production-support proposal I have advanced is workable, achievable and not complicated. The Tinubu government and its spin doctors have tried to make it sound impossible, yet they are now reaching for a temporary subsidy-style intervention because the pain has become impossible to ignore,” Atiku said. He reiterated his proposal for capped and budgeted production support tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, with safeguards to ensure that the benefit reaches consumers while supporting local refining. “Nigerians need lasting relief, not a countdown to the return of hardship. Tinubu’s government cannot spend years telling Nigerians to endure, then offer 30 days of relief and call it a solution,” he said. Atiku restated his commitment to making life more affordable for Nigerians. The post Tinubu’s 30-Day Fuel Discount A Panic-Driven Publicity Stunt — Atiku appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russia attacks key energy facility for Kyiv – Shmyhal
body:
Russia has attacked a facility critical to Kyiv's energy supply, said Denys Shmyhal, First Deputy Prime Minister for Energy.

"An attack took place on an energy facility vital to the city of Kyiv. Energy workers are doing everything possible to quickly restore power," Shmyhal wrote on Telegram on Thursday evening.

He emphasized that the Russian drone attack was ongoing and that all emergency services had been deployed.

As previously reported, just minutes before Shmyhal's statement, the Ministry of Energy announced that hostile shelling had caused the disconnection of several elements of the electrical grid supplying Kyiv. This resulted in power outages for a significant number of consumers in certain districts of the capital.

Earlier, DTEK announced emergency power outages in Kyiv and the surrounding region.

On Thursday evening, metro operations were briefly suspended, and the movement of electric public transport in Kyiv was restricted.

title: Rising food prices and poor rains fuel fears of hunger crisis in Darfur
body: Rising food prices, declining rainfall and mounting economic pressures are deepening hardship across Sudan’s Darfur region, fuelling fears of worsening food shortages as displacement and the destruction of agricultural livelihoods compound the humanitarian crisis. In West Darfur, particularly the state capital El Geneina, soaring food prices , expensive imports and currency fluctuations have placed further pressure on households. Journalist Mohiuddin Zakaria told Radio Dabanga that the price of a sack of millet had doubled from about SDG300,000 to SDG600,000. Prices of sorghum , cooking oil and other essential commodities have also risen sharply. Zakaria attributed the increases partly to poor rainfall and what he described as attempts by some traders to monopolise essential goods, warning that declining agricultural production could push the state towards a severe food crisis and possibly famine. West Darfur relies heavily on food supplies imported through neighbouring Chad . Zakaria said the price of 1,000 Chadian francs had risen from about SDG35,000 a month ago to around SDG46,000, making imported goods more expensive. High transaction costs through the Bank of Khartoum’s Bankak application have added to the burden. Zakaria said the discount rate in the state had reached approximately 46 per cent, while one resident reported an exchange rate of SDG70,000 through the application. Zakaria said disruptions in the currency market , growing reliance on the parallel market to determine the exchange rate between the Sudanese pound and the Chadian franc, and fluctuations in the dollar’s value had all contributed to rising commodity prices and increased economic pressure on residents. In North Darfur, however, the agricultural outlook appears more promising in some areas. Sheikh Mohammed Bakr Suleiman, an administrator in the El Hamra area south of Kutum, described this year’s agricultural season as promising. Speaking to Radio Dabanga, Suleiman praised the authorities for providing farmers with agricultural machinery and equipment, which he said had improved productivity. However, he said the area had also received large numbers of people displaced by fighting in El Fasher. Many own agricultural land but need access to essential services. Saleh Mahmoud, head of the Darfur Bar Association, warned that insufficient rainfall threatened the agricultural season and could further deepen Sudan’s humanitarian crisis . He called on the international community to impose a 90-day truce and compel both sides in the war to halt hostilities, allowing humanitarian organisations to deliver aid to displacement camps and other affected areas. Mahmoud said the Darfur Bar Association had issued a statement warning that the situation was more critical than before, with the lives of millions of Sudanese people at risk. He said the war had destroyed villages, homes, crops and farms across Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile, as well as the gum arabic belt, undermining food production and livelihoods. The destruction has left millions dependent on urgent humanitarian assistance, he added, warning that some areas had officially entered famine. On behalf of the Darfur Bar Association, Mahmoud urged Sudanese people and the international community to press both sides to end the war immediately. Share article The post Rising food prices and poor rains fuel fears of hunger crisis in Darfur appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

title: Ukraine war latest: Russian glide bomb strikes in Kramatorsk kill at least 33
body:
A Russian glide bomb strike on two minibuses in Kramatorsk killed 33 people on the morning of Oct. 8, Ukraine's emergency service (DSNS) said.
Twenty-two more people were injured in the Russian attack, Donetsk regional governor Vadym Filashkin said . Fire broke out in at least two busses following the Russian strikes, according to DSNS .
"Russia comes to the Ukrainian land with death. She hits our cities, kills our people and multiplies her crimes every day," Filashkin said .
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that doctors were still fighting for the lives of some of the injured people and warned that the number of dead may still increase. Two dead people could not yet be identified due to the severity of their injuries, he added.
"This strike will not go without our response. Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and the world needs to react to this," Zelensky said.
The Kramatorsk and Sloviansk military administrations ordered the stop of all public transport.
"The Russians are targeting civilians. For them, a bus with passengers is an attractive target precisely because one hit can kill as many people as possible," Filashkin said.
Across Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast, four more people had been killed and six injured by Russian attacks as of the morning of Oct. 8, prior to the Kramatorsk strike, according to the governor .
In total, Russian forces shelled settlements in the Donetsk region 31 times over the last day, and 256 people, including 32 children, were evacuated from the front line, according to the Donetsk governor.
Russian drone strikes on Oct. 8 have killed four people and injured at least 19 in Kyiv, the city's authorities said.
A Russian drone struck a four-story commercial building in Solomyanskyi district, killing two and injuring two, and leading to a fire, while the wreckage of another fell on the Holosiivskyi district, Klitschko said .
Prior to that strike, Klitschko said that Russian attacks on the capital this morning had killed one person and injured 11 others.
A fourth person died of their injuries in hospital, the Kyiv city military administration (KMDA) said in the afternoon.
Klitschko raised the number of injured to 19, 13 of which were hospitalized, in an update on 07:21 p.m. local time.
At 10:00 a.m. local time, Ukraine’s biggest private energy firm DTEK announced emergency energy shutdowns in Brovary, Buchanskyi, Vyshgorod, and Boryspil districts of the oblast.
Shortly after, KMDA announced that the right bank of Kyiv may experience interruptions in water supply, as the power decrease in the electricity grid also meant a decrease in pressure of the water supply network. This applied especially to the Holosiivskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Solomyanskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts.
The drop in voltage from external power supply centers also temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the KMDA said .
DSNS also said that a fire broke out at a logistics facility in the Buchanskyi district in Kyiv Oblast following a Russian drone strike.
In Sviatopetrivske in Buchanskyi district, a school-kindergarten and a nearby playground in a residential complex were damaged in the attack, Kyiv Oblast Governor Tymur Tkachenko said . In another settlement in the district, a woman was injured and hospitalized, he added.
Overnight, Russian drone strikes on Kyiv had already killed four people and injured 21 across four districts, KMDA said .
Polish military prosecutors found Polish SIM cards in some of the Russian drones downed during a Russian mass drone incursion into the country on the night of Sept. 9 to Sept. 10, 2025, RMF24 reported on Oct. 8.
Polish authorities didn't disclose whether three Polish SIM cards had been stolen or obtained illegaly, according to RMF24 . The investigation was discontinued after it did not lead to the identification of the specific people responsible for the Russian incursion.
"The investigation was discontinued because the perpetrator of the crime of violating Polish airspace and thus posing a threat to public safety was not identified," Marcin Kozak, spokesman of the District Prosecutor’s Office in Lublin, said.
On Sept. 9, 2025, more than 30 Gerbera-type drones breached Polish airspace, some of which were shot down by the Polish military, RMF24 reported .
Ending Russia's war against Ukraine through negotiations is currently unattainable , U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Greek media outlet Kathimerini on Oct. 8, casting further doubt on President Donald Trump's latest push to broker peace.
The comments confirm earlier Kyiv Independent reporting that Washington's latest effort to advance negotiations faces growing uncertainty.
At this point, there appears to be no prospect of a negotiated settlement, Rubio said . He added that the goal remains out of reach because Russia insists on gaining full control over Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast without fighting, a demand Kyiv has rejected.
The latest rounds of peace negotiations have also stalled over Moscow's territorial demands.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected a ceasefire and demanded that Kyiv surrender the partially occupied Donbas, a strategically important region in eastern Ukraine . Moscow is effectively seeking territory that Russian forces have failed to capture militarily.
Ukraine has instead called for a ceasefire along the current front line.
The diplomatic effort now faces another obstacle: Moscow has given little indication that it intends to take part in further talks. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said on Oct. 7 that there were currently no plans for U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine.
"There are currently no plans to hold talks in this format," Ryabkov told reporters.
The latest effort began in early September, when Trump's envoys traveled to Kyiv and Moscow seeking progress before the U.S. midterm elections. The trips produced one tangible outcome: an agreement in principle to hold a trilateral meeting between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.
A month later, however, even the trilateral meeting remains uncertain.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Oct. 8 that Ukrainian negotiators will meet with Trump's envoys in the U.S. later this week to discuss the prospects for peace talks with Russia.
Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its forces struck Russia's Omsk oil refinery in Russia's Omsk Oblast on Oct. 8.
"The destruction of such facilities is the exercise by Ukraine of its inalienable right to self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter and is aimed at reducing the military-economic potential of the Russian Federation," the General Staff said .
Ukrainian drone manufacturer Fire Point had previously reported an attack on the refinery, saying that the refinery was hit with its own long-range FP-1 attack drones.
Videos and images from local residents, shared by Ukrainian monitoring channels , show explosions, fire, and smoke rising from the area surrounding the oil refinery.
Omsk Oblast Governor Vitaly Khotsenko confirmed that there was a drone attack on the region. Ukrainian authorities have not yet confirm a strike on the refinery.
Omsk is located in southwestern Siberia, north of the Kazakh border. The city of more than 1 million people is some 2,500 kilometers (about 1,550 miles) east of Ukraine controlled territory.
The Omsk oil refinery is owned by Russia's state-owned energy giant Gazprom. It's the country's largest refinery by refining capacity, processing more than 21 million metric tons of crude oil per year.
The plant produces a wide range of fuels, lubricants, and petrochemical products and is involved in supplying the Russian military, Ukraine's General Staff said after Ukraine struck the refinery on July 6. According to the military , the facility has a refining depth of about 99%, one of the highest rates in Russia.
Earlier, an overnight Ukrainian strike on the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan region caused a large blaze at the plant, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on Oct. 8.
The U.K. published 38 new sanctions listings on Oct. 8, targeting ships helping Russia evade existing sanctions and a range of companies in Moscow's military-industrial complex, energy, and cryptocurrency sectors.
"The message is simple: if you help Russia fund or equip this war, you will face the consequences," reads a U.K. government press release.
Among the businesses in the new sanctions listings are three cryptocurrency exchanges and two payment platforms.
Xeltox Enterprises, one of those listed entities has "been involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the government of Russia by carrying on business in a sector of strategic significance (...) the financial services sector," reads the U.K. government's sanctions listing .
Russia has increasingly sought to use cryptocurrency , which is hard to track, to circumvent global sanctions, and the new U.K. sanctions target the "A7" network, which is at the heart of Moscow's attempts to evade financial sanctions.
That has prompted the U.K., the U.S ., the EU , and Ukraine to target crypto schemes in recent sanctions packages.
Also featuring on the listings are two further oil companies: Zarubezhneft and INK Capital.
"The U.K. was the first country in the G7 to sanction the top four Russian oil companies," reads the press statement.
The U.K. has also added 12 ships to its list of sanctioned vessels accused of being part of Russia's shadow fleet — dilapidated vessels suspected of helping Moscow evade price caps and bans on its trade in oil and gas.
That takes the number of ships sanctioned by the U.K. to 645 and the total number of Russia sanctions to 3,537.

title: Returned Benin artefacts to go on public display
body: …Cultural troupes from South-South, South-East to perform By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — Returned Benin artefacts taken away during the 1897 British expedition will be displayed for public viewing as part of activities marking the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II. Chairman of the anniversary organising committee and former Edo State Deputy Governor, Lucky Imasuen, disclosed this while addressing a press conference on the month-long celebrations in Benin City. Imasuen said the exhibition would be organised by the National Commission for Museums and Monuments (NCMM) and would provide members of the public an opportunity to see some of the artefacts that have been returned to Nigeria. He said the return of the artefacts was part of efforts associated with the Oba’s advocacy and that of previous monarchs for the restitution of Benin cultural heritage taken abroad. According to him, the Federal Government had directed that returned artefacts be taken to their original locations for display. “Those artefacts that were stolen by the British invaders in 1897, carted away to England and sold to various countries in the world to both public and private collections, are gradually making their way back home. “With the leadership of this great Oba, an effort started by his grandfather, passed over to his father and now to him, these artefacts are gradually making their way back home. “In recognition of his effort, the former president and the Federal Government gazetted that these artefacts, upon return to Nigeria, should be taken to the original location where they were stolen from. They will be displayed for the public,” Imasuen said. Cultural troupes to perform The former deputy governor said cultural troupes from Edo and other parts of the South-South and South-East geopolitical zones would feature prominently in the celebrations. He said cultural groups from the 18 local government areas of Edo State, as well as groups from Delta, Ondo and Anambra states, would participate in the activities. He added that representatives of Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa communities resident in Edo would also showcase their cultural heritage. “You know the Oba of Benin is not just the Oba for the Benin, he is the Oba for the entire people,” Imasuen said. He also announced the Calabar Carnival as part of the programme, saying the procession would begin at the Boys Scout Ground near the Ogba Zoo and proceed through Airport Road to the Oba Akenzua Cultural Centre. Concert to feature Edo musicians Imasuen said the anniversary celebrations would also feature a musical concert involving musicians of Edo origin. He listed some of the artistes expected to perform as Influence Akaba, Fabomo and Young Bolivia, with Shallipopi expected to headline the concert. “We have our indigenous musicians who will be participating in this festival. We have Influence Akaba, Fabomo, Young Bolivia among others, and to crown it all, we have our son in whom we are well pleased, Shallipopi,” he said. The post Returned Benin artefacts to go on public display appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Despite Seoul recalling ambassador, Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue – MFA
body:
Despite South Korea's decision to recall its ambassador, Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue – even if it takes time, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhiy Tykhy said.
"This week, we invited the Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Ukraine to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to present our position and seek constructive solutions. The Ukrainian side's position was conveyed to him. We are convinced that diplomacy must prevail over emotions. Despite Seoul's decision to recall its ambassador, Ukraine remains open to resuming constructive dialogue-even if it takes time," the spokesperson said in response to journalists' questions regarding the ambassador's recall.
Earlier on Thursday, the South Korean government announced its decision to recall its ambassador to Kyiv due to disagreements over the situation with prisoners of war from North Korea. This is indicated in a statement from the South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs
As reported, in September, during his address to the UN General Assembly, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had handed over to South Korea two North Korean soldiers who had been captured last year.
Following this, South Korea stated that the handover was to take place confidentially for the safety of the prisoners of war and their families. According to Seoul, Ukraine agreed not to disclose information about the handover.
Subsequently, Ukrainian media, citing a source in the President's Office, said the Ukrainian side denies the existence of a confidentiality agreement with Seoul.
The South Korean administration said such a denial "seriously undermines" mutual trust and harms friendly relations between the countries.
The Ukrainian government itself insisted on the confidentiality of the handover, fearing domestic criticism over the loss of an opportunity to exchange North Korean prisoners of war for Ukrainian prisoners of war. Seoul, he said, agreed to the confidentiality out of concern for the safety of the prisoners of war and their families, as well as for diplomatic and security considerations.

title: 3 Samsung phones that can compete with the new iPhone 18
body: Apple’s new iPhone 18 series has raised the bar in the premium smartphone market, but Samsung has several flagship devices capable of giving Apple’s latest models serious competition. Samsung’s Galaxy S26 series and its latest foldable devices combine powerful processors, advanced camera systems, high-refresh-rate displays and artificial intelligence features, making them strong alternatives for consumers considering the iPhone 18. Here are three Samsung phones that can compete with the new iPhone 18. 1. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra The Galaxy S26 Ultra is arguably Samsung’s strongest competitor to Apple’s top-end iPhone 18 models. The flagship comes with a 6.9-inch QHD+ AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, offering smooth scrolling and sharp visuals. Its camera system is another major selling point. The phone features a 200MP main camera alongside ultrawide and telephoto cameras, giving users extensive options for photography and long-range zoom. The Galaxy S26 Ultra also features a powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, up to 16GB of RAM and up to 1TB of storage. Samsung has retained one feature that continues to distinguish its Ultra models from Apple’s iPhones — the built-in S Pen. For users who prioritise photography, productivity, gaming and customisation, the Galaxy S26 Ultra is arguably the closest Samsung alternative to the iPhone 18 Pro Max. 2. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra For smartphone users looking for something beyond the traditional phone design, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra offers a different kind of competition. The foldable device combines a smartphone form factor with a much larger internal display, making it particularly useful for multitasking, reading, productivity and entertainment. It is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor and offers up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. The device also features a 200MP main camera and a 5,000mAh battery. While the Z Fold8 Ultra may not compete with the iPhone 18 simply by copying Apple’s conventional smartphone design, it has an advantage in screen size and multitasking. For consumers who want a premium smartphone that can also function as a compact tablet, Samsung’s foldable is a compelling alternative. 3. Samsung Galaxy S26+ The Galaxy S26+ offers many flagship features without going all the way up to the Ultra model. It comes with a 6.7-inch QHD+ AMOLED display and a 120Hz refresh rate, making it suitable for gaming, streaming and everyday use. The phone features a 50MP main camera, 12MP ultrawide camera and 10MP telephoto camera. It is available with up to 512GB of storage and packs a 4,900mAh battery, while supporting 45W wired charging. Depending on the market, the Galaxy S26+ is powered by either the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 or Samsung’s Exynos 2600 processor. The S26+ is therefore aimed at consumers who want a premium Samsung experience but do not necessarily need the Ultra model’s highest-end camera system and S Pen. title: ‘Very large question mark’: Decision on Kingston Alto rail stop won’t come until 2027
body:
Kingston remains “promising” as a potential stop on the Alto high-speed rail corridor, but an official decision may have to wait until spring, the Crown corporation said.
During its annual meeting Wednesday, Robert Prichard, chair of the Alto board of directors, said the city has made a strong case for inclusion, but a feasibility assessment would still need to be completed.
“We think there is a presumptively strong case to go to Kingston, but we still have to do the work,” he said.
The company has only officially announced Peterborough as a stop on the Toronto to Ottawa corridor.
Prichard said with each additional stop there is a tradeoff between journey time and how many passengers will be added to the trip. An analysis will need to be undertaken to determine how much a stop in Kingston will increase ridership.
“Every additional stop extends the journey time,” Prichard said.
Other eastern Ontario communities like Smiths Falls and Perth will not be directly serviced by Alto, but Prichard said those communities will still have access through the high-speed rail’s intersection with VIA Rail.
“It’s the synergy between the two systems,” he said.
Martin Imbleau, the CEO of Alto, said the company’s first priority is the Ottawa to Montreal corridor, so the earliest a decision would be made about Kingston would be spring 2027.
Kingston was not a stop on the initial corridor, Prichard said, so consultations with that community have yet to happen.
But opponents of the rail system say those who could be directly affected by the rail line, deserve to have their questions answered.
“At some point, being told to wait for answers simply isn’t good enough,” Heather Levy, local lead of Stone Mills Against Alto and a member of United Against Alto, told Global News.
“We are being asked to live inside a very large question mark, with potentially life-changing consequences hanging over us, while the people making the decisions continue to tell us to be patient,” she added.
The concern is particularly great for farmers and the owners of rural properties in Lennox and Addington and South Frontenac townships.
“What seems to get lost in that conversation is the distinction between the potential benefits of a station in Kingston and the consequences of getting the railway there,” Levy said. “For communities like Stone Mills, that could mean losing homes, severing farmland and permanently altering rural communities. Those impacts deserve at least as much consideration as the potential benefits to Kingston.”
Stone Mills is located approximately 50 km northwest of Kingston.
Imbleau said Alto will continue to listen to the concerns of residents and has new consultations planned for next year.
“We don’t want to cut land,” he said. “We will find the route that has the least impact.”
David Bellerive, founder of the advocacy organization Go Alto, said he feels Alto is actively listening to the public and “refining its plans based on community feedback.”
“The project is still in development, and finding the right solutions takes time,” he said.
At an unrelated news conference Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said the federal government will continue to work with the governments of Quebec and Ontario to advance the rail project.
Quebec’s premier designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon was adamant throughout his campaign that he would end the province’s co-operation with the project.
An Abacus poll released in the spring found 62 per cent of Canadians supported the rail project with 25 per cent strongly supporting it.

title: Diia explains how to file Europrotocol in event of traffic accident
body:
The Diia app now features a function for filing a Europrotocol report, which allows users to report a traffic accident via their smartphone without calling the patrol police or filling out a paper form.
According to a statement from the Diia press service on Thursday, to use the service, users must update the Diia app and navigate to the "Services," "Driver," and "Europrotocol" sections.
Next, users should verify the details; specifically, information about the drivers, vehicles, and insurance policies will be automatically retrieved from government registries.
The press service added that drivers will need to fill out the details of the accident and upload photos of the damaged vehicles at the scene. Subsequently, drivers will receive the other driver's consent and signature via a QR code or a notification in the Diia app.
It is noted that after completing these preliminary steps, users will need to sign the document using Diia.Sign and submit it. It is expected that after both parties have successfully signed the document, the app will automatically submit the Europrotocol to the Motor Transport Insurance Bureau of Ukraine (MTIBU), and MTIBU will subsequently forward it to the insurance companies.
"Next, contact your insurance company for further instructions," Diia said.
According to the press release, before filing the claim, you should ensure that no one is injured, that only two vehicles were involved in the accident, that neither driver is under the influence of alcohol or drugs, that both have valid MTPL insurance policies, and that they have reached an agreement regarding the circumstances of the accident.
It is expected that drivers who have the following in Diia at the same time can complete the Europrotocol: a verified RNOKPP (IPN), a digital passport (ID card), foreign passport, or residence permit, a driver's license, and a vehicle registration certificate – as the owner or authorized user – as well as a valid MTPL policy for the vehicle involved in the accident.
"In other cases, fill out a paper Europrotocol or call the police," Diia said.

title: White vs traditional marriage: Aesthetics above culture?
body: “I don’t believe a white wedding is necessary. I believe our traditional marriages are beautiful and complete. Yet, when I imagine my own wedding, I still picture myself in a white dress. My view that a white wedding is unnecessary is driven by the Pan-Africanism and love for Ghanaian culture in me, yet my interest in the white wedding is driven by the beauty that comes with it. In Ghana, marriage does not begin with a bride walking down an aisle. It can begin with a knock at the door. Across Ghana’s ethnic groups, traditional marriage ceremonies may differ in name and detail, but they share a common thread: marriage is not treated as a union between two individuals alone, but as a coming together of families. Among the Akan, this is known as kɔkɔɔkɔ, while the Ewe refer to their form of knocking as vɔƒoƒo. The Ga have Agboshimɔ, followed by rites involving acceptance, the presentation of a cover cloth, and traditional food. Among the Mole-Dagbani, customs include Diɛŋ, Nyuyu ɲmabu, Dɔyiripaya and payipin, while traditions among the Guan vary across their different communities. Despite these differences, the ceremonies generally involve families formally meeting, seeking approval, and presenting gifts or items as part of the marriage process. Then came another form of marriage: the white wedding, which involves the aisle, the white dress, the church, the vows and the words, “By the power vested in me…” And somehow, for many Ghanaians, the white wedding has become the picture many people grow up imagining when they think of what a “proper” wedding should look like. After families have gathered to recognise the union, another ceremony often follows, one in which the couple publicly makes vows to each other. Mary, a university student, says she would like to experience a white wedding because she finds them beautiful and likes the idea of wearing a gown. Like other Ghanaian women interviewed for this story, she does not consider the white wedding necessary, viewing it instead as an aesthetic choice. Marriage Under the Ordinance According to the Judicial Service of Ghana, the Marriage Ordinance, Cap. 127 provides the statutory framework for marriages under the Ordinance. An ordinance marriage is monogamous, while a customary marriage is potentially polygamous. The Judicial Service notes that marriages conducted under the Ordinance have the same legal validity whether they take place in an orthodox church, metropolitan assembly or court. In other words, an ordinance marriage does not become legally valid simply because there is a white gown, a church, an aisle or a bridal train. Yet for some Ghanaians, the appeal of the white wedding extends beyond its legal status. For Sarah, a university graduate, it is largely about the beauty and emotion associated with the ceremony. “I feel like it is just beautiful, being in your white dress and having your daddy or this man walking you down the aisle with your man standing there. Like those ones where the groom sees you and he starts crying? How crazy, but yeah, it is beautiful. A white wedding is beautiful, so that’s what appeals to me.” But aesthetics are not the only factor. For Sarah, her Christian faith also influences her desire for a white wedding. “I am a Christian, and a white wedding is not all the time, but most of the time it takes place in a church. And there’s this man of God blessing your marriage, and it’s like you are getting married in front of God, like God is in your union, and I feel like that is good, that is beautiful. So, I’d say yes, maybe my religion is part of why I may want a white wedding.” For some Christians, therefore, the church ceremony carries significance beyond the aesthetics of the wedding. Some churches have specific requirements concerning marriage, where couples who have not undergone a church wedding cannot take the Holy Communion. Does the Bible Require a White Wedding? The Bible contains several passages that speak about marriage, companionship, and the responsibilities of husbands and wives. Genesis 2:24 speaks of a man leaving his father and mother and holding fast to his wife, while Ecclesiastes 4:9 describes the value of two people working together. Proverbs 18:22 speaks positively of finding a wife, and Ephesians 5:25 instructs husbands to love their wives. These passages affirm marriage and the responsibilities that come with it, but they do not prescribe a specific modern wedding format, whether a couple must marry in a church, wear a white gown, walk down an aisle, or have a particular type of ceremony. There is nothing wrong with a white wedding; in fact, it is beautiful, sophisticated and memorable. What matters is the couple involved, their financial readiness, and their motivation for desiring both the traditional and white wedding.

title: Lithuania puts up to 100 soldiers on Kaliningrad border as officials brace for possible Russian mobilization
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Lithuania plans to deploy up to 100 soldiers to support border guards along its frontier with Russia's Kaliningrad Oblast, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said on 7 October. Lithuanian Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas has described the deployment as a preventive measure linked to possible Russian mobilization and a recent incident on the Latvia-Belarus border, where masked, armed escorts tried to push a group of migrants into Latvia. Katelynas said Lithuania could face people trying to avoid mobilization and seeking asylum. Kaunas said he had granted permission to use Lithuanian soldiers to strengthen border protection for the next several weeks. “The order starts being implemented immediately,” he wrote on Facebook. Russia denies a new mobilization The Kremlin denies a new mobilization is coming. In early September, Russian President Vladimir Putin called reports of one "complete nonsense " and "an information attack on Russia." Ukraine's military and foreign intelligence services say Russia's General Staff has prepared a scenario to mobilize 600,000 people over 2026 and 2027. On 28 September, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that "in effect, the Russians have already begun additional mobilization." Frontier-station patrols for a couple of weeks, possibly longer On 8 October, the Lithuanian army said soldiers were being brought in to help the State Border Guard Service from that day. A company-sized unit was planned for the assignment, initially for two weeks, with the option to extend. Soldiers will patrol with border guards in frontier-station areas, while mobile patrols, mobile observation posts, and military police crews may be added as needed. The army described the deployment as preventive and a normal form of interagency cooperation. Kaunas had told LRT TV the soldiers would stay until 16 October. On the morning of 8 October, he said the deployment "was supposed to start" overnight and that he would check with the army. On 8 October, the Lithuanian army said soldiers were being brought in to help the State Border Guard Service from that day. Kaunas also said that “ on the Kaliningrad side ” there were no physical barriers, unlike the border with Belarus. Lithuania says its border guards are stretched On 8 October, Katelynas said the border guard service’s capacity was insufficient, with shifts growing while officer numbers were not increasing. He said the threat level had not changed. In a Facebook post the previous day, he said the situation at Lithuania’s border was calm and there was no reason to panic. He said Russia was planning mobilization after the elections and that Lithuania may face people trying to avoid it and seeking asylum. Lithuania's State Border Guard Service had turned back 1,693 people trying to cross illegally from Belarus this year and about 26,300 since the migration crisis began, as reported by ELTA on 8 October. Katelynas said 43 migrants tried to enter southern Lithuania last week and were turned back. title: What happens on Day 31? - Atiku rejects FG’s 30-day petrol discount
body: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has rejected the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol price discount, describing the measure as a temporary intervention that cannot address the hardship caused by high fuel prices. Atiku, in an article by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, said the offer was coming after years of rising fuel prices and worsening cost-of-living pressures. The former vice-president said Nigerians should not be expected to accept a one-month discount as a solution to the economic difficulties they have faced under the administration of President Bola Tinubu. “Atiku totally rejects this calendar-scheduled, election-laced subsidy package. Nigerians are not fools to be offered a month of discounted fuel after years of punishing prices and then expected to forget the hardship when the discount expires,” he said. He described the proposal as a political response to a crisis created in part by the government’s fuel pricing policies, questioning what would happen after the 30-day period. “What happens on Day 31? Nigerians wake up to the same brutal prices, the same punishing transport fares and the same rising cost of food,” Atiku said. He also questioned the scope of the proposed discount, noting that it would apply to petrol sold at NNPC stations. According to him, the government had yet to disclose how much motorists would save per litre or guarantee that savings enjoyed by transport operators would translate into lower fares for passengers. The former vice-president said the government’s decision to introduce the temporary intervention amounted to an admission that the hardship caused by high fuel prices could no longer be ignored. “This volte-face proves that the production-support proposal I have advanced is workable, achievable and not complicated,” Atiku said. He reiterated his proposal for capped and budgeted production support tied to petrol refined in Nigeria, with safeguards designed to ensure that consumers benefit while supporting domestic refining. Atiku said the government should pursue a sustainable solution instead of providing temporary relief that would expire after one month. “Nigerians need lasting relief, not a countdown to the return of hardship. Tinubu’s government cannot spend years telling Nigerians to endure, then offer 30 days of relief and call it a solution,” he said. The Federal Government had earlier announced a 30-day discount on petrol sold by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, with public transport operators to receive priority under the arrangement. Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed the plan on Thursday during a press briefing in Abuja on petrol prices and subsidy-related issues. Atiku, however, maintained that Nigerians needed a lasting reduction in the cost of living. “Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again,” he said. The post What happens on Day 31? - Atiku rejects FG’s 30-day petrol discount appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Retail trade turnover during 8M 2026 above last-year figure — Russian Industry Ministry
body:
OMSK, October 8. /TASS/. The retail trade turnover in Russia gained more than 5% as of the end ofg January - August 2026, Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Roman Chekushov said.
"The Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade support the multi-format pattern. The results of moving along this path speak for themselves - the retail trade turnover increased by more than 4% as of the end of 2025. Its incremental growth is also more than 5% during the current eight months," Chekushov said in a video address.
The sector passed through a serious transformation in recent years and accumulated domestic solutions in the sphere of software, equipment and transport, the official said. "Provision of consumer rights acts as a cornerstone in this regard. They must have an opportunity to buy high quality and safe products by any convenient method," Chekushov stressed.

title: Power plants utilise 81% capacity — NERC
body: …Towers collapse leave Nasarawa communities in darkness By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Power plants in Nigeria utilised 81 per cent of their available generation capacity in September 2026, producing an average 4,089 megawatts (MW) from an available capacity of 5,038MW, the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has said. NERC disclosed this in its September 2026 factsheet on the operational performance of power plants, showing that 81 per cent of the capacity available to generating plants was utilised during the month. According to the commission, the average available capacity of 5,038MW represented a 5.89 per cent increase from the previous month, while average hourly generation of 4,089MW declined marginally by 0.30 per cent. The commission said the 81 per cent capacity utilisation was reflected in the average load factor recorded by the power plants during the month. Kainji Power Plant recorded the highest load factor among the major energy producers at 98 per cent, generating an average of 341MW from an available capacity of 347MW. Egbin and Afam 2 plants each recorded a 94 per cent load factor. Egbin generated an average 402MW from an available capacity of 429MW, while Afam 2 generated 337MW from 358MW. Ihovbor 2 recorded a 91 per cent load factor, generating 343MW from an available capacity of 376MW, while Shiroro recorded 86 per cent, with average generation of 388MW from 450MW. Delta and Jebba plants each recorded 79 per cent load factors. Delta generated 300MW from an available capacity of 378MW, while Jebba generated 388MW from 490MW. Odukpani recorded a 70 per cent load factor, while Okpai recorded 68 per cent, generating 203MW from 290MW and 253MW from 370MW available capacities, respectively. Towers collapse disrupt Nasarawa power supply Meanwhile, electricity supply to customers in Keffi and Akwanga in Nasarawa State has been disrupted following the collapse of three transmission towers along the Karu-Keffi-Akwanga 132kV transmission line corridor. The Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) said Towers T78, T79 and T80 collapsed during rainy and windy conditions on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, affecting power supply through the 132/33kV Keffi and 132/33kV Akwanga transmission substations. According to TCN, the transmission line tripped on overcurrent relay protection at about 4:06pm on Wednesday, prompting investigations that revealed the collapse of the three towers. The company said it subsequently isolated the affected transmission line for safety reasons, resulting in the unavailability of all 33kV outgoing feeders at the Keffi and Akwanga substations. “Consequently, all 33kV outgoing feeders at the Keffi and Akwanga Transmission Substations are presently unavailable. No load can therefore be nominated on the affected feeders in the interim,” TCN said in a statement issued Thursday. The development means electricity distribution to customers supplied through the affected feeders in Keffi and Akwanga will remain unavailable until the transmission infrastructure is repaired and bulk power supply restored. TCN said its engineers were already on site assessing the extent of the damage to determine the materials and other requirements needed to commence restoration work. The post Power plants utilise 81% capacity — NERC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukrainian medics learn about the Dutch model of care for premature babies
body:
As reported by an Ukrinform correspondent in The Hague, during the visit Ukrainian medics learned about the organization of the neonatal intensive care unit and the approaches used by their Dutch colleagues to treat and care for premature babies. Dutch specialists demonstrated advanced technologies and shared a new approach that involves actively engaging parents in their child’s care. The approach was explained by Kiki Ruhe, a Dutch nursing scientist and Neonatal Intensive Care Nurse.
“Previously, parents were welcome, but they were not directly involved in caring for their tiny newborns. We now have a great deal of research showing that involving parents is beneficial for the parents themselves, for the children, and for medical staff,” Ruhe said.
She explained that the family integrated care approach includes, among other things, 24-hour access for parents to the unit, access to essential facilities, participation in medical rounds, and training in how to care for their child.
According to Ruhe, parents are taught practical skills such as feeding a baby with a syringe, changing diapers, practicing Kangaroo Care, and performing other procedures depending on the newborn’s condition.
The unit cares for babies born from approximately 24 weeks of gestation. It currently has between 18 and 25 operational beds, out of a designed capacity of 36.
Ruhe also said that during the visit, Ukrainian specialists mainly asked practical questions, particularly about medical equipment and respiratory support for newborns.
According to her, the smallest baby she treated at the unit weighed 410 grams.
“Working with such patients requires significant effort and involves gradually engaging parents in their care,” she said.
The experience-sharing program for Ukrainian medical professionals was organized by the Ukrainian Academy of Pediatric Specialties and the NGO Early Birds.
“We are grateful to the team at Emma Children’s Hospital for their openness and for the opportunity to learn about the work of the neonatology department. Here, we saw how the family-integrated care approach is implemented in daily practice: parents are part of the team caring for a premature baby. Particular attention is paid to training healthcare professionals, including communication with families. As a parent-led organization, it is important for us to learn from this experience so that we can help promote the implementation in Ukraine of approaches that support children and their parents,” said Oleksandra Balyasna, co-organizer of the program and head of the Early Birds NGO.
Among the Ukrainian specialists taking part in the visit was pediatrician and anesthesiologist Iryna Kondratova, who previously headed the Kharkiv Regional Perinatal Center. During the intense shelling of Kharkiv in 2022, she and her team remained at the hospital around the clock, caring for women in labor and saving newborns.
“Ukraine needs a comprehensive system of medical and social support for children who are born prematurely, have severe illnesses, or receive incurable diagnoses. The focus of this system should not be only on the child, but on the entire family,” she said.
According to Kondratova, Ukraine has individual elements of support for such children, but they are not integrated into a single system. This includes support from the moment a child is born, assistance to the family during treatment and preparation for discharge, further outpatient follow-up, assessment of the child’s development, and, when necessary, palliative care.
She was particularly impressed by the way the neonatal intensive care unit in Amsterdam is organized. According to her, the focus is not only on the child, who may require mechanical ventilation, continuous monitoring, and a large amount of medical equipment. The mother, father, and other family members can remain close to the child.
“This is not even a hospital room in the way we understand it. It is more like a three-room apartment built around the family. And if there are older children in the family, they can stay here as well,” the doctor said.
She also highlighted how thoroughly the needs of medical equipment are taken into account when the space is designed. In one of the rooms, she counted 22 electrical outlets around the child’s bed alone.
“An engineer or a builder simply would not understand all the requirements involved. Doctors and nurses need to be consulted before implementing this philosophy. This is all about the family, dignity, and the best practices in the world, so that the family does not feel abandoned. I find it truly remarkable,” she said.
Kondratova also highlighted the role of nurses in the Dutch healthcare system. According to her, the visit to the neonatal unit and children’s hospice made it clear that a significant share of the workload is carried by nursing staff.
As reported by Ukrinform, in December 2025, the renovated Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, along with the hospital’s mobile neonatology team, was officially opened at the Okhmatdyt National Specialized Children’s Hospital under Ukraine’s Ministry of Health.

title: Tumu Municipal Hospital receives new delivery bed to boost maternity care
body: The Tumu Municipal Hospital’s Maternity unit has received a new delivery bed and light to support its operations. Almost all the beds in the ward have broken down, making it extremely difficult for health workers to provide women in labour with a suitable and comfortable place to deliver. However, the challenge has been slightly eased with the provision of a new bed by a group of individuals who describe themselves as friends of the Member of Parliament. The Tumu Municipal Hospital continues to grapple with several challenges, including the absence of a dedicated children’s ward and a deplorable maternity ward. The beds in the ward are not only in poor condition but are also too small to comfortably accommodate women during delivery. Acting Nurse Manager at the facility, Cicelia Haluri Iddrisu, says the situation is putting considerable strain on the hospital’s operations. She explained that the limited space in the maternity ward makes it difficult for the facility to accommodate more women at the same time. “The ward generally is so old, and we don’t have most of the equipment that we need to use. The space too is so small, so if you have three or four women coming in, it’s difficult to get all of them into that space, and there’s also no privacy in the room,” she said. But there is now some relief for women using the delivery room, as friends of the Member of Parliament for Sissala East have donated a well-furnished delivery bed to the facility. For the donors, seeing people in the area struggle to access proper care due to the poor state of the ward prompted them to support the hospital. “I see people in need, and we decided to come and help”, Funda Gocuk said. “The government should be giving the help, but they don’t always do it. Therefore, people of the North always tend to suffer. So, this time round, we decided to go for maternity care, and hopefully this will help the women here,” Sandra Kodimah added. Receiving the donation on behalf of the Medical Superintendent, Dr Raymond Danso, Head of Pharmacy, Johnson Yandanbil, commended the donors for the gesture, describing it as a timely intervention. He, however, noted that the hospital continues to face several other challenges that require urgent attention. “Tumu Hospital is one of the referral hospitals in this Municipality, and so we conduct over 100 deliveries in a month. So, this particular intervention has come at the right time. However, we also lack a Children’s ward and other facilities, and we call for urgent intervention,” he said. The Member of Parliament, Mohammed Issah Bataglia, expressed gratitude to the three individuals for their support and assured the hospital of further interventions to help address some of its outstanding needs. “I sincerely do appreciate their efforts. They’re doing very little things that are having a great impact on the people,” he noted.

title: Saskatoon encampment removal resumes to address ‘safety concerns,’ city says
body:
The process of removing an encampment in Saskatoon began Thursday morning after previously being paused by the city due to protests .
The clearing of the site, which sits on private property at 20th Street and Avenue K South, began Thursday. It has the city’s support, as well as that of community, Indigenous and provincial government organizations, Yvonne Raymer, deputy fire chief at the Saskatoon Fire Department, told reporters at a news conference Thursday after the work began.
Police officers and firefighters were witnessed at the site by Global News crews on the ground.
It comes after an injunction application was dismissed last week at Saskatoon Court of King’s Bench over a lack of standing from the applicants. A second injunction attempt was originally supposed to be heard in court on Thursday, but the interim application was denied with a court hearing still set for Oct. 27.
Global News has reached out to Lawyers with Community Legal Assistance Services for Saskatoon Inner City, the party involved in the second injunction request, for comment.
“Encampments are removed because they begin to become unsafe for both the residents living in them, the schools, services, businesses and neighbourhoods around them,” Raymer said.
Clean-up work at the encampment included representatives offering available supports to those who live there. Encampment residents who reject those offers are told they must move out, she said. The deputy fire chief was unsure if the residents are being given a deadline for when their belongings must be removed, as Saskatoon police officers are also at the scene to support fire department staff and ensure safety.
Encampments in general present significant fire, public safety and sanitation risks – and the site being removed Thursday is no exception, according to a City of Saskatoon news release.
“Safety concerns increase as encampments grow,” Raymer said, adding since Monday the city’s fire service has been called to four fires at various encampments.
Two of those fires spread to trees in Optimist Park, another destroyed a makeshift shelter in the backyard of a vacant property and the fourth was said to have become out of control in a park off Idylwyld Drive.
The city also alleged possible gang activity, domestic violence, assaults and open drug use have been observed or reported at the 20th Street encampment.
“While we recognize the challenges people face, we also have an obligation to address significant wider community safety risks and work towards safer, more sustainable alternatives,” Raymer said.
Saskatoon Tribal Council (STC) Tribal Chief Mark Arcand described the encampments as having “too much violence and gang activity, including drugs and sex trafficking,” in the city’s news release.
“In the last few weeks, we have seen an escalation of violence throughout that neighbourhood and seen that relatives who had been interested in supports are now refusing them,” he continued.
“The real solution is for people to access the supports they need, to get housing, addiction treatment, medical care, and connection to culture, in a safe environment. This won’t happen as long as they are at an encampment.”
He said help is available through the STC – including its housing outreach program and outdoor washroom project.
The exact cost of this removal project is not yet available, according to the fire chief.

title: Anne Carson’s Nobel Literature Prize ‘A Proud Moment For Canada’, Says PM
body: Canadian poet Anne Carson winning the Nobel prize for literature is a “proud moment” for the country, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday. The 76-year-old’s works feature “wit, imagination, and a style entirely her own,” Carney said on X. “She has brought ancient stories to new audiences and transformed the way we think about literature,” he said, calling the award “an extraordinary achievement and a proud moment for Canada.” A renowned classicist, Carson has taught at several prestigious Canadian and American universities, including McGill in Montreal. She joined McGill’s Department of Classics in 1988 and left the university in 2002. “This is a wonderfully deserved honour for Anne Carson, whose work has captivated readers around the world by bringing ancient voices into conversation with the present,” Lisa Shapiro, McGill’s dean of arts, was quoted as saying by The McGill Reporter. “Her extraordinary talent, originality and intellectual depth have had a profound influence on contemporary literature. We are proud that McGill was her academic home for many years and delighted to see her remarkable contributions recognized on the world stage.” Outside the university in Montreal, Vicky Huang, a 24-year-old political science student, expressed pride. “My friends and I love ‘Eros the Bittersweet,’ so this is such exciting news,” she told AFP. “Yeah, I mean, the fact that she’s a Canadian woman working in high literature makes all of us really proud.” The post Anne Carson’s Nobel Literature Prize ‘A Proud Moment For Canada’, Says PM appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Foreign ministry clarifies foreign traders’ status after Kalisto remarks
body: South Sudan’s Foreign Affairs Ministry said on Thursday there was no government directive requiring foreign nationals to leave the country, adding that commercial activities are governed by national laws and any restrictions must be handled by the relevant authorities in accordance with the law. The statement followed remarks by Juba County Caretaker Commissioner Kalisto Ladu Nyigilo calling for foreign nationals to be barred from operating small-scale businesses in the capital. The ministry said it had taken note of recent public statements concerning the participation of foreign nationals in small-scale commercial activities in Juba. “There is no directive from the national government requiring foreign nationals to leave South Sudan,” it said in a statement dated Oct. 8. Ladu said earlier this week that foreign nationals should not operate small-scale retail businesses in Juba and should instead focus on wholesale trade, factories and other larger investments. He cited businesses including the sale of chapati, onions and tomatoes, as well as motorcycle taxi services, saying such activities should be reserved for South Sudanese. His remarks were later circulated on social media as an order for foreign nationals to leave Juba or South Sudan within seven days. Ladu denied issuing such an order, saying he did not have the authority to expel foreign nationals from the country. The Foreign Affairs Ministry did not specifically address whether Juba County has the authority to restrict foreign nationals from particular types of businesses. It said commercial activities are subject to South Sudanese laws and regulations and that any measures affecting such activities should be handled by the competent authorities in accordance with the law. “The Government recognises that commercial activities are subject to applicable laws and regulations,” the ministry said. It also reaffirmed its commitment to the rule of law, legitimate foreign investment and constructive relations with foreign nationals and their respective countries. The statement comes amid concerns among foreign traders, including Ugandans, Kenyans and other East Africans, who operate small businesses in Juba. Uganda has also sought talks with South Sudan over restrictions affecting foreign-owned retail businesses. Ladu, who was appointed caretaker commissioner last week, has said his position is aimed at protecting economic opportunities for South Sudanese rather than expelling foreigners. The post Foreign ministry clarifies foreign traders’ status after Kalisto remarks appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russia’s censorship agency bans two dystopian novels by Olga Ptitseva about an alternate Russia ruled by the ‘Party of Cold’
body: Russia’s communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, has banned Olga Ptitseva’s novels “Dvesti trety den zimy” (“The 203rd Day of Winter”) and “Vesna vody” (“Spring of Water”). A notice appeared on the God Literatury portal on October 7, Vyorstka reported. “The book in question has been added to Roskomnadzor’s Unified Register of Prohibited Information and the Registry of Book Assessments kept by the Russian Book Union’s expert center and must be withdrawn from public circulation in Russia,” the website said. On October 2, Roskomnadzor ordered the portal to remove information about “Vesna vody.” On July 16, the portal had removed information about “Dvesti trety den zimy,” the first book of the duology, at the regulator’s request. The books have also disappeared from the website of their publisher, Polyandria No Age, and from the catalogs of LitRes and Chitai-Gorod. Polyandria confirmed that Roskomnadzor had banned them. The ban may have been prompted by signs of “propaganda of nontraditional sexual relationships” in the books, The Blueprint reported . The two novels form a dystopian duology set in an alternate Russia, where eternal winter sets in after the Party of Cold comes to power. Residents are required to maintain a prescribed level of snow cover, food is distributed using ration cards, and dissenters are sent to freezers. Ptitseva confirmed that her books had been withdrawn from sale. “Friends, it’s true that DTDZ [the novel ‘Dvesti trety den zimy’] has been pulled from sale, but I’m OK. Hugs to all of you,” she said on her Telegram channel. Olga Ptitseva has written several novels and collections of contemporary prose. In 2023, her novel “Tam, gde tsvetet polyn” (“Where Wormwood Blooms”) was adapted into a television series of the same name. A year later, the book was nominated for the Yasnaya Polyana literary prize in the Youth category. Her novel “Vyidi iz shkafa” (“Come Out of the Closet”) was shortlisted for the FICTION35 prize, while “Krai chudes” (“Land of Wonders”) was longlisted for the Lyceum prize. title: USS Arleigh Burke enters dry dock in Spain, expanding U.S. Navy maintenance capability in Europe
body: The Navy said it was the first such docking in the 6th Fleet’s operating area since the arrival of Forward Deployed Naval Forces–Europe destroyers. Performing the work locally is intended to improve operational readiness and ship availability. “The dry docking of Arleigh Burke is a major milestone in expanding U.S. Navy forward-deployed maintenance capabilities in Europe,” said Vice Adm. J.T. Anderson, commander of U.S. 6th Fleet. “By integrating dry docking into planned maintenance periods overseas, the Navy is increasing material readiness for our forward-deployed warships.” Military and civilian personnel from the Forward Deployed Regional Maintenance Center are working alongside the ship’s crew and Navantia personnel. They are carrying out the scheduled maintenance and modernization throughout the availability. Supporting NATO missions from Spain Arleigh Burke is one of five forward-deployed destroyers stationed at Naval Station Rota, Spain. It is assigned to Commander, Task Force 65 in support of NATO’s integrated air and missile defense architecture. The ship moved its homeport from Norfolk, Virginia, to Rota in April 2021 after nearly 30 years in Norfolk. It joined the 6th Fleet’s Destroyer Squadron 60. The forward-deployed destroyers operate across Europe and Africa, from the Cape of Good Hope to the Arctic Circle. Their missions support maritime security and stability. Lead ship of the Arleigh Burke class Commissioned in Norfolk on July 4, 1991, USS Arleigh Burke is the lead ship of its guided-missile destroyer class. Bath Iron Works laid its keel in Bath, Maine, on December 6, 1988. The ship was launched on September 16, 1989, by Roberta Gorsuch Burke, wife of Adm. Arleigh A. Burke. Both attended its commissioning, where the admiral told the crew: “This ship was built to fight. You better know how!” The destroyer is named after Burke, who distinguished himself during World War II and the Korean War. He later served as chief of naval operations during the Eisenhower and Kennedy administrations. The ship’s awards include three Navy Unit Commendations, three Meritorious Unit Commendations and eight Battle Efficiency Awards. It has also received the National Defense Service Medal, Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal, Kuwait Liberation Medal, 13 Sea Service Deployment Ribbons and one Overseas Service Ribbon. U.S. 6th Fleet is permanently assigned to U.S. Naval Forces Europe-Africa, headquartered in Naples, Italy. The command operates U.S. naval forces in the European Command and Africa Command areas of responsibility.

title: Trump rules out attack on Iran before midterm elections
body: President Donald Trump on Thursday said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections and that Washington was engaged in “productive discussions” with Tehran. In a post on Truth Social, Mr Trump said Iran was in a “very bad condition” economically and militarily and the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz would remain in “full force”. “We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3,” he wrote. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran.” The announcement comes a day after reports in US media that Washington was preparing to launch renewed military action against Iran before the midterm elections. Last month, Mr Trump said the war with Iran would end “immediately” after the midterm elections. He has also previously said the US was no longer seeking a negotiated end to the war. Shortly afterwards, he said fuel prices and the cost of living would go down. But polls show the war Mr Trump started alongside Israel in February is unpopular among US voters . A major issue has been the rise in fuel and everyday prices, which has followed disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway, through which about a fifth of the world’s oil supply typically flows, has emerged as a major sticking point for Mr Trump. The Republican President had campaigned on promises of lower costs and repeatedly blamed inflation on his predecessor, Joe Biden. With the elections less than a month away, Mr Trump is also facing historically low approval ratings. The midterm elections are critical for Mr Trump, who still has two years left in office. At stake is control of Congress, where Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers.

title: Russian attacks plunge Kyiv into near-total darkness, disrupt power, metro, water supply
body:
Residential buildings are seen without power during widespread outages following Russian attacks on Kyiv, Ukraine on Oct. 8, 2026. (Olga Rudenko / The Kyiv Independent)
The Russian attack on Ukrainian energy infrastructure on Oct. 8 has caused widespread power outages across the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, home to over 3 million people.
"There was an attack on one of the energy facilities important for the city of Kyiv," Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said . "Energy workers are doing everything possible to restore electricity as quickly as possible." Throughout the day, the city experienced power outages in most neighborhoods, with the city metro shut down due to lack of electricity. Without power, many residents also reported a lack of running water. As of 12:30 a.m. local time on Oct. 9, areas of the city to the left of the Dnipro river still remained without power, while electricity has been restored in parts of the right bank. Ukraine's state electrical operator, Ukrenergo, announced that limits to electricity consumption will be placed on certain regions of the country on Oct. 9 due to the attack.
DTEK subsequently announced that emergency power cuts had been introduced on Kyiv's right bank and in the Bucha and Vyshhorod districts of Kyiv Oblast on Ukrenergo's orders.
Допис, поширений Kyiv Independent (@kyivindependent_official)
Kyiv Independent reporters across the city on Oct. 8 observed power cuts in Podil, Pechersk, Solomianskyi districts, and the left bank. Ahead of winter, the sound of generators returned to Kyiv throughout affected neighborhoods, as businesses sought to keep operating. In the dark of the evening, buskers continued to perform on the capital's main street of Khreshchatyk.
The drop in voltage temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the Kyiv City State Administration (KMDA) said . Other parts of the capital's public transport network were also affected.
The city administration said that some services had been temporarily suspended because of the drop in voltage, while authorities were working to replace part of the Borshchahivka high-speed tram line with buses.
Kyiv Independent reporters described heavy traffic, people hailing taxis, and streets filling with people, as commuters sought alternative transportation.
The power disruption also affected Kyiv's water network. The city administration warned that residents on the right bank could experience interruptions in water supply because lower voltage had reduced pressure in the system, particularly in the Holosiivskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Solomianskyi, and Shevchenkivskyi districts. By 9 p.m. local time, pumping equipment was reactivated, though the city said it would take "some time" to fully restore normal water pressure throughout the entire network.
Earlier on Oct. 8, Ukraine's largest private energy company, DTEK, announced emergency power shutdowns in parts of Kyiv Oblast, including the Brovary, Bucha, Vyshhorod, and Boryspil districts.
The Kyiv Oblast Military Administration said Russia had significantly intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in recent weeks, targeting power lines and transformers and disrupting electricity transmission to consumers.
Energy workers are operating around the clock to repair damaged equipment and stabilize the grid, the administration said.
The disruptions followed a morning of repeated Russian drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region that killed and injured civilians and damaged buildings and infrastructure.
Russian drone strikes on Oct. 8 killed four people and injured at least 19 in Kyiv, the city's Mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said .
Polina Moroziuk is a junior reporter at the Kyiv Independent. She holds an MSc in Human Rights and Politics from the London School of Economics and a BSc from the University of Amsterdam. Before joining the newsroom, she worked in human rights advocacy and as a project assistant at a research and consultancy organisation, supporting projects for international organisations including UNICEF and War Child, with a focus on Ukraine and the Middle East.

title: ‘Pink Lung’, or why claim that Abkhazia has no good wine is outdated. VIDEO
body: Wine in Abkhazia For a long time, Abkhazia was known mainly for its basic range of wines. The region’s unpredictable climate, with annual rainfall of up to 2,000 mm, was seen as a challenge, as was the popularity of mass-produced semi-sweet wines. However, modern winemaking practices have challenged this perception. Today, Abkhaz wine producers are shifting their focus towards premium wines. The Association of Winemakers is actively reviving local indigenous grape varieties. It says fermentation control and modern scientific methods now make it possible to produce delicate, dry and fresh rosé wines. title: Telecel Ghana unveils Project X with Black Sherif partnership
body: Telecel Ghana has unveiled Project X, a new initiative in partnership with Ghanaian music star Black Sherif, aimed at engaging young people while promoting the Telecel Cash platform. Speaking at the launch, Chief Executive of Telecel Ghana, Ing. Patricia Obo-Nai, said the partnership brings together the bold and vibrant Telecel brand with the story and influence of Black Sherif. She said the initiative will run over the coming year, with Black Sherif delivering a series of surprises to consumers through his social media platforms. “Over the next year, almost every month, there will be surprises, and he will bear the surprises on behalf of Telecel Cash. So anytime he goes live, people need to listen to him, because you don’t know what surprise he has,” she said. Ing. Obo-Nai also highlighted the security of Telecel Cash, assuring customers that their funds are protected as long as they keep their passwords and passcodes confidential. “We wanted to portray how safe and secure Telecel Cash is, and you can keep your money with us, and you know it’s safe,” she added. Black Sherif, who is at the centre of the partnership, also encouraged Ghanaians to use Telecel Cash and follow his social media platforms for updates on the campaign. He said his appearances on TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram would include special codes, free transactions, gifts, and other rewards for consumers. “When you see me talking, it’s not just talking, not just playing music. There’s a Blacko code. I have codes that I will be sharing for free transactions, all of that. You’ll be getting gifts and tokens from me,” he added. Project X is expected to deepen customer engagement and encourage greater use of the Telecel Cash wallet and Telecel Play app.

title: Nigerian man, Chimaobim arrested after caught with pants off, exposing self in public in US
body: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has arrested a Nigerian national, Chimaobim Adedayo Igbojekwe in Pennsylvania after he pleaded guilty to a disorderly conduct charge following a public exposure incident. The U.S . Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said ICE took Igbojekwe into custody on October 1, following his arrest by local police on September 27. According to DHS, Igbojekwe pleaded guilty to the disorderly conduct charge. Following his conviction, ICE arrested him on October 1. Local reports cited by DHS said Igbojekwe was working as a canvasser for Janelle Stelson, the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania’s 10th Congressional District, when the incident occurred. He was allegedly found in a residential neighbourhood near a park with his trousers down and exposed in public, with residents, including children, in the area. ICE Deputy Director Charles Wall criticised Stelson’s campaign for employing Igbojekwe, while announcing the arrest. “It’s unbelievable that Janelle Stelson would employ an illegal alien to work on a Congressional campaign, let alone a pervert who exposed himself in public,” Wall said. “Every single day, the men and women of DHS are working hard to target and remove dangerous illegal aliens like this sicko from our communities. The Trump Administration will always put the safety of the American people first.” DHS said Igbojekwe was lawfully admitted into the US in June 2017 but remained in the country after his authorised period expired in November 2019. He was subsequently granted deferred action by the Biden administration in September 2021. The department did not provide further details on his current immigration status or say when removal proceedings against him would be concluded. The case comes amid the Trump administration’s wider immigration enforcement campaign, with ICE continuing to arrest and seek the removal of non-citizens accused of violating US immigration or criminal laws.
