title: Syria deepens diplomatic ties with US as it weighs role in Saudi conflict with Houthis - analysis
body: Syrian Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani met with US Presidential Special Envoy to Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack in Istanbul, Syrian state media said on October 8. This comes amid rumors in the region about Damascus supporting Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. It also comes amid Syria's continuing demands that Israel withdraw from areas that the Jewish state seized in 2024 near the Golan border.The meeting with Barrack came just after Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh this week. He held talks with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS).“Sharaa and the Saudi crown prince discussed relations between their countries and ways to develop them, as well as regional developments and issues of mutual concern, with the aim of supporting security and stability, according to official statements on Tuesday,” the Arab Weekly noted.Barrack has played a key role in advancing US policy in Syria. He is also envoy to Iraq, which means he coordinates US policy in a broad part of the region. “The meeting also addressed prospects for cooperation and coordination on issues of mutual interest, as well as efforts to support security and stability in the region,” Syrian state media reported.Relations between the United States and Syria have undergone a dramatic transformation since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime in December 2024. After decades of hostility, sanctions, and diplomatic isolation, Washington has moved toward working with Sharaa, Syria's new president.During the Assad era, relations were strained by Syria's support for Hezbollah and other terrorist organizations, its close ties with Iran and Russia, and its involvement in Lebanon. The US imposed sanctions on Damascus and withdrew its ambassador in 2005, although diplomatic talks later resumed. Then-US secretary of state John Kerry and House speaker Nancy Pelosi appeared open to better ties.Relations deteriorated following the Syrian protests in 2011 as part of the Arab Spring. The regime's violent crackdown led to the US essentially closing its embassy in 2012. It helped provide limited support for the Syrian rebels.US pursues closer ties with post-Assad Syria despite concerns over Sharaa's pastThe fall of Assad opened a new chapter. US diplomats visited Damascus in December 2024, establishing contact with the new authorities.However, some in Washington urged caution because Syria's new leader had previously led Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), an organization with roots in al-Qaeda.  Israel also urged caution. However, US President Donald Trump has actively pursued ties with Damascus.The major breakthrough came on May 14, 2025, when Trump met Sharaa in Riyadh. The meeting, arranged with MBS, was the first between American and Syrian presidents in 25 years. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan participated by telephone. Trump encouraged Sharaa to cooperate against ISIS, address foreign terrorist activity, and pursue improved relations with Israel.US envoy Tom Barrack plays key role in Syria rapprochement and regional security talksBarrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and special envoy for Syria, became the central figure in the rapprochement. He visited Damascus in May 2025, raised the American flag at the US diplomatic residence, and held discussions with Sharaa. His role expanded to mediating regional security issues, including Syria's relations with Israel and the integration of armed groups into state institutions.Syria has strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Riyadh is now working with Pakistan, Turkey and US Central Command (CENTCOM) regarding the Houthi threats.The Houthis targeted Saudi Arabia on October 7. Riyadh has backed a Yemeni government offensive against the Houthis this week.Syria, UAE discuss stronger economic ties and regional security cooperationAs Barrack met with Syria's Foreign Minister, the Syrian President Shara'a held a call with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.“During the call, the two leaders discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and ways to develop them in a manner that serves their shared interests, as well as the latest regional developments,” Syrian state media SANA said.“The two sides also explored ways to boost economic and investment cooperation and expand partnerships between the two countries, stressing the importance of continuing coordination and communication on issues of common interest.”Syria has sought to keep out of a conflict in Lebanon. It is unlikely it will want to send more than a limited force to Saudi Arabia. Nevertheless, it remains to be seen what happens next.Barrack posted on X/Twitter on October 3 that “President Trump opened the door to Syria's recovery. Restoring financial connectivity is how we help turn that opportunity into lasting prosperity.” He was “pleased to join the Treasury banking roundtable with Syrian financial leaders and US banks and payment providers,' he added.“Combating illicit finance, advancing credible reforms, and rebuilding confidence are essential to responsibly reconnecting Syria to the global financial system,” Barrack wrote.

title: ‘How Will It Be Funded Sustainably?’ Again, FG Questions Calls For Return Of Fuel Subsidy
body: The Federal Government has again cautioned against calls for the return of the petroleum subsidy, saying the country would be worse off if the policy were reversed. Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and the Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said this on Thursday during a press briefing on fuel prices and the subsidy questions. “We remain open to ideas, but any credible proposer should answer three questions. Number one, what will it cost? Number two, how will it be funded sustainably? Number three, what pump price will it deliver? We will engage in good faith with any proposer that shows its arithmetic,” he said at the event in Abuja. He spoke amid calls for the return of fuel subsidy, which critics argued has led to a hike in the cost of living in the country. However, the minister said a return of the policy could portend danger for the country’s economy and the exchange rate. “Return subsidy, and the sequence is familiar. Weaker revenues invite a sovereign credit downgrade. As the rating agencies themselves have already signalled, and you can read all their reports, that would put at risk the upgrade we have recently earned, including our first from S&P in 14 years,” Oyedele said. “Borrowing becomes costlier, capital leaves, reserves fall, naira weakens. The progress on inflation, which has allowed the central bank to begin lowering interest rates, will be put at risk. Our estimate is that the exchange rate could approach ₦3,000 per dollar within months. And the so-called subsidised petrol will cost at least ₦2,000 per litre. This is well above what Nigerians pay today.” To cushion the impacts of the policy, the minister said the Federal Government has introduced several policies, including a discount window for the product. “We are offering a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for the next 30 days in the first instance with priority for public transporters nationwide. So, it’s not a subsidy, the government is just saying we sell to you at cost,” he said. title: 2027: Sensational reports may deepen voter apathy — Amupitan
body: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe LAGOS — The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has warned online publishers against sensational and unverified election reports, saying fake news and misinformation could erode public confidence in the electoral process and deepen voter apathy ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the warning on Thursday in Lagos while speaking at the 10th Annual Conference of the Guild of Corporate Online Publishers (GOCOP), with the theme, “2027 Elections: Trust, Transparency and Shared Responsibilities.” The INEC chairman, who was represented by the Lagos State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Ayobami Salami, said the media had a critical role to play in protecting the integrity of the electoral process by ensuring that election-related information was verified before publication. A statement issued by Amupitan’s Chief Press Secretary/Media Adviser, Adedayo Oketola, and made available to journalists on Thursday, quoted him as saying that inaccurate reports could have consequences beyond the immediate news cycle. He said unverified allegations of electoral fraud could cause lasting damage to public confidence, even when subsequently corrected or retracted. Amupitan said, “While INEC carries the legal mandate to conduct elections, the wider democratic health of Nigeria and indeed West Africa depends on the information infrastructure maintained by the media, particularly online publishers. “This is where the core concept of shared responsibility becomes operational. We live in an era where the velocity of digital information frequently outpaces the verification of truth. “Across our sub-region, election windows are increasingly targeted by coordinated information warfare, political violence narratives, synthetic media and AI-generated deepfakes designed to inflame ethnic divides or passions and undermine institutional legitimacy.” He warned that fake news, unverified leaks and sensationalised reports could undermine public trust, heighten tension and discourage citizens from participating in elections. “When an unverified claim regarding electoral fraud is published, the damage to public confidence is immediate and enduring; subsequent retractions or fact-checks rarely repair the injury,” he said. The INEC chairman urged online publishers to prioritise accuracy over the pressure to break stories ahead of competitors, particularly during election periods. He also cautioned against clickbait headlines and the publication of unverified election results, allegations of manipulation and purported result sheets. Amupitan urged media organisations to provide adequate context when reporting operational challenges during elections, rather than presenting isolated incidents as evidence of systemic failure. He said responsible election reporting required publishers to verify claims with INEC and other credible sources, particularly when reporting polling-unit results and allegations of electoral malpractice. INEC proposes partnership with GOCOP Amupitan disclosed that the commission was proposing a three-point partnership with GOCOP to strengthen election-related information management. The proposed areas of collaboration, he said, included dedicated digital fact-verification mechanisms, stronger editorial self-regulation against the publication of unverified election results and altered result sheets, as well as a national voter-education partnership. He said the initiative was necessary because online publishers had become “primary storytellers and narrative custodians” of Nigeria’s democracy. Amupitan urged online media organisations to use their platforms to improve citizens’ understanding of the electoral process, including voter education and Permanent Voter Card collection, rather than contributing to distrust and voter disengagement. He said INEC was taking steps to strengthen its systems ahead of the 2027 elections, including the deployment of artificial intelligence for data auditing and cyber defence in partnership with technology companies, including Google and Microsoft. According to him, the commission had “embedded automated AI data-auditing tools and multi-layered firewalls” to protect its databases against cyber intrusions, distributed denial-of-service attacks and unauthorised data injection. He said the measures were intended to build confidence in the 2027 elections through verifiable processes. Voter register rises to 103m The INEC chairman also disclosed that the national register had risen to about 103 million registered voters following the conclusion of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise. He added that nationwide collection of Permanent Voter Cards was scheduled to commence on Thursday. Amupitan reiterated the commission’s commitment to conducting transparent elections and said all stakeholders, including the media, had a shared responsibility to build public confidence in the electoral process. He said the INEC leadership was engaging Resident Electoral Commissioners, Administrative Secretaries, Heads of Department, Electoral Officers and Assistant Electoral Officers to identify operational gaps and implement corrective measures before Election Day. According to him, comprehensive training programmes were also underway for election personnel, focusing on electoral administration, technology handling, conflict mitigation and compliance with relevant electoral laws. The commission, he added, had commenced early procurement and distribution of non-sensitive electoral materials to its 36 state offices and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the early procurement would allow adequate time for batching, inventory auditing and distribution to the 774 Local Government Areas ahead of Election Day. Amupitan further disclosed that INEC had procured and commenced the distribution of new operational pick-up vehicles to its state offices and LGAs to address transportation challenges in difficult terrains, riverine communities and remote border settlements. He said the commission had also introduced a centralised Operational Activity Schedule to monitor material movement, storage security and vehicle deployment in real time across state command centres. Who has power to declare election results? Meanwhile, the Lagos REC, Prof. Ayobami Salami, clarified the constitutional responsibility for declaring election results. Salami explained that the Constitution vested the authority to return an election result in the designated Returning Officer. He stressed that being an INEC official did not automatically confer the constitutional authority to return election results. According to him, even as a Resident Electoral Commissioner, he did not possess the constitutional power to announce or return an election result. He said Returning Officers were appointed by the commission and were constitutionally empowered to return the results of elections assigned to them. Agbakoba challenges presidential candidates on fuel subsidy Earlier, the Conference Chairman, Dr Olisa Agbakoba, SAN, stressed the constitutional right of Nigerians to vote and urged INEC to ensure that the 2027 elections were free, fair and credible. Agbakoba, a former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, also urged presidential candidates to clearly state their positions on the future of fuel subsidy and explain what they would do differently if elected. He questioned the constitutional authority for declaring election results against the backdrop of the increasing circulation of opinion polls, election projections and unofficial results through traditional and digital media. The legal practitioner also questioned whether opinion polls and other electoral projections should be subjected to the same standards of verification and fact-checking expected of other election-related information. The conference brought together online publishers, editors, media professionals, election stakeholders, civil society organisations, academics and other stakeholders to discuss the role of trust, transparency and shared responsibility in strengthening Nigeria’s democratic process ahead of the 2027 elections. title: NLC Issues FG Two-Week Ultimatum On Petrol Price, Minimum Wage
body: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has issued the Federal Government a two-week ultimatum to reduce the price of petrol and begin the renegotiation of the national minimum wage, warning that failure to meet its demands could trigger further action by the labour movement. The ultimatum was contained in a communiqué issued after a joint meeting of the NLC National Executive Council (NEC) and Central Working Committee (CWC) at Labour House, Abuja. In the communiqué signed by its President, Joe Ajaero, the NLC said the deadline would begin on Friday, October 9, 2026. The Congress directed its affiliates and progressive allies to remain on high alert and prepared for what it described as “decisive efforts” against policies it considers detrimental to workers and the wider population. The labour body said the decisions followed discussions on what it described as the worsening economic, political and survival crises confronting workers and Nigerians. “The joint meeting-in-session notes with profound alarm the deepening misery inflicted on the Nigerian working class and the broader masses by the neo-liberal policies of the federal government and its state institutions,” the communiqué said. It added that “inflation continues to soar unabated, the naira remains traumatised, wages have been rendered worthless, and the cost of living has become unbearable.” Minimum Wage On the national minimum wage, the NLC said the value of workers’ earnings had been significantly eroded by the depreciation of the naira and the rising cost of living. “The current national minimum wage has been rendered worthless by the relentless depreciation of the naira and the astronomical rise in the cost of living,” the Congress said. It added that Nigerian workers could no longer afford basic necessities including “food, shelter, healthcare, transportation, and education” on their current wages. The NLC consequently demanded that the Federal Government begin renegotiation of the national minimum wage before the end of October. “The Congress demands a living wage that reflects the true cost of living and the dignity of the Nigerian worker. Any further delay by the federal government remains unacceptable,” it said. Petrol Price The Congress also renewed its demand for an immediate reduction in the price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), commonly known as petrol. “The joint meeting reiterates its call on the federal government to work with relevant agencies to immediately reduce the price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), commonly known as petrol,” the communiqué said. According to the NLC, the high cost of petrol has had a “cascading effect” on transportation, food and other essential goods, worsening the hardship faced by workers and the wider population. It called on the government to reduce the price of petrol nationwide to the level it was when the current national minimum wage was signed into law in 2024. The Congress also demanded that the Federal Government grant tax relief to workers and immediately provide wage awards to cushion the impact of rising living costs. “These measures are the bare minimum required to alleviate the suffering of Nigerian workers and restore a measure of dignity to their lives,” the NLC said. Two-Week Ultimatum The labour body said the government has two weeks from Friday, October 9, to act on its demands. The NLC specifically demanded that the Federal Government: Take measures to reduce the price of petrol nationwide to its 2024 level when the current national minimum wage was signed; Commence the process of renegotiating a new national minimum wage; Implement the Terms of Settlement reached with the Joint Health Sector Unions and Assembly of Healthcare Professionals (JOHESU) on February 5, 2026, alongside other outstanding demands; Implement the demands of the Joint Public Sector Negotiating Council (JPSNC). The Congress warned that failure to meet the demands within the stipulated period would compel it to take further action. “Failure of which the NLC will be compelled to take remedial steps as would be directed by the relevant Organs,” the communiqué said. The NLC also reaffirmed what it described as its “historical responsibility” to resist exploitation and oppression and urged its affiliates and allies to remain prepared to act against what it termed anti-people policies. title: Saskatchewan MLAs racked up $10.9 million in expenses last year
body:
Saskatchewan MLAs collectively spent nearly $11 million in taxpayer dollars during the last fiscal year, with opposition members spending more on average than their government counterparts, according to newly released expense statements.
The report, released annually by the Legislative Assembly Service, details a range of expenses by each member across four spending categories, including phone bills, travel and office-related costs, between April 1, 2025, and March 31, 2026.
When combining totals across all four categories, the average Saskatchewan MLA spent around $179,000.
But spending was not consistent across the board, with Opposition MLAs spending more than government caucus members on average.
During the fiscal year, members of the Opposition NDP spent about $182,000 each, compared with roughly $176,000 among government MLAs.
Meanwhile, government ministers spent slightly less than the average MLA, coming in at about $2,500 below the overall average.
However, these figures do not include out-of-province travel by ministers, which is reported separately twice a year. The latest of these statements covers the period between Oct. 1, 2025, and March 31 of this year and includes a $63,000 trip to India taken by Premier Scott Moe in February.
Gage Haubrich, the Canadian Taxpayers Federation’s prairie director, said MLAs should look for ways to keep their expenses below the average.
“If they’re below the average, they should keep those expenses there. If they’re above the average, they should talk to their colleagues and figure out a way to get under that average to save taxpayers some money,” he told Global News in an interview.
Four of the five MLAs with the highest expenses last fiscal year were members of the opposition.
Cumberland MLA Jordan McPhail topped the list, with expenses totalling about $233,100.
Behind him was Athabasca MLA Leroy Laliberte at $212,700.
Jamie Martens, provincial secretary and MLA for Martensville-Blairmore, came in at third at $211,500. With Saskatoon Fairview’s Vicki Mowat and Saskatoon Meewasin’s Nathaniel Teed holding the fourth and fifth spots with $207,700 and $203,600, respectively.
In a statement to Global News, the opposition party said its MLAs work throughout the province.
Haubrich said the spending figures warrant some context, particularly when comparing government and opposition members.
Ministers typically travel throughout the province for government announcements and other duties, he said, making higher expenses expected in some cases.
“So it warrants a little more of an explanation to say, why are they in the top?” Haubrich said, referring to the top MLA spenders.
At the other end of the list, David Marit, the province’s agriculture minister, held the lowest spot, spending around $134,000 last fiscal year.
Behind him were White City-Qu’appelle’s Brad Crassweller at $139,500 and Moe at $144,600.
The fourth- and fifth-lowest spending spots are held by opposition MLAs Bhajan Brar at $145,300 and Nicole Sarauer at $148,000.
The amount an MLA spends can also depend on where they represent.
MLAs based in Saskatoon and Regina — where all but two city-centre constituencies are currently represented by the NDP — are likely to spend more on office-related costs, while rural MLAs tend to incur higher travel expenses.
Across the four categories, MLAs spent the most on constituency assistant costs, at around $4.3 million, and the least on telecommunications, at $358,000. Travel and living expenses totalled $2.4 million, while constituency services, which include rent and office supplies, totalled $3.8 million.
The Legislative Assembly Service publishes MLA expense statements annually, allowing the public to see how elected officials are spending public dollars.

title: Four killed, 19 injured in Kyiv in Russian attacks throughout day
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said this in a Telegram post.

title: Nigerian Photographer Bolaji Alonge’s Photos Featured in New Fela Kuti ‘Zombie’ Vinyl
body:
Nigerian photographer Bolaji Alonge’s photographs of the New Afrika Shrine in Lagos have been featured in a new limited-edition vinyl release of Fela Kuti’s Zombie.
The edition is a collaboration between American fashion brand Denim Tears and the Fela Kuti Estate, with designer Tremaine Emory reimagining the album’s packaging.
According to Partisan Records , Emory used photographs of the New Afrika Shrine taken by Mr Alonge, along with elements from Nigerian artist Lemi Ghariokwu’s original artwork. The new design was created to connect the album back to Lagos and the Shrine while paying tribute to Mr Ghariokwu’s original work.
The release, limited to 1,000 vinyl copies, is scheduled for 9 October. The records will be available through Dover Street Market in London, Turntable Lab in the United States, and the online stores of Partisan Records and Fela Kuti.
Mr Alonge’s photographs were taken at the New Afrika Shrine, a Lagos venue closely associated with Fela Kuti’s musical legacy.
Fela’s original Afrika Shrine was the Lagos venue where he built his reputation as a musician and political voice. The New Afrika Shrine later became part of the Kuti family’s efforts to preserve and continue that legacy.
For the new Zombie edition, Mr Emory chose photographs from that contemporary Lagos setting and placed them alongside the original album’s visual language.
The result connects two periods of Fela’s history: the era in which Zombie was created and the present-day cultural life surrounding the New Afrika Shrine.
Mr Alonge has spent years documenting Lagos and Nigerian culture through his photography project, Eyes of a Lagos Boy. His work includes images connected to the Kuti family, Afrobeat, and the New Afrika Shrine.
His photographs now form part of the physical packaging of one of Fela’s most recognised albums.
Fela released Zombie in 1976, and the album became one of his best-known works and a major part of his criticism of Nigeria’s military government.
The title track criticised soldiers who blindly followed orders, comparing them to zombies.
The album angered the military government. On February 18, 1977, soldiers attacked Fela’s Kalakuta Republic in Lagos, setting the compound on fire and assaulting people inside. Fela’s mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was thrown from a window during the attack and later died from injuries linked to the incident.
The original Zombie album artwork was designed by Lemi Ghariokwu.
For the new edition, Emory has combined elements of Ghariokwu’s original artwork with Alonge’s photographs of the New Afrika Shrine.
According to Partisan Records , the new packaging was designed to connect the album to Lagos and the Shrine while giving it a new visual identity.
The new edition comes as Fela’s music and legacy continue to attract attention worldwide.
Fela was posthumously inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2026 and received the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award this year. His music and influence have also continued to inspire artists across music, fashion and visual culture.
For Alonge, the new edition adds another chapter to his work documenting Lagos and its cultural history.
His photographs, originally made in Lagos, will now appear on a limited physical edition of an album whose history is deeply connected to the city and to Fela’s political and musical legacy.

title: ‘A complete sham’: European Parliament condemns Russia’s September elections and refuses to recognize its new lower house as legitimate
body: The European Parliament adopted a resolution rejecting the results of Russia’s State Duma elections. It says the vote was a “sham” held in an atmosphere of fear amid Russia’s ongoing invasion of Ukraine. The resolution passed with 482 votes in favor, 41 against, and 39 abstentions. The European Parliament said the elections offered voters no genuine alternative candidates and lacked free media and “credible” observers. It also said all critics of the Russian authorities have been imprisoned, killed, or forced into exile. Members of the European Parliament refused to recognize the newly elected State Duma as Russia’s legitimate legislature and called on EU countries to end official contacts with Russian lawmakers. They also opposed normalizing Russia’s participation in international sporting and cultural events. The resolution calls for “continued” support for Russian democratic forces that openly oppose the war against Ukraine. The lawmakers said EU relations with Russia could return to normal only if Moscow restored Ukraine’s territorial integrity, released prisoners of war, and paid reparations, among other requirements. According to The Insider , those who voted against the resolution included German lawmaker Petr Bystron, who has been accused of ties to Russia; Slovak politician Ľuboš Blaha, who met with Sergei Naryshkin, the head of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service; and Czech lawmaker Ondřej Dostál, who visited Moscow at the invitation of a Russian foundation linked to Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU. title: Former Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, wife face new charges over alleged torture
body:
Prosecutors allege Maduro "presided over this system of repression and torture."
Federal prosecutors in New York on Thursday unsealed new charges against ousted Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro that accuse him of conspiring with his wife to torture individuals who were held in Venezuelan prisons.
The new indictment, unsealed in Manhattan federal court, specifically accused his government of torturing Americans because Maduro "assigned blame to the United States for the instability in Venezuela."
Federal prosecutors alleged Maduro "presided over this system of repression and torture" and his wife, Cilia Flores, is accused of helping him develop it.
"When Maduro became President of Venezuela in or about 2013, he authorized the use of torture against specific individuals and oversaw a system designed to use torture, military detention, and violence as a means of repression against the political opposition," the new indictment alleged.
Maduro was charged by superseding indictment with one count of conspiracy to commit torture and Flores was charged with one count of conspiracy to commit torture and one count of narcoterrorism.
"As alleged in the indictment, the Maduro regime subjected over a dozen American citizens to torture while held in custody of the Venezuelan government -- including drugs, electrocution, sexual assault, and more," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. "They will now answer for their crimes."
While leader of Venezuela, Maduro allegedly conspired to torture one American for no reason other than he could be "useful in a prisoner exchange with the United States," according to the new indictment.
An American citizen identified in the indictment as Victim-8 had been in Venezuela visiting family when "officers attacked Victim-8 from behind, severely injuring Victim-8's back such that Victim-8 required a lengthy hospital stay," the superseding indictment alleged. Venezuelan officers allegedly "electrocuted Victim-8's testicles and put a pressure device on his ankles, causing him to faint several times" during transport from the hospital to prison, according to the indictment.
Once in prison, the torture continued, prosecutors alleged. On one occasion, one of Victim-8's torturers told him the only reason he was alive was because he was a United States citizen and, therefore, "Victim-8 could be useful in a prisoner exchange with the United States," according to the indictment.
In 2024, after Maduro declared victory following what the United States called a sham election, Venezuelan authorities allegedly beat an American citizen identified as Victim-9, according to the indictment, which alleged, "For two days they beat him with their fists to the face, head, and stomach approximately every half an hour. The beatings caused permanent injury to Victim-9's eye."
After about a year in custody, Victim-9 was released on Jan. 15, 2026, two weeks after Maduro's ouster, according to the indictment. Still, Victim-9 and other Americans were warned "they were not allowed to say the Venezuelan government had hurt them or had otherwise subjected them to abuse," the indictment said.
In January 2002, an American citizen identified as Victim-7 was detained in Venezuela on charges alleging participation in a conspiracy to assassinate Maduro. Victim-7 was taken to a concrete house where officials "tortured him over the course of two or three days," the indictment stated. "Among other things, the officers punched him in the face and abdomen, covered his face and poured a noxious liquid over his face that caused him to vomit, which the officer then forced him to eat."
From there, Victim-7 was transferred to Boleita Norte prison where, the indictment alleged, his torture continued and "included electric shock to Victim-7's arms, legs and genitals; asphyxiation; beatings; deprivation of food and water; and forced injections of a substance that caused Victim-7 to experience seizures."
Maduro did not appear in court Thursday. His attorney, Barry J. Pollack, said in a statement that Maduro "denies the charges in the new indictment and looks forward to his day in court."
Flores appeared in court on a related matter and the federal judge presiding over the case denied her pretrial release on bail.
"Jail is not a nice place to be, but these are serious allegations," Judge Alvin Hellerstein said. "I don't think the conditions are there to release her."
Defense attorney Mark Donnelly said Flores needs a medical procedure and cannot recuperate in a jail cell. He proposed placing Flores under house arrest with a private security detail.
"The conditions that the defense proposes address all the risk of flight concerns that the government may have," Donnelly said.
Federal prosecutors opposed her release. They accused Flores of "horrific acts" and said "witnesses who were in the room" would testify about the torture she allegedly conspired with her husband to carry out.
Maduro and his wife will be arraigned on the new charges at a later date.
Both previously pleaded not guilty to narcoterrorism and drug trafficking charges and maintained their innocence during their first court appearance in January, following their capture by U.S. forces in a military operation in the Venezuelan capital of Caracas.
Maduro's lawyer argued in a court filing last month that the former president is immune from prosecution because he was the leader of a sovereign nation.

title: Bail granted for driver in Saskatchewan crash that killed mother and daughters
body:
A truck driver involved in a crash that killed three people, including two girls, in Saskatchewan last week has been granted bail.
Kelly Knopf, a 40-year-old South Carolina resident, appeared in Yorkton court via phone Thursday – almost a week after the fatal crash near Foam Lake, Sask.
RCMP said Knopf was driving a truck when he allegedly smashed into an SUV while trying to pass a semi-truck on a rural road.
Three people in the SUV were killed, including 40-year-old Amber Olsen and her two daughters, eight-year-old Isla and five-year-old Everly. A man who was also in the SUV was taken to hospital in serious condition. The driver of the semi was not injured.
Knopf and two other truck passengers were also taken to hospital. He was charged with dangerous driving causing death and bodily harm.
Knopf’s lawyer, Brian Pfefferle, said the man was on a hunting trip in Saskatchewan when the crash occurred.
Knopf will be able to return to the United States on $20,000 bail, court heard Thursday. Several conditions were attached to his release, including not being to operate a vehicle in Saskatchewan and that he return to Canada to address the charges.
“He is returning to his home in South Carolina to receive treatment for the injuries he sustained in this accident,” Pfefferle said in a statement. “This is a terrible tragedy and Mr. Knopf intends to comply with the conditions and is grateful the Crown agreed to his release.”
His next court appearance is scheduled for Jan. 21.

title: British foreign secretary announces nearly EUR 64 mln winter support package during Ukraine visit
body:
During his first visit to Ukraine in this capacity, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced nearly EUR 64 million in additional winter aid for Ukraine and reaffirmed continued support for Kyiv.
According to the British government, Miliband announced a winter resilience funding package totaling GBP 54 million (EUR 63.73 million). He also noted that today's new sanctions mean that more than 90% of Russia's total oil production capacity is now covered by the UK's sanctions regime.
The government said the UK's new humanitarian and energy funding will help strengthen Ukraine's preparedness for the fifth winter of Russia's full-scale invasion. Upon arriving in Ukraine for his first visit as foreign minister, Ed Miliband, together with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, visited the site of a recent strike in the Chernihiv region that claimed the lives of at least 22 people. There, he also announced new sanctions against Russia and GBP 6 million in funding for the investigation of war crimes.
During his meeting with President Zelenskyy, the foreign minister announced a sweeping package of sanctions against individuals and organizations that help sustain Russia's war.
The package, which targets approximately 40 entities in Russia's financial, oil, and technology sectors, is designed to disrupt Russia's supply chains and cut off its sources of funding.
"£54 million in combined energy and humanitarian funding is expected to support ordinary Ukrainians during the winter months – as Putin once again attempts to weaponize winter and plunge communities into darkness. The UK is backing Ukraine through a triangle of support – bolstering Ukraine's resilience; going after those who help to fund Russia's war machine; and shoring up NATO security and meeting threats to our national security with robust action," the statement reads.
Miliband said "Russia could end this war tomorrow. Instead we've seen escalating attacks, including on key infrastructure and Ukrainian cultural landmarks."
"My message to Putin is clear – You cannot wait us out. Until you choose the path of peace, the UK will not relent in its support for Ukraine, our values, or our national security. You will remain a pariah," he said.
Government officials said the United Kingdom has supported more than one million vulnerable civilians by providing much-needed generators and assistance in restoring damaged water and heating systems.
It is noted that the UK's current contribution includes GBP 20 million to support Ukraine's energy security: funding for teams carrying out emergency repairs to the power grid following attacks, investments in backup generators and solar energy sources for periods of outages, as well as investments in new technologies to diversify energy supplies.
The package also includes GBP 34 million to protect and support heating and water supply for Ukrainian families ahead of winter and to provide direct cash assistance in cooperation with the Ukrainian government and local partners, including UNICEF, UNHCR, and the Ukrainian Red Cross.
After his visit to Chernihiv, the Foreign Secretary returned to Kyiv and visited a hospital where Ukrainian veterans were receiving medical care. There, he announced GBP 6.3 million in support from the United Kingdom for Ukraine's domestic efforts to hold those responsible for the horrific war crimes committed during Russia's full-scale invasion accountable.
To date, the United Kingdom has provided over GBP 1 billion pounds in humanitarian and energy support to Ukraine since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion.

title: Customs seize three live pangolins in suspected wildlife-trafficking operation in Ogun
body:
The Nigeria Customs Service has intercepted three live pangolins allegedly being smuggled through Ogun State, in the latest seizure highlighting the illegal trade of one of the world’s most trafficked mammals.
The endangered animals were intercepted by officers of the Ogun I Area Command, Idiroko, at Abeokuta waterside following credible intelligence, according to the command.
It stated that the animals were found confined in wire-mesh cages and concealed inside sacks in what Customs described as an attempt to evade detection. It added that the suspected traffickers fled after sighting the Customs patrol team.
The spokesperson for the command, Chado Zakari, said the manner in which the animals were concealed showed the cruelty associated with the illegal wildlife trade.
“The pangolins were found tightly bound in sacks, a cruel method of concealment used by wildlife traffickers to evade detection,” Mr Zakari said.
He said the packaging also suggested that the seizure may be connected to an organised wildlife-trafficking operation.
“Upon inspection, officers discovered three pangolins confined in wire mesh cages and concealed within a sack. The sophisticated packaging suggests the involvement of an organised smuggling syndicate,” he said.
Following the interception, the Acting Customs Area Controller of Ogun I Command, Abdulhamid Ibrahim, handed the three pangolins over to Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation for rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected habitat.
Mr Ibrahim said the seizure demonstrated the command’s commitment to combating wildlife trafficking alongside its conventional anti-smuggling operations.
He, however, warned people involved in the illegal wildlife trade to desist.
“Trafficking pangolins and their derivatives attracts severe penalties. Under the recently passed Endangered Species Conservation and Protection Bill, offenders risk fines of up to A12 million and prison terms of up to 10 years.
“The Nigeria Customs Service, in collaboration with Green Finger Wildlife and other stakeholders, remains resolute in enforcing these laws to protect the nation’s biodiversity,” Mr Ibrahim said.
He commended the officers involved in the operation and said the command would continue working with conservation organisations to tackle the illegal wildlife trade.
Receiving the animals, the Administrative Manager/Supervisor of Green Fingers Wildlife Conservation, Isaac Ime, commended the Customs command for intercepting the animals.
Mr Ime assured that the organisation would provide the necessary care for the rescued pangolins and work towards their rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected environment.
The seizure comes amid growing concern over Nigeria’s role in the international trafficking of pangolin products.
Researchers have identified Nigeria as a major transit hub for pangolin trafficking, with Nigerian-linked seizures involving hundreds of thousands of kilogrammes of pangolin scales over the years.
Pangolins are not animals that individuals can simply capture from the wild and keep as pets or for commercial purposes in Nigeria.
The Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act places pangolin species listed in its schedules under legal protection. The law prohibits the hunting, capture and trade of species listed in its First Schedule.
Also, NESREA said its enforcement covers the possession and display of endangered wildlife specimens and products.
NESREA specifically warned in March 2026 that individuals cannot possess, display or trade endangered wildlife specimens on social media, listing pangolins among the species affected by the prohibition.
The agency said the restrictions are based on Nigeria’s environmental laws and its obligations under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).
In CITES Appendix I, Pangolins were given the highest level of protection against international commercial trade. WhileNigeria’s existing wildlife legislation separately prohibits the hunting, capture or trade of pangolins listed under the Endangered Species Act.
In March, the Federal High Court in Lagos jailed two men after pleading guilty to charges involving the unlawful possession and trade of three live pangolins.

title: Stefanchuk, German Ambassador Ruge discuss Ukraine's fulfilment of international obligations
body:
Verkhovna Rada Chairman Ruslan Stefanchuk and the newly appointed German Ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, discussed Ukraine's fulfillment of its international obligations.
"We also discussed Ukraine's reform agenda and the fulfillment of its international obligations. The Verkhovna Rada is working on legislative measures necessary to further strengthen the state and attract international support. In particular, this concerns draft laws on which access to the next financial aid package, amounting to approximately 20 billion, depends," Stefanchuk said on Facebook after meeting with the ambassador on Thursday.
According to Stefanchuk, Ukraine is committed to reforms, but
"for us, it is not only the number of laws passed that matters, but above all their quality, their compliance with the Constitution, and their consideration of the realities of martial law."
He said that Germany is one of Ukraine's key partners, whose consistent support is of particular importance to the country amid a full-scale war.
Stefanchuk said that everyone understands the domestic political context in Germany, where the issue of supporting Ukraine remains the subject of active debate.
"Therefore, it is important that our cooperation be based on concrete results, mutual trust, and a clear understanding of shared priorities. I am convinced that the Ukrainian-German partnership will continue to strengthen, particularly at the parliamentary level," he said.

title: Thailand’s Queen Suthida takes controls of single-seat Gripen fighter for first solo flight
body: The report identifies her as the first reigning queen to pilot a fighter jet solo. King Maha Vajiralongkorn, also known as Rama X, watched the flight from the ground. After she landed, the king presented her with flowers and pinned on her a Gripen Order Golden Patch badge embroidered with gold thread. The aircraft carried special tail artwork marking 15 years of Gripen service in Thailand in 2026. Preparation for the flight The queen’s training followed Royal Thai Air Force standards and included preparatory flights in the Pilatus PC-9 turboprop and L-39 Albatros jet trainer. She also trained in a Gripen simulator and flew 10 hours with an instructor in the two-seat JAS-39D. Photo: Royal Thai Air Force. Queen Suthida has logged more than 1,188 flying hours across various aircraft types. She holds qualifications for several light and commercial aircraft, including the Boeing 737-400 and 737-800. She has repeatedly served as co-pilot on those airliners during state visits. The Gripen flight added a solo fighter sortie to that experience. Thailand purchased 12 Gripen C/D fighters from Sweden. The aircraft were used in combat during the border conflict with Cambodia in July and December 2025.

title: Fuel subsidy return could push petrol to ₦2,000/litre — Oyedele
body: …Says FX could weaken to ₦3,000/$1 By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to fuel subsidy could push the price of petrol to about ₦2,000 per litre and weaken the naira to as much as ₦3,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning while briefing journalists on the ongoing debate over fuel subsidy in Abuja on Thursday. He said the reintroduction of subsidy could reduce government revenue and place additional pressure on the country’s finances and foreign exchange market. According to the minister, weaker government revenue could affect the country’s credit rating, increase borrowing costs and contribute to capital outflows. He said the resulting pressure could also reduce foreign exchange reserves and weaken the naira. Oyedele said, “Return subsidy and the sequence is familiar. Weaker revenue invites a sovereign credit downgrade, as the rating agencies have already signalled. “That would put at risk the upgrades we have recently earned, including our first from S&P in fourteen years. Borrowing becomes costlier. Capital leaves. Reserves fall. The naira weakens. “The progress on inflation, which has allowed the Central Bank to begin lowering interest rates, would be put at risk. “Our estimate is that the exchange rate could approach ₦3,000 to the dollar within months, and so-called subsidised petrol would cost at least ₦2,000 a litre. That is well above what Nigerians pay today.” The minister maintained that returning to a fuel subsidy regime was not an option, arguing that the government’s priority should be to strengthen revenue, stabilise the economy and protect recent gains. Oyedele’s projections were presented as an estimate of the possible economic consequences of a return to fuel subsidy, rather than as a certainty. The post Fuel subsidy return could push petrol to ₦2,000/litre — Oyedele appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Zelensky Visits Pryluky With UK’s Miliband, Thanks EU for €1.2B Tranche for Drones
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to Pryluky with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to honor the victims after a Russian barrage – coinciding with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 74th birthday – left 22 civilians dead, including five children.
In a series of statements issued on Thursday, Oct. 8, Zelensky condemned Wednesday’s strikes and confirmed that the strike on the apartment building left 54 people injured. During the visit, the two leaders met with residents who survived the attack and were briefed on the scale of the destruction.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We must support our people,” Zelensky said, pointing to a veteran who lived in the apartment building destroyed by Russia.
“When partners are literally standing alongside Ukrainians, it truly matters,” he continued, thanking Miliband for standing beside him in Pryluky and alluding to Western partners who continue supplying Kyiv with funding and air defense it needs to protect itself against Russia’s aggression.
The damage extends far beyond the destroyed building. According to Zelensky, more than 100 residential buildings across Pryluky were damaged, along with schools, kindergartens, shops, businesses and other critical infrastructure the city depends on.
Residents who spoke with the president described a shortage of both shelters and housing. In response, Zelensky ordered the head of the Chernihiv Regional Military Administration to quickly help those who have nowhere to live, adding that temporary assistance should eventually be followed by permanent solutions.
“It is also important that the victims ultimately receive new housing,” he said.
Those whose homes were in the destroyed building should be allowed back into their apartments once the security situation permits, Zelensky said, placing the head of the State Emergency Service (SES) in charge of the process.
Ukrainian authorities consistently remind their partners that the war is not a distant fact on paper, but a reality measured in human lives and relentless terror.
This became particularly visible in the last few weeks, as Russia increased its strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure following the departure of senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner from Moscow.
The two visited Moscow on Sept. 5 to hold talks with Russian diplomats and Putin himself, aiming to broker an end to the war. For the first time ever during their tenure, the envoys also visited Kyiv just a day after.
Despite all three sides describing the negotiations as positive and productive, Russian barrage amplified.
The latest attack on Pryluky left 17 civilians hospitalized, including a five-year-old girl. It also highlighted gaps in the city’s protection.
After the health minister briefed him on efforts to build shelters in medical facilities, Zelensky ordered officials to speed up the work and secure additional funding. The hospital’s own shelter must be repaired as a priority, he said, while a new, modern one is built in its place.
Together with city authorities, the health minister and the head of the Chernihiv Regional Military Administration will be responsible for the project, Zelensky said .
He also tasked the interior ministers with inspecting every shelter in the city.
The Pryluky attack was the deadliest in a broader Russian assault launched on Wednesday, Oct. 7.
A Kh-101 cruise missile was used to strike the five-story apartment block as Russia targeted cities across Ukraine with ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as Shahed drones, before continuing with aerial bombs during the day.
As rescuers continued recovering bodies, the toll from Russia’s latest attacks kept rising. By Thursday, Zelensky said strikes on Pryluky, Kramatorsk, Kyiv and other cities had killed 78 people and injured 215 in recent days alone.
He described the attacks as a severe escalation and “terror directed against people and life,” warning that world leaders must not ignore what is happening.
The same concerns were raised during a telephone call with European Council President António Costa later on Thursday.
Zelensky also thanked Costa for the €1.2 billion (l $1.4 billion) tranche that arrived in Ukraine on Wednesday, saying the money would go toward defense, primarily drones.
“This will provide tremendous support,” Zelensky said.
Beyond immediate military needs, the two leaders discussed the timeline for opening the next clusters in Ukraine’s EU accession talks , a winter energy package and further financial assistance . The call came ahead of the EC summit in Brussels, scheduled for Oct. 15-16.
Between Zelensky and Costa, an agreement was reached to meet in a trilateral format with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
Zelensky also briefed the EC President on meetings with US officials planned for the coming days , particularly Oct. 9-10, noting that a Ukrainian delegation is already on its way.

title: Russian billionaire Mikhail Gutseriev spent years fighting EU sanctions over Belarus. He finally won (but remains sanctioned over Russia’s war in Ukraine).
body: EU ambassadors removed Russian billionaire Mikhail Gutseriev from the bloc’s Belarus sanctions list on October 7, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported . The EU imposed the sanctions on Gutseriev in June 2021. The Council of the EU cited his close ties to Alexander Lukashenko, alleging that he financially supported Lukashenko’s regime and benefited from it. The council pointed to his investments in the construction of the Nezhinsky mining and processing plant and his attendance at Lukashenko’s 2020 inauguration. Gutseriev spent several years challenging the sanctions in European courts. In May 2026, he won a ruling annulling the Council of the EU’s latest decision to renew them. The court found that the council had not presented enough up-to-date evidence that he still had ties to Lukashenko’s regime. Removal from the Belarus list does not mean all sanctions against Gutseriev have been lifted. He remains subject to EU sanctions over Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. In 2024, the Czech publications Denik N and Respekt reported that Gutseriev had offered to share information about Vladimir Putin’s and Lukashenko’s plans with Western intelligence services in exchange for having sanctions lifted. To that end, he met twice with representatives of the FBI and Czech police in Prague in 2022. In September, the EU lifted sanctions against two Russian billionaires: USM Holdings founder Alisher Usmanov and Alfa Group co-founder Mikhail Fridman. Both were placed on sanctions lists after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. EU authorities considered both billionaires part of Putin’s inner circle. France and Slovakia pushed to lift sanctions against Usmanov, while Luxembourg advocated for Fridman. The effort to lift Usmanov’s sanctions was intended to advance talks with Azerbaijan on the release of prisoners. Luxembourg’s support for Fridman has been linked to his lawsuit over frozen assets — he is seeking $16 billion from the country’s authorities. title: Russian stock market closes in decline
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. The MOEX Index fell by 1.07% to 2,312.35 points at the close of Thursday’s main trading session, while the dollar-denominated RTS Index declined 1% to 852.8 points. The yuan exchange rate fell by 7.1 kopecks to 12.679 rubles.
"A wave of profit-taking swept through the stock market today. Investors reacted to the latest inflation data and the strengthening of the ruble. The rise in oil prices helped limit the decline," Andrey Smirnov, a stock market expert at BCS World of Investments, said.
"Shares of Samolet Group (+1.6%) were the top gainers in today’s declining stock market, probably following statements by Sberbank executives that the bank is working with the company to improve its financial performance," Natalia Milchakova, lead analyst at Freedom Global, said.
According to her, Mechel common shares (-3.7%) were the biggest losers, likely due to forecasts of weak Russian steel export performance in 2026.
BCS World of Investments expects the MOEX Index to trade in a range of 2,270-2,350 points on Friday. The yuan exchange rate could range from 12.6 to 12.8 rubles, while the dollar could trade at 84-86 rubles.
Freedom Global expects the MOEX Index to trade in a range of 2,300-2,400 points on Friday. Its forecasts for the dollar, euro, and yuan exchange rates are 84-86 rubles, 94-96 rubles, and 12.5-12.9 rubles, respectively.

title: Rev. Kwadwo Bempah defies restriction on preaching on buses; warns it won’t succeed
body: The Head Pastor of Holy Hill Chapel of the Assemblies of God, Reverend Dr Kwadwo Boateng Bempah, has vowed the church will keep preaching wherever people gather, despite the law restricting preaching and hawking in moving public vehicles. He said attempts to restrict preaching on buses will not succeed, insisting the church cannot be silenced in its duty to spread the gospel. “So today I send the message. Who is behind that? The church is too quiet. People are secretly planning, planning, planning. I don’t know who they are, but I’m talking to them. But you will not succeed. Oh, what you are trying to do, you will not succeed. You will not succeed. “Wherever human beings gather, we will preach. Wherever human beings gather, the word must go forth… Even at the back of Okada we will be shouting the name Jesus,” Rev. Bempah said in a message delivered to his congregation and widely circulated on social media. Rev. Bempah described the restriction as an attempt to “gag the church” and questioned why preaching on buses should be prohibited when other forms of public activity continue. Read Also: Explainer: Why preaching in moving tro-tros could mean eight months in jail “Now they say we shouldn’t preach in the bus as if they bought a bus for somebody… When my bus is going, come and tell me,” he said. He further urged Christians not to remain silent in the face of what he described as efforts to limit the church’s evangelism. “Never please people to displease God,” he said, adding that the church must remain vocal in spreading Christianity. His comments follow the coming into force of the amended Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519), which prohibit preaching and hawking on public service vehicles while they are in motion. Under the regulations, a person found preaching in a moving public or commercial vehicle may face a fine of between 10 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both. The law has been in existence since 2012, but was not enforced until the recent amendment, which now increases the prison sentence from three to eight months.

title: Russia would respond with all available weapons to Gulf of Finland blockade — expert
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Russia would be forced to use all available weapons in the event of a blockade of the Gulf of Finland, head of the Center for the Study of Military and Political Conflicts Andrey Klintsevich told TASS.
"They are counting on NATO being able to rapidly deploy its first echelon of forces there, let’s say, to close the border. But I think these are just words for now, because Russia would react very aggressively to such a blockade. And we would be prepared to use all available weapons, including tactical nuclear weapons, as we have recently warned," the expert said.
He noted that Baltic politicians do not fully understand the potential consequences of such statements. "Baltic politicians do not fully grasp these risks when making such statements. Even the Americans, with their entirely different level of military capabilities and strategic nuclear forces, do not allow themselves to make such statements," he explained.
Earlier, Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told The Times that NATO could deploy a force of 50,000 experienced troops within hours and close off the Baltic Sea.

title: Two arrested inside US airbase in UK as counter-terror police investigate
body: Two men have been arrested after being found inside an RAF base used by the US military in the UK. The Metropolitan Police said two Latvian men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested in the early hours of Thursday by Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) on suspicion of trespassing inside the base perimeter at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire, 100km north of London. RAF Molesworth is home to US intelligence-operation centres for Europe and Africa, as well as a Nato intelligence hub, according to the CIA's website. It is the second airbase used by the US in Britain to be subject to a security alert in the past two weeks. The US pulled all its strategic bombers out of the UK over concerns at RAF Fairford after an incident. Both men remain in police custody and an investigation is being carried out by counter-terrorism police. At this stage, the incident is not being linked to the several arrests that were made in connection to RAF Fairford. The pair were detained at RAF Molesworth after an MDP patrol near the perimeter spotted an abandoned vehicle. Police officers attended and carried out further searches around the site. A small breach of the perimeter fence was identified, leading to the two men being found and arrested. They were initially arrested on suspicion of trespassing on a prohibited site and criminal damage, and were taken to a Cambridgeshire police station. The pair have since been arrested again on suspicion of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK under the National Security Act 2023 “We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week,” said Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, which is leading the investigation. “Our investigation into this incident is at its very early stages. A big part of this is looking at any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site, but I must stress we are keeping an open mind at this stage and enquiries are very much ongoing.” Officers are carrying out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area, about 30km from the RAF base, in connection with the investigation. The abandoned vehicle was recovered by police and is undergoing further searches. Concerns over the vehicle led to the deployment of specialist ordnance disposal officers to carry out additional checks. As a precaution, a cordon was put in place but was lifted after nothing of concern was found. On Tuesday, a British citizen, 22, was arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with the incident close to RAF Fairford, counter-terrorism police said. Five men, aged 23 to 25, had already been arrested on September 27 near the base on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an “investigative decision” that was “grounded in experience and strategy”. A sixth man, a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British citizen, was arrested on October 1 in Westminster, central London and was later released on bail.

title: Big tech can’t ‘tell us what to do,’ Carney says on Musk’s separatism talk
body:
Canadians will decide the future of Canada, not “large tech firms that think they can tell us what to do,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday, responding to Elon Musk’s comments that three Canadian provinces “should separate” from Canada.
“The future of Canada will be decided by Canadians, and the priorities of Canadians, the priorities of the people of Quebec,” Carney told reporters in Sherbrooke, Que., on Thursday.
Musk, a former adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump, said on his social media platform X that Quebec should separate, as should Alberta and Saskatchewan .
Any discussion on the future of the provinces should be “free from interference from foreign governments and large tech firms that think they can tell us what to do,” Carney said on Thursday.
Carney recently announced a major $2.3-billion contract with Telesat for low-Earth orbit satellite connectivity for the military.
That service has aspirations to become a direct commercial challenger to Musk’s Starlink, which dominates the global market for low-Earth orbit satellite internet service.
Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too.
Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe had a concise response to Musk on social media: “No.”
On Oct. 19, Albertans go to the polls to decide if the province should stay in Canada or whether there should be a second binding referendum to begin the process of separation.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, who states she’s voting to stay in Canada in an upcoming referendum, says she also strongly disagrees with Musk’s opinion.
Speaking in Edmonton on Thursday, Smith argued separatist sentiment in her province has weakened because she and Carney have addressed the “very real issues that were frustrating Albertans.”
“The federal government has changed. Their approach to us has changed and they’re willing to work together on addressing those issues,” she said.
Quebec voters elected a separatist government on Monday by granting the Parti Québécois a minority government.
PQ Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon pledged during the election that his party would not hold a referendum on separation while U.S. President Donald Trump remains in office.
Carney has sought to use his ambitious economic agenda as an olive branch to the province and its new government, vowing Quebec will benefit from cooperative federalism.

title: French Embassy to partner Kobby Kyei Media for bloggers’ training
body: The French Embassy in Ghana is set to partner with Kobby Kyei Media for a one-day training programme for bloggers, content creators and online journalists. Kobby Kyei, founder of Kobby Kyei Media, announced the initiative on his social media platforms, describing it as an opportunity to create a platform where young bloggers and content creators can learn, connect and grow. The training is scheduled for Thursday, 29 October 2026, at the French Ambassador’s Residence in Accra, where participants will gather for a full day of learning, practical sessions, discussions and networking. The main training session will run from 9:00am to 5:00pm, followed by a cocktail reception from 6:00pm to 8:00pm at the French Ambassador’s Residence. The reception will provide participants and invited guests with an opportunity to network, engage and explore potential collaborations beyond the formal training sessions. The programme is expected to focus on digital storytelling, content creation, responsible online journalism and the professional development of digital creators. According to Kobby Kyei, the initiative is driven by his long-standing desire to create a platform where young bloggers and content creators can gain practical knowledge, connect with industry professionals and build sustainable careers in the digital space. Building a stronger digital media community The partnership comes at a time when social media has become an increasingly influential part of Ghana’s media and communication ecosystem. Bloggers, influencers, online journalists and content creators now play a significant role in shaping conversations, breaking stories, promoting businesses and telling stories that may otherwise receive limited attention. However, the rapid growth of the digital space has also created the need for greater professionalism, responsible storytelling and continuous skills development. The 29 October programme at the French Ambassador’s Residence in Accra is expected to address some of these areas by providing participants with practical insights that can help them improve the quality of their work and better understand the responsibilities that come with having a digital audience. Issues surrounding responsible content creation, misinformation, digital storytelling, personal branding, audience engagement, artificial intelligence and digital entrepreneurship are expected to form part of the broader conversations around the programme. Kobby Kyei’s vision for creators For Kobby Kyei, the initiative goes beyond simply organising another training programme. His vision is to help create an environment where young creators can see digital media as more than just a platform for entertainment or chasing trends. Through Kobby Kyei Media, he has consistently used digital platforms to highlight social issues, support communities and tell human interest stories, while also building his own brand within Ghana’s digital media ecosystem. The training therefore represents another step towards creating opportunities for creators to develop the knowledge and professional networks needed to make a meaningful impact. French Embassy and Kobby Kyei Media partnership The collaboration also builds on the relationship between Kobby Kyei and the French Embassy in Ghana. In May 2026, Kobby Kyei was invited to the Africa Forward Summit 2026 in Nairobi, Kenya, where conversations focused on Africa’s future, innovation, technology, development and strengthening partnerships between Africa and France. The upcoming training further demonstrates the potential for collaboration between diplomatic missions and Ghana’s growing creative and digital community. A day of learning and networking The programme will take place at the French Ambassador’s Residence in Accra on 29 October 2026. The training will run from 9:00am to 5:00pm, giving participants a full day of learning, discussions and practical engagement. This will be followed by a cocktail reception from 6:00pm to 8:00pm, also at the French Ambassador’s Residence, allowing creators, industry stakeholders and invited guests to network, exchange ideas and explore possible collaborations. The event is expected to bring together bloggers, online journalists, social media creators and other players within Ghana’s digital ecosystem. Kobby Kyei says further details regarding registration, participation and the programme line-up will be announced in due course. The 29 October gathering at the French Ambassador’s Residence in Accra is expected to provide a platform for Ghana’s digital creators to learn, connect, collaborate and grow, while promoting a more responsible and professional digital media culture.

title: Return Of Subsidy Could Lead To ₦2,000/Litre Petrol, ₦3,000/$ Exchange Rate — FG
body: The Federal Government has again defended removing the fuel subsidy, saying the essential commodity would have cost at least ₦2,000 per litre. The Minister of Finance and the Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Tawio Oyedele, said this on Thursday during a press briefing on fuel prices and questions about the subsidy. “Return subsidy, and the sequence is familiar. Weaker revenues invite a sovereign credit downgrade. As the rating agencies themselves have already signalled, and you can read all their reports, that would put at risk the upgrade we have recently earned, including our first from S&P in 14 years,” Oyedele said at the event in Abuja. “Borrowing becomes costlier, capital leaves, reserves fall, naira weakens. The progress on inflation, which has allowed the central bank to begin lowering interest rates, will be put at risk. Our estimate is that the exchange rate could approach ₦3,000 per dollar within months. And the so-called subsidised petrol will cost at least ₦2,000 per litre. This is well above what Nigerians pay today.” He argued that if subsidy is returned, Nigerians would pay the price “in inflation and in a collapsing currency”. “However, it is described, a subsidy must be financed through salaries and pensions not paid on time, through higher taxes, or through the printing of money, like we saw before this current administration. Over 30 trillion naira was printed. That’s inflation we’re dealing with. It wasn’t even just about the reform. Each of these has done great harm before,” the minister said. “Short-term relief, but with long-term fragility, is the most expensive money a government can spend.” There have been calls for the return of fuel subsidy more than three years after the President Bola Tinubu administration announced an end to the policy. But Oyedele has questioned proponents of fuel subsidy return. “We remain open to ideas, but any credible proposer should answer three questions. Number one, what will it cost? Number two, how will it be funded sustainably? Number three, what pump price will it deliver? We will engage in good faith with any proposer that shows its arithmetic,” he said. title: Siberian governor announces ‘all-clear’ following death of Russian plague research institute employee
body: Authorities in Russia’s Irkutsk region have completed a “series of preventive measures” after the death of Darya Shipilova, an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, Governor Igor Kobzev said. She had community-acquired pneumonia, he said. Kobzev said Shipilova had been vaccinated and “had immunity to the dangerous infections involved in her work.” He said authorities had found no “accidents while handling pathogenic microorganisms” at the institute. Specialists also finished monitoring everyone who had been in contact with Shipilova and found no health problems. Kobzev said: The public health situation in Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable. […] Amid media pressure, specialists carefully investigated the situation. It was a test, but we handled it well. Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s public health watchdog, said there were no risks to public health in the Irkutsk region and that the public health situation there was “stable.” Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee of an anti-plague research institute, died overnight on October 2 in Shelekhov, a satellite city of Irkutsk. Authorities later isolated about 200 people who had been in contact with her. The news outlet Lyudi Baikala reported that several hospitals in Irkutsk had been closed and placed under quarantine. Reports began circulating in the media and on social media that Shipilova had died of pneumonic plague after contracting it at her research institute. Rospotrebnadzor said in an official statement that she had died of “pneumonia of unknown cause.” Further reading Plague may have resurfaced in Russia. But this isn’t the Black Death. A 28-year-old plague researcher died in Russia. Authorities have imposed a quarantine but deny any threat of plague, and locals are struggling to make sense of it. body:
