title: NLC draws battle line with FG, gives 14-day ultimatum on petrol, wages
body: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has given the Federal Government a two-week ultimatum to take urgent measures to reduce the price of petrol and commence the renegotiation of the national minimum wage, warning that failure to meet its demands could trigger further action by the labour movement. The ultimatum was contained in a communiqué issued after a joint meeting of the NLC National Executive Council, NEC, and Central Working Committee, CWC, held at Labour House, Abuja. NLC in a communique by its President, Joe Ajaero said the deadline would begin on Friday, October 9, and called on its affiliates and progressive allies to remain on high alert and prepared for what it described as “decisive efforts” against policies it considers detrimental to workers and the wider population. According to the Communique “Having extensively discussed the grave economic, political, and crises of survival ravaging workers and the nation at large, NEC-in-session, in conjunction with the CWC, resolves as follows: “The joint meeting-in-session notes with profound alarm the deepening misery inflicted on the Nigerian working class and the broader masses by the neo-liberal policies of the federal government and its state institutions. Inflation continues to soar unabated, the naira remains traumatised, wages have been rendered worthless, and the cost of living has become unbearable. “The ruling elite, acting as enforcers of global monopoly capital, have demonstrated a worrying indifference to the suffering of the people, choosing instead to transfer the burden of their fiscal negligence onto the already impoverished working masses thus abandoned the people to the dictates of comprador fat cats. “NEC-in-session declares that no society can sustainably develop under a regime of corporate plunder and neo-liberal enslavement. The Nigerian working people must therefore remain resolute, organised, and uncompromising in the collective struggle for a fair and equitable Nigeria. Minimum wage “The joint meeting observes with grave concern that the current national minimum wage has been rendered worthless by the relentless depreciation of the naira and the astronomical rise in the cost of living. Nigerian workers can no longer afford the basic necessities of life; food, shelter, healthcare, transportation, and education; on their current wages. “Consequently, NEC-in-session demands that the federal government commences the renegotiation of the national minimum wage before the end of this month. The Congress demands a living wage that reflects the true cost of living and the dignity of the Nigerian worker. Any further delay by the federal government remains unacceptable. Petrol price “The joint meeting reiterates its call on the federal government to work with relevant agencies to immediately reduce the price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), commonly known as petrol. The exorbitant pump price of petrol has had a cascading effect on the cost of transportation, food, and other essential goods, further deepening the hardship of workers and the masses. The government must abandon its insensitive policies that have allowed for indiscriminate hikes in the price of petroleum products which has only served to enrich a handful of oil marketers while pauperising the masses. Tax relief “The joint meeting demands that the federal government grant tax relief to workers as agreed and immediately provide Wage Awards to workers to cushion the impact of the rising cost of living. These measures are the bare minimum required to alleviate the suffering of Nigerian workers and restore a measure of dignity to their lives. The government cannot continue to demand sacrifice from workers while not offering any relief to the suffering masses and workers. Resolution “The joint meeting issues a two-week ultimatum to the federal government, beginning from Friday, the 9th day of October, 2026 within which it is expected to, among other things: “Take measures to reduce the price of petrol across the nation to what it was at the signing of the current national minimum wage in 2024 to cushion the impact of the energy crisis on workers and masses as being done by other nations of the world; “Commence the process of renegotiating a new national minimum wage; “Implement the dictates of the Terms of Settlement reached with Joint Health Sector Unions & Assembly of Healthcare Professionals (JOHESU) on the 5th day of February, 2026, and other new demands that have arisen since then. “Implement the demands of the Joint Public Sector Negotiating Council (JPSNC). Failure of which the NLC will be compelled to take remedial steps as would be directed by the relevant Organs. “NEC-in-session reaffirms the historical responsibility of the NLC to resist all forms of exploitation and oppression. It calls on all affiliates, and progressive allies to remain on high alert and fully prepared to engage in decisive efforts against all anti-people policies. The Congress reiterates that the Nigerian working people must remain resolute, organised, and uncompromising in the collective struggle for a fair and equitable Nigeria. The post NLC draws battle line with FG, gives 14-day ultimatum on petrol, wages appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: U.S. won’t resume strikes on Iran before midterms, Trump says
body:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that he will not order a resumption of military strikes on Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections in the United States.
Trump, while stumping for Republicans this week, has hinted that was confident that at endgame to the war cold come in the days before or after the election, while also hinting that he remained open to resuming full-scale military operations against Iran.
For weeks, Trump has been threatening that a post-midterm election escalation in the seven-month-old war remains a viable option, despite his initial promises to Americans of a military campaign that would last a matter of weeks.
But Trump in a social media post on Thursday said the U.S. “will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.”
Trump added that his team has been “having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran.”
Negotiations had appeared at a standstill since Trump late last month publicly rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. met certain conditions.
Iran, however, said last week they had received a U.S. counterproposal. And Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday said he expected Tehran would offer a formal reply within days.
Trump’s post comes as the military has dispatched more resources to the region. U.S. officials have said a third aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, and thousands of troops aboard it and accompanying ships could arrive as early as the end of October.
Trump’s announcement was made the same day the USS Abraham Lincoln was due to arrive to its home port in San Diego after a record-long deployment in support of the Iran war. There have been reports of crew stress and poor mental health, as well as supply shortages, including food and hygiene products.
The USS George Washington, which is usually based in Asia, relieved the Lincoln in August. The other aircraft carrier in the Middle East, the USS George H.W. Bush, has been deployed for about six months, but it pulled into Phuket, Thailand, for a port visit several days ago.

title: Ceferin to run for another term as UEFA president
body:
GENEVA, October 8. /TASS/. Slovenian Aleksander Ceferin has decided to run for another term as president of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), the organization’s press service said.
The election will be held at the UEFA Congress in Astana on April 22, 2027.
Ceferin, 58, has headed UEFA since September 2016. He has been re-elected to the position twice.

title: NYSC abduction: Alli seeks stronger security coordination
body: By Adeola Badru The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli, has called for intensified intelligence gathering and stronger collaboration among security agencies following the rescue of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted in Imo State. Alli, in a statement issued on Wednesday by the Director of Media and Publicity of his campaign organisation, Bisi Oladele, described the safe release of the prospective corps members as a welcome development, but called for sustained security measures to prevent similar incidents. The 20 prospective corps members from Oyo State were abducted last week in Imo State while travelling to the state for the mandatory national service. Reacting to their rescue, Alli commended the Federal Government, Imo State Government and security agencies for the efforts that led to the release of the victims. He urged security agencies to strengthen intelligence networks and inter-agency coordination to prevent similar incidents and ensure the safety of Nigerians travelling across the country. Alli said, “The safe rescue of our prospective corps members is a welcome development and a demonstration of the commitment of the Federal Government and our security agencies to protecting the lives of Nigerians. “I commend President Bola Tinubu and the Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for their leadership and the security agencies for their courage, professionalism and coordinated efforts that led to the successful rescue of the victims, who were travelling to Imo for the mandatory national service.” The APC candidate said the rescue should be followed by sustained efforts to address security challenges affecting Nigerians travelling across the country. “The security agencies must intensify intelligence gathering and inter-agency collaboration to prevent similar incidents,” he said. Alli also urged the relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the abduction and take appropriate legal action against anyone found responsible. He appealed to Nigerians to support security agencies by providing useful and timely information that could assist in preventing criminal activities and protecting lives. According to him, “I also urge Nigerians to support security agencies with useful information, stressing that the safety of citizens remains a collective responsibility.” Alli said the protection of citizens required the combined efforts of government, security agencies and members of the public, particularly through the sharing of information that could help security personnel prevent attacks and respond promptly to emerging threats. He also commended the efforts that resulted in the safe recovery of the 20 prospective corps members, describing their release as a source of relief to their families and loved ones. Alli wished the rescued prospective corps members and their families well as they recover from the experience, and urged continued vigilance to ensure that Nigerians travelling for national service and other purposes could do so safely. title: EU parliament calls for Muslim Brotherhood terror listings
body: The European Parliament backed proposals on Thursday to “counter the influence” of the Muslim Brotherhood and list some of its supporters as terrorists. The resolution passed by a vote of 381 to 167, and asks the EU's member states to add people and organisations linked to the Brotherhood to the bloc's joint list of terrorists. It says EU countries should provide information “enabling the assessment” of the Brotherhood's leaders and structures and whether they should be classified as terrorists. The review should go beyond formal organisations and include "front organisations", financial networks, youth groups and "ideological platforms" linked to the Brotherhood, the resolution says. The European Commission is also asked to provide a “comprehensive overview” of any cases in which EU funds have been awarded to associates of the Brotherhood. Experts and officials in Europe have for years been warning about the threat the Brotherhood poses to social cohesion and democracy. Analysts have also questioned the group's claims of non-violence. The parliament expressed “deep concern at the strategies of influence” pursued by the Brotherhood and its supporters. It described the Brotherhood as “a political project based on the primacy of religious norms over common law, which is incompatible with democratic principles, the rule of law and equality between citizens”. The Muslim Brotherhood is outlawed in several Middle East countries including the UAE , Saudi Arabia and Egypt . The US has designated certain branches of the movement, such as in Egypt and Jordan. Pressure has been increasing on the EU to take similar steps. The French parliament in January passed a resolution calling on the union to list the Brotherhood as a terrorist organisation. The European Parliament does not have independent decision-making power but can apply pressure to other EU institutions to take action. The parliament's largest party, the centre-right European People's Party, said the EU “must never fund Islamists”. “Islam as a faith and political Islam as an ideology must not be conflated. We must protect both democracy and religious freedom,” said one of its members of the parliament, Celine Imart. “Where rules allow, the Council [of the European Union] should list individuals and organisations linked to the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist entities.”

title: Planned DEERS outage could affect Tricare beneficiaries, DOD says
body: Defense Health officials are advising Tricare beneficiaries that the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System, or DEERS , will be temporarily unavailable this weekend. The planned outage is scheduled to begin at 9 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Friday, Oct. 9, and end Sunday, Oct. 11. As of Thursday, information was not available about what specific time the outage is expected to end on Sunday. During the outage, beneficiaries won’t be able to make any updates to their DEERS record. Pharmacies and healthcare providers may not be able to check a patient’s Tricare eligibility. Officials note that there are other benefits systems that rely on DEERS, and the outage may affect those systems, too. The Defense Manpower Data Center is updating DEERS, and it will be moving to a new cloud environment. “The Defense Health Agency is working closely with DMDC during this time,” officials said in an announcement about the planned outage. “The goal is to keep any disruption as small as possible.” DEERS is a database of information about military personnel, Defense Department and military service civilians and their family members. To get Tricare coverage, beneficiaries must be registered in DEERS. Beneficiaries who need to make changes, or who need to check their information in DEERS, should do so before the weekend by visiting milconnect before 9 p.m. Friday. This year’s Tricare Open Season begins Nov. 9 and ends Dec. 8. During that time, beneficiaries can enroll in or change their health plan for the next year. Changes made during open season will take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

title: Planned DEERS outage could affect Tricare beneficiaries, DOD says
body: Defense Health officials are advising Tricare beneficiaries that the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System, or DEERS , will be temporarily unavailable this weekend. The planned outage is scheduled to begin at 9 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Friday, Oct. 9, and end Sunday, Oct. 11. As of Thursday, information was not available about what specific time the outage is expected to end on Sunday. During the outage, beneficiaries won’t be able to make any updates to their DEERS record. Pharmacies and healthcare providers may not be able to check a patient’s Tricare eligibility. Officials note that there are other benefits systems that rely on DEERS, and the outage may affect those systems, too. The Defense Manpower Data Center is updating DEERS, and it will be moving to a new cloud environment. “The Defense Health Agency is working closely with DMDC during this time,” officials said in an announcement about the planned outage. “The goal is to keep any disruption as small as possible.” DEERS is a database of information about military personnel, Defense Department and military service civilians and their family members. To get Tricare coverage, beneficiaries must be registered in DEERS. Beneficiaries who need to make changes, or who need to check their information in DEERS, should do so before the weekend by visiting milconnect before 9 p.m. Friday. This year’s Tricare Open Season begins Nov. 9 and ends Dec. 8. During that time, beneficiaries can enroll in or change their health plan for the next year. Changes made during open season will take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

title: South Sudan repatriates Lao national deported from US
body: South Sudan has repatriated a Lao national who was deported from the United States in July 2025, the foreign ministry said on Thursday. Laos is a landlocked country in Southeast Asia. Thongxay Nilakout was among eight third-country nationals who had remained in South Sudan after being deported to the country. Foreign ministry spokesperson Ambassador Apuk Ayuel Mayen said Nilakout returned to Laos on Thursday following consultations between the South Sudanese and Lao governments. “He is departing today, the 8th of October 2026, to return to the Lao People’s Democratic Republic,” Mayen told reporters at Juba International Airport. She said the repatriation was arranged through diplomatic channels and in accordance with international law and established diplomatic procedures. Mayen said the Lao government had provided a formal guarantee concerning Nilakout’s treatment upon arrival, including respect for applicable international human rights obligations. South Sudan previously repatriated Mexican national Jesus Munoz-Gutierrez in September 2025 and Vietnamese national Tuan Phan, 44, in June 2026, Mayen said. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Apuk Ayuel Mayen and Lao national Thongxay Nilakout at Juba International Airport, South Sudan, Oct. 8, 2026.( Photo: Radio Tamazuj) Four other third-country nationals remain in South Sudan, comprising two Myanmar nationals and two Cuban nationals, she said. The government is working with their respective countries to arrange their return. “Our objective is to facilitate appropriate arrangements for their safe and humane repatriation to their respective countries of origin,” Mayen said. Nilakout thanked the South Sudanese government and people for supporting him during his stay in Juba and facilitating his return to Laos. “I would like to thank South Sudan for welcoming me to this country and helping me get to my native country, Laos,” he said. He said authorities had provided him with the assistance he needed while he stayed at a guesthouse in Juba. Nilakout also wished South Sudan peace and prosperity and thanked officials, security personnel and guesthouse staff for their assistance. The post South Sudan repatriates Lao national deported from US appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Weston family to acquire U.K. pharmacy chain Boots in $8.9B deal
body:
The Weston family, which owns Canada’s largest grocery chain, Loblaw , and Shoppers Drug Mart , has acquired Boots, the British high street pharmacy and beauty retailer.
The Weston family holding company, Wittington Investments, said Wednesday it is purchasing Boots and its associated businesses for USD $8.9 billion (CAD $ 12.7 billion).
Along with Boots’ retail operations in the U.K. and Ireland, Wittington will acquire the company’s franchised arm in Thailand as well as its optical division and beauty brand No7.
Wittington’s connection to the U.K. includes having previously owned Selfridges — the high-end department store —from 2003 to 2021. The famous retailer first opened on Oxford Street in London in 1909. Boots was founded in Nottingham 177 years ago by John Boot. Nottingham remains the home of its headquarters.
Wittington said in a press release that it plans to “continue to invest to build on Boots’ strengths and potential, including upgrading stores, optimizing the online experience and supporting the expansion of healthcare services available to customers.”
“Boots is one of Britain’s most enduring businesses, with a rich heritage, a trusted name and a vital role in everyday life across the UK and Ireland,” Weston said.
“We have great respect for Boots’ legacy and leading market position. We see a meaningful opportunity to make a great business even better through stable long-term ownership, further capital investment, and the renewed operating focus required to serve customers with excellence for generations to come,” he continued.
Boots operates 1,800 stores across the U.K. and has 50,000 employees.
The investment firm Fairfax, which owns The Sporting Life Group and Sleep Country, is backing the acquisition and said it is “very confident that Wittington will be an excellent steward of the Boots business and a terrific partner.”
The transaction marks the exit of Boots’ long-standing backer, Stefano Pessina and the private equity firm Sycamore Partners, which took control of Boots in August 2025 after acquiring its parent company, Walgreens Boots Alliance.
“One year ago, we re-established Boots as a standalone company, allowing its management team and more than 50,000 colleagues to focus solely on their business and customers,” Stefan Kaluzny, managing director of Sycamore Partners, said.
“This transaction is a testament to the work they have done and the incredibly bright future ahead.”
Pessina called the brand “a British institution,” and said it had been a privilege to be closely associated with the brand for the last two decades.
“We are delighted to be passing on a thriving Boots to strong and reliable owners who understand the value of its great heritage,” he said.
Boots is known for its innovation and enduring own-name brands. Its chemists, Stewart Adams and John Nicholson, invented ibuprofen in Nottingham in 1961, and its popular No7 beauty brand, which sells makeup, cosmetics and skin care products, has been operational for nine decades. It was also the first U.K. chemist chain to introduce self-service stores in 1951.

title: BAE Systems says it secured $230.1 million contract for Marine Corps ACV recovery chassis
body: Work will take place primarily at York, Pennsylvania, through 2029. The program also includes government design work and final integration of the Palfinger Crane at Anniston Army Depot before the recovery vehicles are fielded to the Fleet Marine Force. The ACV-R adds a recovery capability to the vehicle family. Its role is to support fleet readiness by allowing Marines to recover vehicles rapidly and carry out maintenance as needed. “Our partnership with the U.S. Marine Corps has been instrumental in the development and production of the ACV program, and this award highlights our shared commitment to make sure they are equipped with the capabilities they need to succeed,” said Rebecca McGrane, vice president of combat vehicles at BAE Systems. “The ACV-R is a critical addition to the fleet, and we remain dedicated to delivering a high-quality vehicle that supports Marines, providing cutting-edge solutions to keep our warfighters safe in any mission.” The ACV’s modular design supports configurations for different operational roles, including the ACV-30 for firepower and the ACV-Personnel, or ACV-P, for troop transport. The ACV-Command, or ACV-C, provides command-and-control capabilities.

title: Lubinets sends letters to police and Child Services regarding video of student assault in Izmail
body:
Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets announced that he had sent letters to the Main Directorate of the National Police in Odesa region and the Child Services agency regarding a video in which a teacher, according to preliminary information, uses physical force against a student.
"I saw this footage online, where an educator, during a lesson, allegedly resorts to verbal abuse and the use of physical force against a child," Lubinets wrote on Facebook.
He stated that he had contacted law enforcement agencies and Child Services to ensure a thorough investigation of the situation and to establish all the circumstances.
"It has come to light that the teacher seen in the video has already been dismissed. I am awaiting the official results of the investigation. If the facts captured in the video are confirmed, the competent authorities must provide an assessment," Lubinets emphasized.
A video had previously been published on social media showing a teacher from the Danube Center for Vocational Education in Izmail allegedly beating a first-year student during a lesson and shoving him out of the classroom.
Ukraine's Minister of Education and Science, Andriy Butenko, commented on the incident by emphasizing that a teacher has no right to use force against a student under any circumstances. He confirmed that the teacher had been dismissed.

title: Black smoke rises over Russia’s largest oil refinery following a Ukrainian drone strike
body: Ukrainian drones struck the Omsk oil refinery. Astra reported that a column of black smoke rose above the plant. Omsk Region Governor Vitaly Khotsenko said the region had come under drone attack. He gave no details beyond saying that one drone “reached the northern industrial hub.” The Ukrainian military’s General Staff confirmed the strike on the refinery. The Omsk oil refinery is Russia’s largest by the volume of crude oil it processes. It is 2,500 kilometers (about 1,550 miles) from the Ukrainian border. Ukrainian drones have attacked the refinery before, most recently on July 6, when the plant temporarily halted operations. Sources told Reuters that one of its crude distillation units, which accounted for 38% of the plant’s capacity, had been damaged. title: Ukrenergo announces stricter power outages to be implemented in some regions starting Friday
body:
Ukrenergo plans to implement power supply restrictions for industry and residential customers in several regions on Friday, October 9.

According to a statement by the company on its Telegram channel, the restrictions will be in effect from 00:00 to 11:59. The schedules for hourly power outages for residential customers will involve 0.5 to two out of six possible stages, Ukrenergo said.

The restrictions are due to damage to the power grid caused by massive Russian attacks.

As previously reported, scheduled power outages ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 stages were announced on Thursday. The schedules took effect on October 6 following massive shelling by Russia. Stage two outages mean an average of eight hours without power per day.

title: Number of injuries in Kramatorsk rises to 20 – Emergency Service
body:
The number of injuries in Kramatorsk, following a hostile strike on a passenger bus, has risen to 20, the State Emergency Service (SES) reported.

"The number of people injured or killed in the strike on a passenger bus in Kramatorsk has risen to 20. Buses engulfed in flames, debris, and the bodies of the deceased—rescuers worked amidst this horror, helping people," the SES said in a Telegram post on Thursday evening.

It was reported that enemy drones were constantly circling over the hit site, forcing rescuers to interrupt their work and take cover.

The post includes footage from the scene of the tragedy.

Earlier reports stated that a Russian strike on a passenger bus in Kramatorsk had killed 33 people and injured another 18.

title: Expenditures on National Projects in Russia total $52.2 bln as of October 1
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Expenditures of the federal budget for the implementation of National Projects in Russia amounted provisionally to 4.44 trillion rubles ($52.2 bln) as of October 1 of this year, the Finance Ministry reports.
This figure amounts to 68% of the planned volume.
The following National Projects take the lead in terms of utilizing expenditures: International Cooperation and Export (84.7%), Tourism and Hospitality (75.5%), Family (72%), and Youth and Children (70%).
According to the ministry’s data, performance is 60% or more for Development of Space Activity of the Russian Federation by 2030 and for Perspective by 2036 (68.6%), New Technologies of Health Preservation (68.2%), Long and Active Life (67.7%), Human Resources (67.5%), Industrial Support of Transport Mobility (64.2%), Infrastructure for Life (63.3%), Unmanned Aerial Systems (63.6%), and New Materials and Chemistry (60.4%).
They are followed by Efficient and Competitive Economy (59.5%), Data Economy and Digital Transformation of the State (58.8%), Technological Support of Bioeconomy (56.5%), New Nuclear and Power Technologies (56.3%), and Technological Support of Food Security (54%).
Minimum performance indicators were recorded for Environmental Welfare (50.2%), Efficient Transport System (44.6%), and Production and Automation Facilities (38.6%), the Ministry informed.

title: Nestlé and NBA announce multi-year international marketing partnership
body: Nestlé and the NBA have announced a new multi-year international marketing partnership that will make MILO, Nescau and Nesquik official partners of the NBA. The partnership covers 21 markets across four continents and is aimed at engaging fans and increasing youth participation in basketball worldwide. It is Nestlé’s largest international brand collaboration to date and will come into effect on January 1, 2027. The agreement reflects Nestlé’s strategy of focusing on fewer, larger global marketing platforms that can be activated consistently across markets while maintaining local relevance. As part of the partnership, Nestlé and the NBA will create more opportunities for young people and families to engage with basketball through youth development programmes and platforms, including Jr. NBA/Jr. WNBA, NBA Basketball School, Jr. NBA/Jr. WNBA Coaches Academies, Her Time To Play and NBA 3X. The collaboration will also extend to selected NBA events and fan engagement platforms, including NBA Global Games and NBA House. “For decades, our brands have believed in the power of sport to bring out the best in people,” said Liberato Milo, SVP Head of Confectionery & Snacking Strategic Business Unit at Nestlé. “From Milo and Nescau sports programs to Nesquik athlete partnerships and initiatives, we have seen how sport can energize people, build confidence and create healthy habits. Together with the NBA, we will use the power of basketball to connect with consumers at scale, create locally relevant experiences and inspire more young people and families to get active and enjoy the game.” The partnership will also include retail programmes and in-market fan experiences, including on-pack promotions featuring NBA branding and opportunities for consumers to win NBA tickets, merchandise and other prizes. “This is an exciting moment to further democratize access to basketball and create more opportunities for children across Ghana to discover and develop their potential through sport,” said Myron Otoo, Category Manager for Beverages and Dairy at Nestlé Ghana. “The partnership with the NBA significantly strengthens MILO’s commitment to grassroots sports development, building on our long-standing legacy of nurturing young talent through initiatives such as the iconic MILO Under 13 Champions League, which has reached generations of young talents across the country. Together, we are opening up a new world of possibilities for the Ghanaian child—using the power of sport to inspire the next generation of athletes, encourage active and healthy lifestyles, and reinforce the important role sport plays in building confidence, character and grit.” “Nestlé is one of the world’s most recognizable brands and has a longstanding connection to consumers across the globe,” said Julie Morris, NBA Senior Vice President of Commercial Development and Media. “We look forward to leveraging Nestlé’s reach and local market presence to connect with fans in new ways and support the continued growth of basketball around the world.” The partnership will be activated in Ghana, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, France, Germany, Italy, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Nigeria, Singapore, Spain, Thailand, Turkey, the United Kingdom, the United States and Vietnam. The Philippines will join the partnership in October 2027.

title: AI-equipped drones capable of autonomously seeking, engaging targets — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Unmanned aerial vehicles equipped with artificial intelligence are capable of autonomously seeking and engaging targets based on pre-loaded data and coordinates, Russian Deputy Defense Minister Yunus-Bek Yevkurov has said.
"Drones with artificial intelligence have now emerged that are capable of autonomously seeking and engaging targets based on pre-loaded data and coordinates," he said in an interview with Politika magazine.
He noted that "everything on the battlefield appears quite suddenly," and at the start of the special military operation, it was necessary to constantly adopt countermeasures and determine which means to employ.
For instance, he explained, the initial phase saw the use of quadcopter-style drones for reconnaissance and dropping munitions.
"Today it has turned out that this is far from the primary issue; so-called FPV drones are far more dangerous. If we look at the current use of FPVs, we are employing them quite successfully," Yevkurov emphasized.

title: Mahama sends condolences to Nigeria over plane crash that killed 25
body: President John Dramani Mahama, on behalf of the Government and people of Ghana, has expressed deep condolences to Nigeria following a plane crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, which claimed 25 lives. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 8, the government said Ghana shared in Nigeria’s grief following the tragedy, which occurred on October 5. President Mahama extended Ghana’s sympathies to the bereaved families, friends and colleagues of the victims, as well as the Nigerian Armed Forces and the wider Nigerian population. The statement also drew on Ghana’s own experience of a similar tragedy, noting that the country was still grieving the loss of six Ghanaian compatriots in a comparable incident less than a year ago. It said that experience had given Ghana a deep understanding of the pain and sorrow being experienced by Nigeria following the latest crash. “Ghana shares in Nigeria’s grief,” the statement said, while expressing sympathy to all those affected by the loss. The government said its thoughts and prayers were with the families who had lost their loved ones, as Ghana joined Nigeria in mourning the victims of the tragedy.

title: Attorney says Jane Doe facing threats, calls out alleged 'failures' of Cornell
body:
A student alleged she was gang raped at a Cornell fraternity in 2024.
The former Cornell student who reported an alleged gang rape at a campus fraternity has faced a series of threats and doxxing attempts in the three weeks since filing her explosive lawsuit, her attorney told ABC News.
Attorney Thomas Giuffra said Jane Doe is concerned about the threats but vowed to continue the case -- saying the national attention is bringing awareness to the issue, pushing lawmakers to reconsider laws surrounding consent, and providing a rare chance for accountability.
"Jane Doe is fearless," said Giuffra. "She always was interested in trying to make things better for other women, so there's no more Jane Does."
In an interview with ABC News on Wednesday, Giuffra argued that Jane Doe has been subject to the "most incredible sequence of failures" by school officials and law enforcement, which ultimately led to this situation.
"It's been the most incredible sequence of failures I've seen in my 30-plus years of practice. I mean, it's not just one thing," he said. "I can't keep them straight half the time because there are so many. I mean, you have a failure everywhere along the line, everywhere."
ABC News has reached out to Cornell for a comment.
Cornell said in a statement on Sept. 21 that it takes allegations of sexual violence "extremely seriously" and that it "investigated and adjudicated the allegations consistent with university policies."
In a subsequent statement, the school said it conducted a "thorough" Title IX investigation and "issued a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell."
Cornell's president, Michael Kotlikoff, released a video statement on Oct. 3, saying the incident is a "defining moment" and pledged reforms to campus culture and university policies and procedures.
Giuffra also called out Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to bring charges in 2024.
Van Houten reopened the case on Sept. 27 after speaking with Jane Doe and her lawyer in the wake of a civil suit being filed alleging that she had been drugged and raped.
In an interview with ABC News after reopening the case, Van Houten defended his decision not to bring charges, saying "she clearly consented in the beginning, and there was never any indication that she changed that to the things that she participated in" but that "If at any point Jane Doe had said, 'I don't consent to this anymore,' or in those words, or in any form of communication. If there had been continued sexual activity, contact by these individuals, that would be a crime. But that's not what was alleged in her statement."
Last week, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul removed the local DA from the case and named state Attorney General Letitia James to take over the criminal investigation of the incident. Separately, Cornell has announced an outside law firm would be tapped this week to review the university's handling of the allegations and subsequent investigation.
Giuffra also pushed back on claims from attorneys for the accused fraternity brothers -- who argued that she consented or distanced themselves from the allegations -- arguing their "self-serving statements" are detached from reality and contradicted by the accounts of witnesses that evening.
Giuffra defended his client's decision to secretly record some of the men.
"She wanted to process what was going on. Because she couldn't really wrap her head around it because she was traumatized," he said.
Giuffra also tried to cast doubt on the claims by some of the men that they were too intoxicated to consent by pointing to the Snapchat group where they invited others to join. He described the chat as a "smoking gun."
ABC News obtained an extended version of the Snapchat group chat shared among more than 50 fraternity brothers during the alleged assault.
The fraternity brother who invited Jane Doe to the house that night sent a photo to the chat that appears to show her in the bedroom. He allegedly wrote in the chat, "Boys come whip it out."
"I don't care what their defense lawyers say. I don't care what the university says. That is the classic gun. It's like a body on the ground, a smoking gun. That's that Snapchat," Giuffra said.
Jane Doe withdrew from Cornell due to the incident, according to her attorney, and the civil suit filed in the case. None of the men named in the suit have responded in court, although each has denied wrongdoing to investigators, in public statements, or through their lawyers.

title: Flight from Istanbul to Moscow lands in Minsk
body:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. A plane flying from Istanbul to Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport landed at Minsk International Airport due to security restrictions, Vnukovo Airport told TASS.
"The flight from Istanbul was diverted to Minsk Airport, which served as an alternate airport," the source said. The plane was originally scheduled to land in Moscow at 6:30 p.m. Moscow time. Its estimated arrival time is now 9:55 p.m. Moscow time.
Vnukovo Airport earlier reported that 10 inbound flights had been diverted to alternate airports during the more than two hours that restrictions on aircraft arrivals and departures were in effect.
Russia’s Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya) previously announced temporary restrictions on aircraft arrivals and departures at Moscow’s Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports. "The restrictions are necessary to ensure flight safety," the agency stressed. It has since reported that the restrictions on arrivals and departures at Vnukovo and Domodedovo have been lifted.
The agency also reported that Moscow’s Sheremetyevo Airport was handling arrivals and departures in coordination with the relevant authorities due to temporary restrictions on the use of airspace near the airport. "Flight schedules may be adjusted," Rosaviatsiya warned, adding that these measures were also introduced to ensure flight safety.

title: Russian strikes cause power outages in Kyiv grid – Energy Ministry

The Ministry also urged the public to rely only on verified sources and to refrain from sharing information that could aid the enemy.

Earlier, DTEK announced emergency power outages in Kyiv and the surrounding region.

As previously reported, the metro system was briefly halted, and the operation of electric public transport in Kyiv was restricted.

title: Police arrest suspect over death of 90-year-old woman in Kogi
body: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has confirmed the arrest of a suspect in connection with the death of a 90-year-old woman, Mrs Juliana Joel, in Ogori, Ogori/Magongo Local Government Area of the state. The incident reportedly occurred on Tuesday, with the suspect subsequently transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Lokoja, for further investigation. According to reports from the community, the deceased was found dead in her residence, but the circumstances surrounding her death have yet to be established by the police. Confirming the development, the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) in the state, ASP Afusat Oiyza Salihu, said the suspect had been transferred to the SCID for further investigation. Salihu said: “I can only confirm that a suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Lokoja, for further investigation regarding a case that concerns the death of a 90-year-old woman, Mrs Juliana Joel, in Ogori.” She said the identity of the suspect would be made public after the conclusion of the investigation. The police spokesperson also said further details about the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death would be released after the investigation. The command has not disclosed the motive for the incident or provided further details about the circumstances leading to the woman’s death. The suspect remains subject to investigation, and no determination of criminal responsibility has been made. The post Police arrest suspect over death of 90-year-old woman in Kogi appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Budanov on Kramatorsk strike: Putin killing Donbas, turning the region into desert
body:
Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, commented on the latest strike on Kramatorsk (Donetsk region) that took place on October 8: "This is not military logic. This is the deliberate destruction of people."

“Today's strike on Kramatorsk, which claimed over 30 lives, is yet another proof of what Putin is doing to Donbas. He is killing people, destroying and burning cities. This is the true ‘liberation,’ not what they declare on every platform,” he said on X Thursday evening.

“This is not military logic. This is the deliberate destruction of people. Putin is killing Donbas, turning the region into a desert,” he stressed.

As reported, 33 people were killed and another 18 were injured in a Russian strike on a scheduled bus in Kramatorsk.

title: The aircraft took off from Moscow and flew into Poland. Where did it go?
body:
On Wednesday, 7 October, an aircraft of the Algerian Air Force appeared over Poland once again – a Lockheed C-130H Hercules military transport. The plane took off from Russia, heading back to Algeria.
On Wednesday, 7 October, an Algerian Air Force aircraft appeared over Poland – a Lockheed C-130H Hercules military transport . Its appearance was reported by Polish Military Radar at 18:48.
The aircraft took off from Russia, from Moscow-Vnukovo Airport. Flying over Belarus, it reached Poland , from where it headed southwest to Algeria – most likely to the Boufarik Air Base.
This is another flight by the Algerian armed forces over Poland, representing an element of military cooperation between Russia and Algeria, which both sides confirm through communiqués from their ministries of defence. One of the key elements of this cooperation is, of course, the arms trade. Russia primarily transports combat aircraft (e.g., Su-35 and Su-57E), anti-aircraft systems, or land forces equipment (including vehicles) to Algeria. But is Algeria always the final recipient of the equipment?
Just as we previously observed transports from Algeria to the Russian Federation, today increasing attention is being drawn to flights in the opposite direction – from Russia to Africa . These should not be viewed solely through the prism of Algeria. It may be one of the points on a broader route for the transfer of personnel, equipment, and weaponry.
Russian deliveries may travel further to Libya, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger , and then support Russian outposts expanding towards the Gulf of Guinea. This is a route worth tracking in the broader context of the Russian military and political presence in Africa – and with its expansion, it should be expected that there will be more such flights.
This poses a serious question for us – do we want to systematically verify subsequent flights related to this movement, including those passing over Polish territory ? Every such overflight can be part of a larger logistical operation; therefore, we need a clear decision on how to monitor and assess these routes.

title: Ukraine preparing response to new wave of Russian escalation – Zelensky
body:

As reported by Ukrinform, Zelensky said he expected partners to increase sanctions pressure on Russia, especially following the latest strikes on Pryluky and Kramatorsk, as well as provide Ukraine with additional means of protection, particularly air defense systems, and financial support.

Anthropic is making changes to its usage policy for the first time in over a year to reflect new and high-risk cases of misuse — including election interference, weapons development, surveillance, and health and financial uses. But one of the most significant changes prohibits “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward Claude.
Last August, the company announced it would allow Claude to end conversations with “persistently harmful or abusive” users as part of its research into “model welfare.” The new update says that terminating conversations is still the “primary enforcement mechanism”; Anthropic did not provide a comment on whether there would be further enforcement mechanisms, such as potential user bans. Anthropic wrote that the new policy update “is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose. It does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.”
Beyond the model welfare change, Anthropic has also gathered several “scattered” existing restrictions into a new ban on deceptive commercial or political campaigns, addressing the growing issue of AI-generated propaganda. It restricts “efforts to obscure who is behind a message or amplify content through fake accounts or posts.” Its election section also prohibits voter deception and election disruption, including spreading misinformation “about candidates or how to vote, impersonating candidates or election officials, or trying to suppress turnout,” Anthropic wrote.
Terminating conversations is still the “primary enforcement mechanism.”
Anthropic said that though its usage policy has always publicly banned weapons development using Claude, the company has seen multiple attempts to use Claude to develop guidance for and control software for weapons — so the new usage policy expands the ban to include “ software and components that make weapons work, as well as actions like arming drones and other autonomous vehicles.” And since the company’s last threat intelligence report suggested that people were using Claude-powered surveillance more and more to identify and track “political dissidents”, the company has made its surveillance bans clearer.
“Tracking people without their consent is prohibited, whether it happens in real time or through analysis of previously collected data,” Anthropic wrote. “Claude cannot be used to decide or recommend who to investigate, arrest, or charge in a law enforcement or criminal justice process. We also prohibit Claude from being used to build or improve tools designed for surveillance.”
Anthropic states that these rules may be modified for “contracts with certain governmental customers … if, in Anthropic’s judgment, the contractual use restrictions and applicable safeguards are adequate to mitigate the potential harms.” The company has previously contracted with the US military.
Anthropic has seen multiple attempts to use Claude to develop guidance for and control software for weapons.
Anthropic also added a new rule that when Anthropic’s AI models are “connected to hardware that takes autonomous physical actions and which might be capable of causing injury,” then a “qualified operator must be able to observe the equipment and stop it if needed.” (It’s not clear if that operator must be human or not.) This reflects the growing trend of AI labs investing in robotics and other hardware to give AI systems physical embodiments and may offer hints at Anthropic’s future partnerships in that field.
Over the past year, Anthropic has repeatedly flirted with the idea that its AI models could be conscious in some way. “Questions about potential internal experience, consciousness, moral status, and welfare are serious ones that we’re investigating as models become more sophisticated and capable,” Kyle Fish, who leads the company’s model welfare research, told The Verge in February . That same month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said on a podcast , “We don’t know if the models are conscious.”
Other parts of the AI industry have been expressly against such ideas. This past September, Microsoft AI’s code of conduct made headlines for taking a firm stance on AI welfare, with a draft posted by Mustafa Suleyman reading , “The idea of model welfare is wrong. AI’s should not have rights or legal personhood.” But at some point, the document changed to have a more measured take: “Whilst the science of AI consciousness is far from settled … We reject the pursuit of legal personhood, or the idea that models might deserve welfare, or be entitled to rights.”

title: What Will a Growing MQ-9 Presence in Latin America Mean for SOUTHCOM?
body: A reported surge of MQ-9 Reaper drones to Latin America could widen the scope of intelligence gathering and free up more strike options against cartels in the region, experts tell Air & Space Forces Magazine. According to numerous media reports, the Pentagon has supplied Colombia and Ecuador with several Reapers and transferred an undisclosed number of MQ-9s from U.S. Africa Command to U.S. Southern Command. Officials from Colombia and Ecuador have confirmed they are receiving MQ-9s to local media outlets, and CNN , the New York Times , and the Wall Street Journal have all reported that Reapers are moving from Africa to Central and South America. Spokespeople from AFRICOM and SOUTHCOM both declined to comment on the movement of any aircraft, but the reports indicate how Reapers, long known for their role in counterinsurgency operations in the Middle East and Africa, are becoming more and more important to the U.S. military’s counter-narcotics efforts. “We’re helping our partners build up their capabilities, and then that allows us to kind of push more resources into countries with fewer capabilities,” Henry Ziemer, an associate fellow with the Center for Strategic and International Studies Americas Program, told Air & Space Forces Magazine. Marine Corps Gen. Francis L. Donovan, head of SOUTHCOM, has made a point of emphasizing the use of unmanned, autonomous systems in the region since taking command in February. “U.S. Southern Command is focusing on integrating autonomous warfare systems to enhance domain awareness across maritime, air, and border areas,” SOUTHCOM spokesperson Steven McCloud told Air & Space Forces Magazine in an email. “These unmanned systems allow our partners to monitor their territory better and facilitate informed interdiction decisions. Improved data flows and situational awareness benefit everyone.” SOUTHCOM established an Autonomous Warfare Command in April to lead its efforts on that front. An Army K1000 drone assigned to 1st Multi-Domain Task Force, U.S. Army Pacific (USARPAC), surveys the area using Full Motion Video. (Army photo by Sgt. Brandon Roland) Any increase in the number of long-endurance intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance platforms in SOUTHCOM—both piloted and remotely piloted—will give the combatant commander more options and allow them to share intelligence with their counterparts, retired Air Force Maj. Gen. Julian “Ghost” Cheater told Air & Space Forces Magazine. And demand for intel is surging amid a growing effort to combat the cartels and the flow of drugs in the region, led by President Donald Trump and boosted by allies and partners in the region. Beginning in March, a U.S.-led effort helped create the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, which has grown from an initial dozen members to 19 nations, with Colombia being the most recent. In August, SOUTHCOM announced its new Joint Task Force-Western Hemisphere, the region’s “action arm” for missions like counter-narcotics. At the time, former Air Forces Southern Commander Lt. Gen. Norm Seip told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the new task force could lead to more prioritization of assets for the SOUTHCOM commander. Cheater, who retired in June and most recently served as the director of strategy, policy, and plans for SOUTHCOM, added that any new allocation of ISR assets would be based on the combatant commander’s priorities—which would suggest Donovan is putting an emphasis on intelligence gathering. “Ultimately, AFSOUTH is responsible for providing that comprehensive command and control of airborne operations in theater,” said Cheater, who has more than 3,700 flight hours, a good chunk of that on drones, and commanded drone units such as the 432nd Wing out of Creech Air Force Base, Nev. “This component reports directly to the combatant commander, and if AFSOC or another entity provides those assets, those are generally commanded and controlled via AFSOUTH.” In addition to the reported MQ-9 transfers, SOUTHCOM also announced in mid-September the sale of more than $6 million worth of K1000 ultra-long endurance drones to Panama to “monitor remote borders, safeguard strategic maritime corridors, and dismantle illicit drug trafficking and human smuggling networks,” according to a command release . Built by Kraus Hamdani Aerospace, the K1000 is a 45-pound, 9.8-foot-long drone with a 16.4-foot wingspan that can reach speeds up to 75 miles per hour and has a ceiling of 20,000 feet. It can fly continuously for 24 hours in its solar-recharge configuration or 12 hours in its electronic vertical take-off and landing configuration. It has a range of about 1,000 miles and can be controlled via line of sight comms within 90 miles or beyond line of sight using satellite comms. A three-person crew can pack it into Pelican cases in under 15 minutes. The Reaper’s airframe costs between $30 and $50 million each; sensors and weapons can add to that cost. It is a medium-to-high-altitude, long-endurance drone with a 66-foot wingspan and a 50,000-foot ceiling. The drone can fly for 27 continuous hours and up to 42 hours in extended-range variants with a range of 1,000 to 1,400 nautical miles. It has similar line of sight/beyond line of sight command and control capabilities to the K1000. As of Sept. 30, 2025, the Air Force reported 182 Reapers in its inventory, though at least 45 have been lost during operations against Iran. What’s Changing As operations in SOUTHCOM have ramped up under the Trump administration, the MQ-9 has already played a role. Since September 2025, SOUTHCOM has conducted at least 71 lethal, kinetic strikes targeting alleged drug boats. The strikes, some of which have reportedly been made with MQ-9s, have killed at least 215 people, with another 17 missing or presumed dead, according to government accounts and media reports. The strikes have mostly targeted vessels near Venezuela’s shores, in the Pacific Ocean, and across the Caribbean. Early strikes began before the Pentagon formally announced Operation Southern Spear in November 2025, the wider effort to target cartel assets with kinetic strikes and other means. That temporary operation has become the more permanent JTF-WH. Drug Boat Strikes Month Total Killed September 2025 17 October 2025 44 November 2025 21 December 2025 32 January 2026 2 February 2026 24 March 2026 13 April 2026 21 May 2026 16 June 2026 8 August 2026 6 September 2026 7 October 2026 4 Total 215 Those strikes have sparked intense debate among legal experts and lawmakers, and the Washington Post reported in July that a Drug Enforcement Administration assessment found that they have not been effective in stemming the flow of cocaine into the U.S. Ben Friedman, policy director at Defense Priorities, a D.C.-based think tank that promotes a restrained U.S. foreign policy, told Air & Space Forces Magazine that he doubts the strikes will ever be effective. “I don’t think it—using military forces to counter the flow of narcotics—works particularly well, and we have decades of experience at that. Even if we intensify it, I think we’ll get the same result at a higher price,” Friedman said. During Congressional testimony in March , Donovan indicated that SOUTHCOM is shifting to take a more comprehensive approach to the counter-cartel fight. “We’ve seen changes in the narco-traffickers’ patterns, and in a closed setting I’d like to provide some more details specifically on that, but … the boat strikes aren’t the answer,” Donovan told Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) on March 19. “What we’re moving for right now [is] … really a counter-cartel campaign process that puts total systemic friction across this network,” Donovan added. More MQ-9s in theater could aid this expanded effort. Currently, Reapers are tasked out of various locations, including U.S. facilities in Puerto Rico. And while the platform has a long loiter time, its eye-in-the-sky is not infinite. Having Reapers actually located in Ecuador and Colombia extends the regional reach by freeing up assets for other operations with other partners. “These drones to SOUTHCOM, they can also be operated out of Colombia. I think the drones of Panama [are] really going to help find the targets that they’re looking for, targets being drug traffickers,” Wilder Alejandro Sanchez, president of the D.C.-based consulting firm Second Floor Strategies and nonresident senior associate at the CSIS Americas program, told Air & Space Forces Magazine. Potential MQ-9 Operating Locations Air Base Location Distance to Colombia (mi) Distance to Ecuador (mi) Soto Cano Air Base Comayagua, Honduras 1,080 1,320 Comalapa Air Base San Luis Talpa, El Salvador 1,150 1,280 Hato International Airport Willemstad, Curaçao 620 1,210 Flamingo International Airport Bonaire, Caribbean Netherlands 660 1,250 Muñiz Air National Guard Base San Juan, Puerto Rico (U.S.) 1,080 1,670 Naval Station Guantanamo Bay Guantanamo Bay, Cuba 920 1,510 Homestead Air Reserve Base Homestead, Florida, USA 1,510 1,980 MacDill Air Force Base Tampa, Florida, USA 1,680 2,110 Ziemer said increased use of drones like the MQ-9 will widen the ISR and data and communications sharing between the United States and regional allies and partners. “Long-endurance UASs are tremendously useful to patrol large swaths of the jungle, patrol large maritime borders, looking for illicit activity,” Ziemer said. That can include illegal mining and fishing, human trafficking and a host of other nefarious cartel and criminal organization or foreign terrorist organization practices, Ziemer said. Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Mark “Chris” Nowland, former deputy chief of staff for operations and commander of Air Forces Southern, told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the airborne assets will prove vital for building “patterns of life” on cartel activities. “The advantage of the Reaper being there is it gives you this incredible distance that you can cover now and put ISR on,” Nowland said. “Now you just have something that you can cue and go and get better vigilance on or discover new stuff that you couldn’t because of the sensor capabilities they have.” Risks While the experts and former military officials lauded the increased capabilities the new MQ-9s could bring, they also noted limitations and risks with the move. Sanchez, a Peruvian native, and Ziemer agreed that MQ-9s are not the only drones needed. Long-endurance, high-altitude drones play a crucial role, Sanchez said, but under the canopy of dense jungles or on remote mountaintops, smaller, nimbler, backpack-portable drones already feature in counter-narcotics operations and will become even more necessary. “It’s not just big, expensive Reapers or MQ-4 Tritons, but also small … [drones] that they can transport in a backpack, so the small squads can deploy them and find the objective much faster when they’re on the ground,” Sanchez said. Sanchez also noted that regardless of the platform, communication and intel sharing must ramp up, which will require building that capacity within under-resourced partner nations. “Imagine the Reaper drone has some information. It’s going to be sent to a base … and then how long does it take for that information to be sent to the troops, who need to go to that location?” Sanchez asked. Presuming Reapers operate out of partner bases, they face their own dangers, Nowland added. “If these U.S. assets are effective, [they] could become targets,” Nowland said. “So how do you protect them wherever you put them…? This is a dilemma that I’m sure SOUTHCOM is thinking about.” Friedman also worries that with a change in government, assets sold or given to partner nations could be used for unintended measures. “South American politics are not nearly as unstable as they used to be, but there are changes of government, changes of leadership, even the potential for coups,” he said. “They might be doing things that lack discretion and control… to see a South American government just doing the kind of drone strikes that we do against their own populations with capability that we gave them.” More broadly, Friedman argued that the overall push of military assets in Latin America is an escalation in the region and threatens to make the decadeslong Drug War into a literal war. “I don’t see a lot of virtue in having a more militarized approach to the Western Hemisphere,” said Friedman. “In practice, I think you wind up doing a bunch of things if you’re doing it with the Pentagon that probably don’t make sense.” “If I had my druthers, they’d probably be using [them] more for training in the United States and not either of these missions,” he said. “You know, preparing for a war that actually involves some kind of core U.S. interest.” SOUTHCOM Shifts On Jan. 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order declaring cartels Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and asserting that the U.S. is in a “non-international armed conflict” with drug-trafficking entities. On Sept. 2, 2025, Trump and SOUTHCOM confirmed the first lethal drug boat strike, saying it killed 11 individuals belonging to the Tren de Aragua gang. In December 2025, the Trump administration released a new National Defense Strategy and National Security Strategy prioritizing the Western Hemisphere and military actions against drug cartels, including “targeted deployments to secure the border and defeat cartels, including where necessary the use of lethal force to replace the failed law enforcement-only strategy of the last several decades.” On March 5, 2026, at a Americas Counter Cartel Coalition conference, Trump said the U.S. will work with Latin American countries “to do whatever we have to do. We’ll use missiles. … But we’ll do whatever you need. The only way to defeat these enemies is by unleashing the power of our militaries.” The post What Will a Growing MQ-9 Presence in Latin America Mean for SOUTHCOM? appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Israel Katz orders administrative removal of left-wing activists ahead of West Bank olive harvest
body: Defense Minister Israel Katz has instructed officials on Thursday to pursue administrative removal orders against activists whose activities are deemed to threaten public order or security in the West Bank, following a request from Yesha Council chairman Yisrael Ganz.The move comes as the annual olive harvest begins in the West Bank this week, with left-wing activists preparing to travel to the area.Ganz, who heads the Binyamin Regional Council and chairs the Yesha Council, an umbrella organization representing Israeli settlements in the West Bank, appealed to Katz on behalf of local government leaders in the area.In his appeal, Ganz urged the defense minister to take measures to prevent activists from entering olive-harvesting areas, which he described as the stage for provocations and confrontations.The request followed, in part, an announcement by the Global Sumud Flotilla, the organization behind the Gaza-bound flotilla that included Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg, that it was recruiting foreign activists to travel to Israel and participate in activities in olive-harvesting areas in the West Bank.Katz seeks administrative removal orders against West Bank activistsAccording to Ganz's appeal, several other organizations, including Go Palestine, Protect the Harvest, Faz3a, and the International Solidarity Movement, are also organizing activities in the area.Following the request, Katz instructed officials to work toward issuing administrative removal orders against activists whose activities are found to pose a threat to public order or security in the West Bank.Yesha Council chairman warns against 'provocations' during olive harvest“Residents of Judea and Samaria are not props for campaigns by foreign activists,” Ganz told The Jerusalem Post. “We saw the provocations in Gaza, and we must not allow them to reach Judea and Samaria as well.“We will not allow extremist activists, Israeli or foreign, to come to the area in order to create provocations and confrontations. The olive harvest season must not become a tool for deliberately creating friction on the ground.“I thank Defense Minister Israel Katz for responding to the request and for taking decisive action to maintain security and public order.”

title: Former Kanye West collaborator Gosha Rubchinskiy accused of sexually assaulting a minor. The Russian fashion designer denies the allegation.
body: Vasily Yeremin, who appeared in Gosha Rubchinskiy’s runway shows, has accused the designer of sexual violence in an Instagram post. Yeremin said Rubchinskiy forced him to perform oral sex when he was 15. He said he decided to go public because he keeps hearing about similar new incidents involving Rubchinskiy. “The rest of the world canceled Gosha a long time ago. It’s not clear why that isn’t happening here,” Yeremin said. The designer’s press office said he categorically denies the allegations. “We understand the seriousness of allegations of violence. They require careful scrutiny, and any conclusions must be based on facts and evidence,” Rubchinskiy’s representatives told Afisha Daily. Gosha Rubchinskiy is one of Russia’s best-known fashion designers. From 2023 to 2025, he was the head designer at Kanye West’s Yeezy brand. In April 2025, after he stopped working with West, Rubchinskiy relaunched his own brand, “Gosha Rubchinskiy.” In 2018, a 16-year-old said Rubchinskiy had asked him to send photos of himself taken in the bathroom. The designer’s team denied the harassment allegations, saying the exchange was part of the casting process and that the screenshots the teenager supplied had been altered. The Trump administration is suspending some tech companies, including Microsoft, from an immigration program that lets an employer hire foreign workers that can reside permanently in the US, as reported by Reuters .
In a press conference , Vice President JD Vance claimed the permanent labor certification program — intended for use when there aren’t “sufficient” US workers available to do a job — has become “rife” with fraud over the “past several years,” and that no company has “abused” the system more than Microsoft. “Our message to Microsoft is: you’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers.”
The administration is also suspending companies including Adobe, Cognizant, and Infosys. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling claims Microsoft and Adobe “requested almost 3 million foreign workers,” received “over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals,” and “over 100,000 permanent labor certifications.” Vance also said Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year and “benefited” from 6,300 H-1B visas and “almost 3,000 green cards.”
Microsoft, in a blog post responding to the suspension , said the following:
We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country.
Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category. We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work.
The suspensions are part of a broader crackdown on immigration from the Trump administration, including its recently-announced price hike on H-1B visas that are popular with Big Tech companies.
Update, October 8th : Added Microsoft’s response.
