title: Seven people injured in Zaporizhia following enemy attacks – Regional Military Administration
body:
The number of people injured in Zaporizhia as a result of enemy strikes has risen to seven, reported Mykhailo Semykin, head of the Regional Military Administration.

"The number of injured from enemy strikes has risen to seven. Among the injured are three men, two women, a child, and a female minor," he wrote on Telegram on Thursday evening.

All are receiving necessary assistance. Information regarding the condition of the injured is being clarified.

Earlier, five injuries were reported. One fatality—the driver of a vehicle struck by a drone—had also been confirmed.

title: Train service resumes on all Kyiv metro lines
body:
Train service has resumed on all lines of the Kyiv Metro.

"Trains are running with extended intervals: Red Line – 10 minutes; Blue Line – 5 minutes; Green Line – 10 minutes," the metro's press service reported on Telegram.

All metro stations are open for entry, the service added.

Earlier, the Kyiv Metro press service announced that train operations and escalator service had been temporarily suspended due to a drop in voltage from external power sources.

title: LA 2028: Black Queens take first leg advantage with 3-0 win over Mauritius
body: Ghana claimed an emphatic win in their second round 2028 Olympic Games qualifier against Mauritius. The Black Queens claimed a 3-0 win in Mauritius to kickstart their campaign in the quest to play at the summer games for the first time. Kim Lars Bjorkegren made several changes to his regular back line opting for the centre-back partnership of Diana Amoako and debutant Margaret Agyapomaa with Afi Amenyeku getting the nod in goal. Comfort Yeboah and Benedicte Simon started as the fullback options with the middle consisting of Jennifer Cudjoe, Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah and Evelyn Badu. Abigail Kim led the line with support from Alice Kusi and Stella Nyamekye on the flanks. The Black Queens took time to settle but they only waited for 16 minutes to get the opening goal. Nyamekye’s low cross after being released down the right wing found Kim, who scored from close range to make to it 1-0. Nine minutes later, Kusi also recorded her name on the scoresheet, having been found by Yeboah’s inch-perfect cross. After holding off Ghana following the concession of the second goal, the Mauritius defense was breached again. Yeboah was on hand again with a pass to Simon, who hit a sweet ball into the top left corner to extend the Black Queens’ advantage. The Black Queens headed into the break with a three-goal advantage. After the recess, Bjorkegren tweaked his setup, introducing Nancy Amoh, Josephine Bonsu and Zakaria Ajegipina. Despite their dominance in the second department of the game, Bjorkegren’s side were unable to add to their advantage as the game finished 3-0. The second leg of the fixture is scheduled for the Accra Sports Stadium on Tuesday, October 13.

title: Marwa Commends Security Agencies Over Rescue of 20 Kidnapped Corps Members
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja The Chairman/Chief Executive of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd.), has commended the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies for the successful rescue of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and another victim abducted in the South-east. Marwa, in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Femi Babafemi, described the rescue operation as a victory for the country and evidence of what coordinated and intelligence-driven operations could achieve in the fight against criminality. He said the safe return of the prospective corps members to their families demonstrated the courage, professionalism and unity of purpose among Nigeria’s security agencies. “Our corps members are the nation’s best, serving their fatherland with hope and idealism. Nigeria owes them protection, and today our gallant men and women have delivered,” he said. Marwa, who is a retired military officer, said it was important to draw public attention to the achievements of security agencies and commend them for their efforts in protecting Nigerians. He also acknowledged other successful rescue operations conducted by security agencies across the country in recent months, saying the operations had freed abducted victims and restored hope to affected families. “Every life rescued is a triumph for our collective resolve. These operations show that criminals cannot outrun a determined and united security architecture,” he said. The NDLEA chairman further pledged the agency’s continued support and cooperation with sister security agencies, noting that illicit drug trafficking and abuse often contributed to violent crimes, kidnapping and banditry. “Where drugs flow, insecurity thrives. That is why the NDLEA will keep working with sister agencies to dismantle the networks that fund and fuel criminality, and we will deepen intelligence-sharing and joint operations,” Marwa said. He urged security agencies to sustain the momentum in the fight against criminality and called on Nigerians to support security forces by providing timely and credible information. Marwa also wished the rescued prospective corps members a speedy recovery and successful reunion with their families.

title: Sikorsky’s “Black Hawk 2070” Strategy Includes Drones, New Engines, And Flying The Pilotless U-Hawk This Year
body: The UH-60 Black Hawk has been the rugged workhorse of U.S. Army aviation for nearly 50 years, with around 4,000 examples currently in service with 36 nations worldwide. Many of these helicopters, and new aircraft coming off the line, are set to fly as far out as 2070, and Sikorsky is curating a suite of upgrades to keep them valuable assets for the future fight. A new “digital backbone” is designed to underpin swift technological insertions such as launched effects , with related initiatives including the provision of more power to lug greater payloads, and the fully-autonomous U-Hawk cargo drone variant. “As part of an overall “Black Hawk 2070” modernization effort we’re developing a number of complementary capabilities, including our U-Hawk uncrewed cargo variant, which we plan to fly later this year,” Jason Wrigley, Sikorsky’s director of business development for Black Hawk, told TWZ at the company’s Stratford plant in Connecticut. Sikorsky plans to fly its U-Hawk uncrewed cargo version of the Black Hawk this year. Sikorsky “A new digital backbone for the Black Hawk is at an advanced design phase in our labs and it’s designed to provide interfaces throughout the aircraft that will provide power, data, a network, cooling and most importantly, open architecture interfaces that enable the easy integration of new equipment, such as sensors. We see this as a core building block for the next generation of Black Hawk, along with new engines and other airframe improvements designed to futureproof the platform.” The new digital backbone is designed to work in concert with a modern, software-driven strategy that meets the Army’s Modular Open Systems Approach and the desire to add technologies cheaper, faster, and more easily. Wrigley says that as customers identify new capabilities and needs for their Black Hawks, the digital backbone will be sufficiently efficient to permit customization even on a mission-by-mission basis. Sikorsky is also introducing a new modular nose to the H-60, which is reconfigurable with sufficient volume to support even more sensors and electronics. “There’s a big focus on open architecture and that ability to quickly plug-and-play,” says Wrigley. “The new modular nose will change the look of the Black Hawk up front to provide even more space for equipment that will work directly with the new digital architecture.” The new modular nose will give the Black Hawk more than twice the internal volume of the original nose section and it’s designed to provide space for internal electronics and an integrated mount for external sensor pods. It is designed to provide sufficient space to accommodate electronics that enable roles such as search and rescue, drone control, and flying in degraded environments, and it will also house some of the equipment required as the Black Hawk’s autonomous capabilities expand. Sikorsky plans to introduce a new modular nose to the UH-60M. Sikorsky Joshua Powers spent 22 years as an Army Aviation officer flying the Black Hawk, and he’s well qualified for his new role with Sikorsky handling business development for rapid capabilities insertions. “Army units know the Black Hawk inside out; how to fly it, maintain it, and use it to maximum effect. The upgrades we are developing will bring new capabilities faster, without time-consuming and complex changes to sustainment, training, and operations, plus we are adding more range, more payload, and more power to meet the demands of the Indo-Pacific region.” “I find it amazing to pair new technology with a rugged platform like the Black Hawk. These new innovations are needed to meet the needs of the new complex battlefield. The fight I fought in Iraq is very different from the current operating environment and what future warriors are going to go up against, and what we’re asking them to do is very different from what came before.” Bringing autonomous co-pilots to the Black Hawk Autonomy is a central pillar of Sikorsky’s strategy for the future Black Hawk. The company’s MATRIX autonomy software is now being matured on a UH-60M variant, and while it’s not necessarily designed to completely replace pilots, MATRIX will assume some of their workload, making flying safer and simpler as mission sets grow increasingly complex and dangerous. “Pilots that are controlling collaborative drones, for example, need to be able to focus on the drone mission, and autonomy will help lighten their cognitive load,” explains Wrigley. “The standard Black Hawk crew operates with two pilots. Adding our MATRIX autonomy system gives the operator options – a single pilot could fly without an unbearable workload and still fulfil a mission commander role, for example. The Army could then operate the Black Hawk with no pilots at all when that’s the appropriate option.” The U.S. Army received its first UH-60MX Optionally Piloted Vehicle (OPV) on March 20, 2026. Sikorsky Sikorsky’s MATRIX autonomy has been developed on the company’s UH-60A fly-by-wire Optionally Piloted Black Hawk , which has been tested by Sikorsky and Army aviators. MATRIX has accumulated more than 1,000 flight hours across 500 tests and demonstrations. It has already been integrated on over 20 different platforms, including on the Black Hawk for testing by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) and the U.S. Army in multiple exercises . “We delivered the first UH-60MX to the Army earlier this year,” says Wrigley. The delivery marked the first full authority fly-by-wire and optionally-piloted UH-60 in the Army fleet. “They are using it for testing and soldier feedback to develop tactics, techniques and procedures for the autonomous Black Hawk. We have since received a contract to deliver three more MX aircraft to the Army.” MATRIX autonomy kits have now been installed on all three U.S. Army Black Hawk models; the UH-60A, UH-60L and UH-60M. Sikorsky plans to incorporate autonomy options into all Black Hawks as they are built, plus the MATRIX system will be able to be retrofitted to existing examples. Powers is well aware of the benefits autonomy will provide from complex combat operations to more mundane day-to-day missions. “Flying at night and seeing the tracer fire coming up at you, things like that, I honestly feel that’s not the big threat. It’s when you’re going to land and there’s just a big dust cloud. When you’re tired, you aren’t as focused. Having MATRIX, whether that’s with one, two, or no pilots, it’s about that reduced workload on the mission. Pilots won’t be as fatigued, plus they have the safety net of a fully autonomous aircraft that can, if needed, land in all of those difficult environments. It will give commanders more operational flexibility and the ability to mitigate risk in less-than-ideal conditions dictated by the enemy or weather.” The first UH-60MX during testing alongside Sikorsky’s UH-60A Optionally Piloted Black Hawk. Sikorsky “The Black Hawk operation isn’t just about pilots, it’s also that integrated four-person crew. As a pilot, you’re relying on your senses and also on the guys in the back to watch out and tell you where you’re going. MATRIX is just going to help that team effort and put you in a better position to bring the crew back safely. It integrates all the systems and sensors and uses altitude, airspeed, radar altimeter, drift indications, and puts the fly-by-wire technology to where it can make rapid adjustments and changes based on what it’s seeing with the sensors.” The volume of testing, the maturity, and the confidence in MATRIX helped Sikorsky to develop the S-70UAS, or U-Hawk, which was unveiled in 2025 . The U-Hawk project essentially removes the cockpit and its associated equipment from a Black Hawk and replaces the front end with cargo doors to provide a huge internal space as a supply drone. “We acquired a used UH-60L Black Hawk as the template for our initial U-Hawk. We added the clamshell doors and that was the actual aircraft that we showed at AUSA last year,” says Wrigley. “Since then we’ve been adding the fly-by-wire and integrating the MATRIX autonomy. It’s currently in our innovations hangar in Bridgeport, Connecticut, getting the final work done and it will make its first flight as a U-Hawk later this year.” The first U-Hawk is based on a modified UH-60L. Sikorsky Sikorsky sees the U-Hawk as a natural evolution for the Black Hawk in contested logistics missions, when cargo needs to be moved but the threat is sufficiently high that it drives a need for uncrewed platforms to tackle the mission. “We’re spending a lot of time on the U-Hawk and its roles. As well as being an uncrewed cargo helicopter, it can also be a truck that can carry a large volume of launched effects,” explains Wrigley. “There are Black Hawk models on the market right now that are being divested, and we see those as being an ideal option for conversion to U-Hawk configuration to affordably introduce this capability to the market.” Drone dispenser The integration of small drones dubbed ‘launched effects’ into rotary-wing operations is a major initiative from the Army as a new means to collect intelligence for commanders on the battlefield, relay communications, jam and distract enemy emitters, and act as loitering munitions. These mini air-launched drones can be carried and fired from stub-wing-mounted launchers , with other concepts seeing larger volumes of them carried inside the cabin as a “mega-pack,” with Sikorsky seeing both as being highly-applicable to both the Black Hawk and the U-Hawk. This is exactly the kind of capability that the digital backbone in the Black Hawk is intended to open the door to; installing plug-and-play drone command kits, which could enable the Black Hawk to act as a “drone mothership” to launch, task, and command swarms of multi-mission launched effects. A Launched Effect-Medium Range is fired from a UH-60M Black Hawk during Project Convergence-Capstone 6, in July 2026. U.S. Army The Army tested its latest operational concepts for launched effects during the Project Convergence Capstone 6 demonstration event this summer. This annual exercise is designed to develop concepts and tactics as well as gather soldier feedback, as it works to transition new systems into service. The latest exercise built on previous launched effects testing on the Black Hawk, when a UH-60M deployed Anduril’s Altius-700 launched effects that then operated as an autonomous hunter-killer team to locate targets, share data on those targets, and then strike them, without the need for the Black Hawk to expose itself to threats. “As a young Black Hawk pilot, the OH-58 Kiowa Warrior was the primary scout platform, but it was limited by range and its ability to be detected,” explains Joshua Powers. “Today, we launch small drones that can remain unseen and they can give us real-time feedback. Launched effects make our lift assets more capable.” “We see the Black Hawk as the aircraft capable of carrying, deploying and then acting as an airborne mission command node for launched effects,” adds Jason Wrigley. “In the operational environment of the future, it’s really about the mass of those launched effects. This isn’t about carrying one or two of them, this is about carrying and controlling a large number of them.” A “quiver” of launched effects inside the U-Hawk shown at the AUSA 2026 trade event. Jamie Hunter “We’ve tested them on the stub-wings, but we are also exploring what we call “quiver” – that large number of launched effects inside the cabin in that “mega-pack.” This creates additional opportunities for mass that we think is going to be really critical. We’ve done a lot of operational analysis in concert with the Army on what the right mix of launched effects might be to extend the standoff range of the aircraft to improve survivability – which is of course what it’s all about – but the right mix will ultimately come down to the mission. We have seen a lot of testing over the past few years, so we do believe this is a capability that can be introduced operationally soon on the Black Hawk.” More power for more missions To support the increased lift that might be needed for a missionized Black Hawk lugging large payloads, including an arsenal of launched effects, Sikorsky is well along in development of a new engine that is designed to create over 1,000 pounds of increased payload capacity and increased range for the Black Hawk. The T901 Improved Turbine Engine (ITE) from GE Aerospace provides 50 percent more horsepower over the existing T700 engines in the UH-60M. “One of the key building blocks of the future of the Black Hawk are the twin ITEs as we look to expand the mission capability and the utility of this aircraft for decades to come,” explains Wrigley. Sikorsky began initial testing of the first UH-60M with ITE in January 2025. “We are actively in the test program right now at our test facility in West Palm Beach, Florida. The twin ITEs in each Black Hawk and that additional power translates into some pretty significant operational opportunities. Since our first flight with ITE in May 2025 we’ve flown the aircraft with the new engine for over 50 hours and up to 17,000 ft above sea level.” A UH-60M fitted with twin GE Aerospace T901 Improved Turbine Engines (ITE). Sikorsky Sikorsky is accompanying the addition of the new engines with a significant expansion of the fuel tank to increase capacity and range. This is being done without impinging on cabin volume and thus retaining the important ability to transport 11 combat troops, while increasing range by around 100 nautical miles. “The T901 also improves fuel efficiency and eases maintenance – so overall we are really improving the payload capacity of the aircraft. We’ll be getting to the milestone C production decision on ITE within the next couple of years, and at that point it will become a core element of the Black Hawk program going forward,” Wrigley explains. Building Black Hawks Touring the Black Hawk production line in Stratford, Connecticut, it’s a hive of activity. Many of the major components for each helicopter are manufactured here. The long final assembly line sees teams of workers busily constructing UH-60M and HH-60M medevac Black Hawks for both domestic and foreign military sales customers, along with new HH-60W Combat Rescue Helicopters for the U.S. Air Force and MH-60R Seahawks . “We’re designing all of these upgrades with the intent that they will all be available off the production line in new build aircraft, as well as in kit form for upgrades to existing assets in the field,” notes Wrigley. “Here in Stratford in what we call the “back shop” we build all the rotor blades, gearboxes, and many other components that go into each aircraft. We are already thinking ahead and we’ve invested significantly into additive manufacturing, with 11 parts on the Black Hawk today that are additively manufactured. It’s a great place to start, but there’s a long way to go and we’re working on qualifying more challenging components and load-bearing parts.” A brand new UH-60M in pre-delivery testing. Sikorsky Cohesively, the digital backbone, larger fuel tank, new engines, and the new modular nose will all be introduced on the production floor in the coming years to pave the way for that increased payload capacity to carry fully-equipped combat troops, supplies, and all the new kit needed for the future fight and the Black Hawk’s role as a multi-mission forward battlefield node. The autonomous U-Hawk and the optionally piloted flexibility afforded by MATRIX – all of these pieces of the future Black Hawk are presently coming together under an overarching effort. “The future Black Hawk will be that complement to the future long-range MV-75 Cheyenne II,” says Powers. “These won’t be a one-for-one replacement for every Black Hawk currently in the fleet – the MV-75 has a specific purpose and function that the Black Hawk isn’t designed to do. What the Black Hawk can do with these new upgrades is shape the battlefield and with its autonomy be out there flying missions into contested environments.” U.S. Army UH-60 Black Hawks assigned to 4th Ranger Training Battalion. U.S. Army “Those homeland missions are equally necessary. I recall talking about this in flight school when choosing an aircraft to fly, how it’s one thing to be deployed on combat missions, but it’s also about being back in the homeland on disaster relief when you need the Black Hawk to go out and save lives, those kinds of missions the Army National Guard does – it really underlines the importance and versatility of the Black Hawk.” Over the past 50 years and looking ahead to the next 50, continuing the proven legacy of the Black Hawk will mean constant evolution to meet new missions and needs. Sikorsky’s task is for all of these new elements to meld into a future Black Hawk that’s ready to roll off this production line soon, that still also provides the same dependable, rugged capability for the Army at home or overseas, well into the future. title: Houthis report new strikes on Saudi airports, air base
body:
DOHA, October 8. /TASS/. Yemen’s rebel Ansar Allah movement - the Houthis - attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh once again and struck Najran Airport and an air base in Khamis Mushait, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated.
"This evening, our armed forces (Houthi armed formations – TASS) attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with two cruise missiles, Najran Airport with a ballistic missile, and the air base in Khamis Mushait, also with a ballistic missile," Saree said in a statement published on his Telegram channel. He added that the attacks damaged the facilities and suspended air traffic at both airports.
Earlier on Thursday, the Houthi spokesman had already reported a ballistic missile strike on the airport in Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition, for its part, reported intercepting three missiles heading toward the kingdom’s capital and Khamis Mushait, while Saudi Civil Defense said debris fell on a kindergarten building and a medical complex in Riyadh.

title: UG academic calendar could collapse if GAUA strike extends into next week – Awandare
body: The University of Ghana’s 2026/2027 academic calendar could be severely disrupted if the ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) extends into next week, Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Gordon Awandare has warned. Prof. Awandare said several critical university systems are currently not functioning because they are managed by GAUA members who are participating in the industrial action. “The reality is that currently many of the systems are not working because they are managed by members of GAUA who are on strike,” he said. “So the university can only do so much in terms of what we can make available in the absence of GAUA people.” Speaking on Thursday, October 8, as the strike continued, Prof. Awandare said management was doing its best under the circumstances but acknowledged that the disruption was affecting the university’s operations. He appealed to the government to urgently resolve the impasse to prevent further disruption to the academic year. “What we would like to appeal for is that the government should try to resolve this as soon as possible so that the academic calendar is not disrupted so badly,” he said. He added: “Because if this goes into next week, then it means that the academic calendar is basically gone and we have to reorganize.” The warning comes after the University of Ghana suspended first-semester registration for the 2026/2027 academic year because of the strike. In a notice to students, management apologised for the difficulties with online registration and attributed them to the ongoing industrial action by university administrators. “Management of the University of Ghana wishes to apologise to our cherished students, Level 100 and continuing students, for the current challenges with online registration for the first semester of the 2026-2027 academic year, which are caused by the ongoing industrial action by the university administrators.” The disruption has affected students’ access to key administrative services, including registration and other university systems. GAUA has been on strike for more than two months following failed negotiations with the government over the payment of negotiated and approved allowances. The association is also demanding action on what it describes as disparities in allowances and conditions of service. National General Secretary of GAUA, Charles Jojo Aidoo, said the association had been negotiating with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission for about two months without significant progress. “None of our grievances have been addressed. We had about six, seven grievances, and none of them has been addressed. The majority of them are not even monetary,” he said. Mr Aidoo said GAUA represents professionals working in various capacities within universities, including medical doctors, lawyers, chartered accountants, auditors and procurement specialists. “From 2008, we don’t have any conditions of service,” he said. The University of Ghana’s academic calendar scheduled Level 100 students to report from October 12 to 13, while continuing students were expected to report from October 15 to 18. Teaching was scheduled to begin on October 19. However, with key administrative systems affected and registration suspended, the university’s ability to maintain the existing calendar is increasingly dependent on the resolution of the GAUA strike. GAUA first declared the strike on August 10 but later suspended the action after Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu assured members that their concerns would be addressed. The industrial action resumed after negotiations stalled. The association has maintained that it remains open to negotiations and could call off the strike if meaningful progress is made on its outstanding concerns. The disruption at the University of Ghana comes amid a wider wave of industrial action in Ghana’s education sector, with a teachers’ strike also affecting teaching and learning in some basic and secondary schools. Parents have expressed concern about the impact of the disruptions on students. “I have invested a lot for my kids, and honestly speaking, I feel so much sad for this outcome, that after all the investment, my child will not go to school to learn,” one parent said. For now, the University of Ghana has not announced a revised academic calendar. But Prof. Awandare’s warning means the October 19 start of teaching could be affected if the GAUA strike continues into next week.

title: Zelensky, Costa discuss Russian strikes, EU aid, opening of negotiating clusters
body:
The Ukrainian President said this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“I spoke with President of the European Council António Costa. I am grateful to António for his clear and principled stance in condemning Russian strikes against our people and for his condolences,” he said.
The head of state recalled that in recent days alone, Russian strikes on Pryluky and Kramatorsk, Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities had killed 78 people and injured 215.
“This is a brutal Russian escalation – terror against people and life. And it is important that leaders do not ignore what is happening,” Zelensky said.
He also expressed gratitude for the €1.2 billion tranche that Ukraine received yesterday. The President assured that the funds would be used for defense, including drones.
“We are working to secure other necessary decisions as well. We discussed the timeline for opening the next negotiating clusters, the winter energy package, and further financial support. We agreed to meet in the near future – the three of us: António Costa, Ursula von der Leyen, and I,” Zelensky stressed.
He also briefed Costa on contacts and meetings with the U.S. side that will take place in the coming days.
“Our team is already on its way. We appreciate Europe's support,” the President concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, European Council President António Costa expects the European Union to open two negotiating clusters on Ukraine’s EU accession as early as next week, with the remaining clusters to be opened by the end of this year.

title: Crew Dragon spacecraft returns to Earth
body:
NEW YORK, October 8. /TASS/. A SpaceX spacecraft carrying the Crew-12 mission team, including Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyayev, has returned to Earth from the International Space Station (ISS). The landing was broadcast live on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
The spacecraft splashed down off the coast of California at 08:34 local time. The journey from the orbital station to Earth took the crew approximately 27 hours.
The Crew-12 team had been aboard the ISS since mid-February. Fedyayev’s fellow crew members were NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, as well as European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot.
On October 4, Meir handed over command of the orbital station to Roscosmos cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov.

title: Black Sherif partners with Telecel Ghana to promote Telecel Cash
body: Telecel Ghana has unveiled musician Black Sherif as the face of its X Project, a partnership designed to strengthen engagement with young consumers and promote its mobile money service, Telecel Cash. The collaboration, announced on October 8, 2026, will feature events, promotional activities and surprise customer rewards over the next year. Black Sherif, widely known as Blacko, will lead customer engagement activities around Telecel Cash. The company says his role will extend beyond a traditional brand ambassador arrangement to include creating experiences that connect customers with the platform. Speaking at the unveiling, Telecel Ghana’s Chief Executive Officer, Ing. Patricia Obo-Nai, said the partnership brings together brands that appeal to young people and share values of authenticity and resilience. She said the musician’s talent and personal journey resonate with young Ghanaians, making him a suitable partner for the initiative. Ing. Obo-Nai encouraged Telecel Cash customers to follow Black Sherif for announcements about upcoming activities and opportunities to receive rewards. Customers will require a Telecel Cash wallet and the Telecel Play app to participate in the programme. At the unveiling, the company also reminded users to protect their accounts against fraud by keeping their passwords, PINs and passcodes confidential, including from anyone claiming to represent Telecel. The initiative forms part of Telecel Ghana’s efforts to expand engagement with younger customers and encourage greater use of its digital and mobile money services.

title: 2027: APC North Central plans mega rally for Tinubu, Shettima
body: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress, APC, in the North Central has announced plans to hold a mega rally in Lafia, Nasarawa State, on Saturday, October 10, in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general elections. The rally, organised under the auspices of the North Central Grassroots Mobilisation Network, will be hosted by Nasarawa State Governor, Engr. Abdullahi Sule, while the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, is expected to headline the event. The APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday after a high-level meeting of North Central APC stakeholders in Abuja. The meeting was attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume; governors and deputy governors from the region; ministers; members of the National Assembly and other political office holders. Yilwatda said the stakeholders had resolved to mobilise their respective political structures and supporters across the six North Central states and the Federal Capital Territory for the Lafia rally. He described the planned gathering as the “mother of all rallies”, saying it would demonstrate the region’s support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket ahead of the 2027 elections. According to him, the meeting also focused on strengthening coordination among party leaders and grassroots structures to ensure effective mobilisation across the region. He said the stakeholders acknowledged Akume’s leadership in bringing together political leaders from the North Central and commended Governor Sule for agreeing to host the rally in Nasarawa State. The stakeholders also reviewed arrangements for the participation of party leaders, women, youths, grassroots organisations and supporters from across the region, while reaffirming their commitment to a successful rally. Yilwatda further expressed condolences to the families of victims of the recent Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Ondo State and those who died in the recent mining-related tragedy in Niger State. He described the incidents as painful losses and sympathised with the affected families and communities. title: Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take
body: Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take Two years after Ismael Zambada Garcia, alias “El Mayo,” was handed over to US authorities in what was deemed a traitorous act by one faction against another, the war between the Chapitos and the Mayiza factions of the Sinaloa Cartel continues to roil the area. The conflict has implications for the criminal superstructure throughout the country. InSight Crime’s Victoria Dittmar and co-director Steven Dudley were recently in Culiacán, Sinaloa, where they interviewed drug producers, residents, and local sources. They found a city where the war is less visible than it was but no less present. In this episode of The InSight Take, managing editor Deborah Bonello talks to them about what that shift actually means for the two factions and for the people of Sinaloa. Below is a summary of their conversation. SEE ALSO: Criminal Profiles of the Sinaloa Cartel, and the Chapitos and Mayiza Factions. What is happening in Culiacán right now? The visible signs of cartel presence such as lookouts, branded caps, and narcocorridos have largely disappeared from the city. But it is not clear if that is a permanent shift or just temporary until a new faction becomes dominant. The nature of the violence has changed, not stopped. Instead of the open shootouts of the war’s first phase, there are more targeted killings. Nonetheless, during their visit, there was a mass shooting at a local Chinese restaurant in the city center where the target appeared to be a local narcocorrido singer. Locals have changed their lives to steer clear of the fighting and not appear to be taking sides. Residents described running a daily security calculation before leaving home. Businesses close their doors early. Nightlife has waned but is sputtering back to life, slowly. Who is winning the Sinaloa Cartel war? There appears to be one major winner: Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “ Chapo Isidro .” He spent years out of the public eye before this conflict, and now he may emerge as the top dog. The fighting has shifted south toward Mazatlán and the Nayarit border. These routes may be worth more to these groups. The war, two years going, has been costly for all sides, and the factions may be getting desperate, looking for sources of revenue in predatory ways. Is this the end of the Sinaloa Cartel? The Sinaloa Cartel is not done. It is more of a reconfiguration of its board of directors. This is the Sinaloa Cartel’s third factional war in the last 20 years. There will be others, but locals say the larger criminal structure is intact. The post Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take appeared first on InSight Crime .

title: Ukraine remains priority issue for EU summit – Costa's letter to leaders
body:
European Union leaders will discuss both Ukraine's urgent needs in countering Russian aggression and its progress toward EU membership.
European Council President António Costa announced this agenda item for the European Council meeting, scheduled for October 15–16 in Brussels, in an invitation letter to EU leaders. The text of the letter was released on Thursday.
“Ukraine remains a key priority for the European Union. We will reaffirm our continued support to Ukraine in the face of Russia’s war of aggression. Considering Russia’s escalating attacks on critical infrastructure, it will be important to hear from President Zelenskyy on the country’s operational needs ahead of the coming winter,” the letter says.
Costa also announced that during the meeting, leaders would assess Ukraine's progress toward EU accession, "that hopefully new negotiating clusters will have already been opened by then."
The President of the European Council identified another issue “increasingly reckless behaviour by Russia, including its campaign of hybrid attacks across Europe.” “We stand united and determined in the face of this escalation and will continue to advance our defence readiness agenda. Building on our previous work, we will take stock of implementation to maintain momentum and accelerate progress across all work strands, including on addressing critical military capability gaps,” he emphasized.
According to Costa, another discussion will focus on enlargement and reform, based on the Commission's communication "Preparing for a wider Union." “Our debate will provide strategic guidance on the way forward. It will specifically highlight the ongoing work on the accession Treaty with Montenegro, and the aim to conclude negotiations with that candidate country hopefully by the end of this year,” he noted.
In addition, the issue of migration has been put forward for discussion. “The figures show that our comprehensive approach is working, as evidenced by a significant and sustained decrease in arrivals of irregular migrants. Adopted EU legislation is producing results. However, we must remain vigilant and prepared, act in solidarity when Member States face crisis situations and continue the work to improve our ability to deal with crises, including all cases of instrumentalization,” Costa emphasized.
The President of the European Council also announced that, at the meeting, EU leaders will “focus on the economy, and on delivering answers to challenges to European competitiveness and to affordability.” “For the short-term, we need to provide guidance to the Commission on targeted and temporary measures to alleviate the impact of high energy prices on our citizens and businesses – while continuing to pursue our strategy to reduce Europe’s dependence of fossil fuels,” he wrote.
Furthermore, Costa proposed to the leaders, together with the President of the European Parliament, that they review the implementation of the overarching competitiveness strategy for 2026–2027, known as the "One Europe, One Market" agenda. “I know this is a major priority for all the Leaders and the Irish Presidency is working hard to achieve results. We need to ensure that additional progress is made, so that the ambition at Leaders’ level – and the expectations that have been raised – are matched by concrete outcomes. These outcomes must translate into tangible opportunities for our companies, our start-ups and our citizens,” the President of the European Council said.

title: Court reserves ruling on Taraba APC chairmanship primary dispute
body:
The Federal High Court in Jalingo, Taraba State, has reserved ruling in a suit challenging the exclusion of Abdulhadi Haruna Lau from the All Progressives Congress (APC) state chairmanship primary.
Justice Mashkur Salisu reserved ruling on Wednesday after lawyers representing the parties adopted their arguments in the case.
Mr Lau is asking the court to invalidate the primary, arguing that he was qualified to contest but was prevented from participating despite completing the processes required by the party.
His lawyer, Musa Attah, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), told the court that Mr Lau paid the required fees and was issued a receipt but was subsequently denied the form needed to contest the election.
“He was denied the form to contest after paying the money,” Mr Attah argued.
The lawyer also urged the court to reject the argument that the dispute was purely an internal matter of the APC and therefore beyond judicial intervention.
He argued that the circumstances surrounding Mr Lau’s exclusion raised issues capable of being examined by the court because they affected his participation in the party’s electoral process.
The APC, through its counsel, Festus Kayode, SAN, urged the court to dismiss the suit.
Mr Kayode argued that the documents placed before the court had been properly executed and that the dispute concerned the internal administration of the political party.
He maintained that the court lacked jurisdiction to interfere with the party’s decision on the eligibility of an aspirant to contest its internal election.
Counsel to the second defendant, John Okezie, also opposed the suit.
Mr Okezie argued that although Mr Lau paid for the aspiration form, he failed to fulfil another financial requirement prescribed by the party.
He specifically alleged that the plaintiff did not pay the ‘penalty’ fee required under the APC constitution.
The defence further argued that Mr Lau failed to produce evidence of payment of the penalty fee or documentation from the APC National Working Committee confirming his eligibility to participate in the primary.
The opposing arguments have left two major questions for determination: whether Mr Lau fulfilled all the requirements to contest the APC chairmanship position and whether the Federal High Court has jurisdiction to intervene in the party’s decision to exclude him from the primary.
Mr Lau’s legal team maintains that he completed the necessary procedures and was denied the opportunity to contest without a valid justification.
The APC and the second defendant, however, contend that he failed to meet the party’s requirements and that the court should not interfere in the party’s internal affairs.
With the parties having concluded their arguments, Justice Salisu reserved ruling in the matter.
The date for the ruling is expected to be communicated to the parties by the court.

title: Nestlé Ghana expands Tema factory, raises evaporated milk production capacity
body: Nestlé Ghana has expanded its Tema factory with a new evaporated milk production line, significantly increasing the company’s capacity to manufacture one of its major products locally. The new line, commissioned by President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday, October 8, 2026, replaces a production line that had been in operation for more than 30 years. The expansion will increase the factory’s annual evaporated milk production capacity from approximately 12,960 tonnes to nearly 30,000 tonnes. The upgraded facility will undertake the filling, homogenisation, sterilisation and packaging of milk locally, with the processes carried out by Ghanaian workers. President Mahama, who commissioned the facility, described the investment as an important demonstration of Ghana’s capacity to produce more of what it consumes and strengthen local manufacturing. He said the expansion was also consistent with the government’s 24-hour economy initiative, which seeks to promote continuous production, increase industrial activity and create jobs. The President urged Nestlé to leverage Ghana’s position as the headquarters of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to expand its reach into markets across the continent. He said the expanded production line gives the company the capacity to increase its contribution to Ghana’s ambition of becoming a production hub for Africa. President Mahama also stressed the importance of protecting local manufacturers from illicit imports and customs evasion, particularly as domestic production capacity increases. The Nestlé Tema factory has been in operation since 1970 and produces a range of products for the Ghanaian market and export markets across Central and West Africa. The expansion comes amid renewed industrial activity in Tema, which President Mahama says is gradually regaining its position as Ghana’s major industrial centre. He cited developments including the expansion of the Tema Port, efforts to revive the Tema Oil Refinery and ongoing work to restore the Volta Aluminium Company (VALCO) as part of the industrial activity taking place in the enclave. The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, also highlighted growing investment activity in Ghana, saying foreign direct investment inflows increased from US$652 million in 2024 to US$2.62 billion in 2025. She said the manufacturing sector recorded the highest number of new investment projects in 2025, with 99 projects , ahead of mining, oil and gas, and general trade. The expansion of Nestlé’s Tema factory therefore adds to the growing push for increased domestic manufacturing, value addition and export-oriented production in Ghana.

title: Future cost, use of Marine Corps ACVs scrutinized in congressional report
body: With today’s armored vehicles vulnerable to drones, congressional researchers are raising questions about the U.S. Marine Corps’ new Amphibious Combat Vehicle . In particular, a Congressional Research Service report , released Tuesday, pointed to the war in Ukraine, where armored vehicles have largely been driven from the battlefield by unmanned aerial vehicles and guided munitions. “As ACVs are intended to provide organic, direct fire support to dismounted Marines in the attack, how vulnerable to these threat systems are ACVs during amphibious operations and when operating ashore to support combat operations?” the research service asked in its report. “Are the Marines considering additional ACV survivability modifications based on lessons learned in Ukraine?” In fact, the Marine Corps did award a contract last month to Anduril for a counter-UAS system to protect the ACV from small drones. Anduril’s Pulsar-L is a sensor and jammer package designed to stop small Group 1 and 2 radio-frequency drones. “The system is currently in use by the Special Operations Command due to the system’s low weight, proven performance in engaging multiple UASs, and simultaneous execution of the full kill-chain while static or on the move,” noted the Marine contract award. The Congressional Research Service also questioned whether a possible plan to expand the Marine Corps would, in turn, require more ACVs, which cost about $6 million each, depending on the variant. Last month, a Force Structure Review suggested adding more than 6,500 personnel by 2032, including additional slots in 19 infantry battalions and two Littoral Combat Teams. If the plan is implemented, “would additional ACVs be required to accommodate growth in Marine infantry units?” CRS asked. The ACV comes in multiple variants, including the ACV-P troop carrier, ACV-C command vehicle, ACV-30 fire support model armed with a 30mm cannon, and the ACV-R armored recovery vehicle. Initially, the Marines envisioned buying 1,122 ACVs. But the current plan is for 608 vehicles, comprising 389 ACV-P, 33 ACV-C, 152 ACV-30 and 34 ACV-R, Marine Corps officials told CRS. BAE was just awarded a $230 million contract modification for 32 ACV-Rs, which will be the final ACV variant. The order is scheduled to be fulfilled by November 2028. For fiscal 2027, the Navy is requesting $237 million for ACV upgrades. The ACV has already experienced teething pains. After two ACVs tipped over in 2022 while operating in surf up to 10 feet high, the Marines briefly suspended ACV operations in the open ocean, as long as significant breaker height doesn’t exceed four feet. One issue is the weight of the ACV, which now stands at around 35 tons. In 2025, a Navy Small Business Innovation Research solicitation called for reducing the weight of all ACV variants, and particularly the heavier ACV-30 and ACV-R. The goal is to slim down at least 2,000 pounds per vehicle. “Components identified as having potential for weight reduction include engine access covers, drive shafts, ramp door, ramp, hatches, external fuel tanks, external metallic and metallic/composite add-on-armor components, suspension, turret exterior panels, and bow plane,” the 2025 solicitation stated. Saltwater corrosion of ACV struts has also created problems. “The high deployment schedule combined with the high training tempo of the United States Marine Corps creates an extremely corrosive environment for the ACV not typically experienced by other vehicles,” claimed a January 2026 Sources Sought notice for more than 5,000 corrosion-resistant struts. In addition, the weight reduction SBIR specified that any solution “must address corrosion issues expected from use in and around salt water. Weight reduction will improve fuel efficiency and can lower the Center of Gravity and Center of Buoyancy.”

title: 2027: Collect PVCs, vote out APC, APM candidate tells Ogun voters
body: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — The governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, in Ogun State, Rotimi Babajide, has urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, and vote massively for the party in the 2027 general elections. Babajide made the call on Thursday in Abeokuta at a town hall meeting organised by the party ahead of the elections. The candidate accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of worsening the hardship faced by residents over the past 12 years and urged voters to reject the party at the polls. He appealed to eligible voters to participate actively in the electoral process, saying the APM had solutions to what he described as the challenges confronting the state. Babajide also cautioned residents against selling their votes, urging them to use their PVCs to elect candidates capable of improving their welfare. Addressing hundreds of party supporters, the town planner unveiled part of his blueprint for Ogun State, promising equal access to education through digital tools for pupils and students in public and private schools. He also pledged to run an inclusive, people-centred administration with emphasis on women and youths. Babajide said, “This poverty is too much, this hunger is too much in the land. Let’s vote out poverty, let’s vote out hunger. “My administration will focus on women and youths and run an inclusive government that prioritises the people. “Every facility and government benefit will go down to everybody in Ogun State. We will ensure equality across all schools and communities. “Ogun State is endowed with limestone and is now officially recognised as an oil-producing state. The state’s development plan is unquestionable and will bring prosperity.” He urged voters to use the state’s large voting population to effect political change, saying Ogun had more than three million registered voters. “Vote out poverty; this poverty is too much, this hunger is too much. Let’s vote out poverty, let’s vote out hunger. Let’s vote APM. “We are going to focus on our women, we are going to focus on our youths, and we are going to have an inclusive government. This is a people-centric Ogun,” he said. On agriculture, Babajide lamented what he described as the decline of Nigeria’s agricultural system, attributing it to rural-urban migration and the abandonment of farming for white-collar jobs. He said an APM administration would make agriculture more attractive and inclusive, using cassava as a symbol of what he described as an agricultural revolution in Ogun State. Earlier, the state chairman of the party, Comrade Abayomi Sanyaolu, criticised the APC over what he described as excessive spending on political campaigns while basic amenities remained inadequate in many communities. Sanyaolu questioned the rationale behind spending billions of naira on campaigns for governorship, senatorial and House of Representatives positions when citizens were still struggling to access basic necessities. “You are wasting billions of naira to campaign to contest for governor, to contest for House of Representatives, to contest for Senate. Why not provide basic amenities such as potable water for citizens? Give us good water,” he said. The party chairman also cautioned voters against selling their votes for small amounts of money, urging them to consider the long-term consequences of their choices at the ballot box. The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, is scheduled to commence nationwide collection of PVCs on Friday ahead of the 2027 general elections. title: Blackbeard Hypersonic Missile Shown Being Fired From Ground Launcher
body: Castelion has released what appears to be the first image of its relatively ‘cheap’ Blackbeard hypersonic missile being fired from a ground launcher, providing a new look at the containerized launch architecture now under development for the U.S. Army. The photograph, posted by Castelion on X, shows a Blackbeard missile leaving a launcher mounted on a high-mobility truck chassis. While the missile itself is by now a familiar sight , the new image offers a first public glimpse of how Castelion intends to package and operate the ground-launched version of Blackbeard, known as Blackbeard GL. Container-compatible Blackbeard. Built to move with the fight. pic.twitter.com/OzWbiChCPQ — Castelion (@Castelion) October 8, 2026 The Army’s previously disclosed plans for the program call for an initial Blackbeard ground-launch demonstration using a modified Multiple Launch Rocket System Family of Munitions , or MFOM, pod, followed by the development of Blackbeard GL prototypes and a dedicated launcher pod. Ultimately, the service intends to conduct an MVP flight test using the M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System ’s (HIMARS) fire-control system. Blackbeard for HIMARS. pic.twitter.com/uA9XgcGvsI — Castelion (@Castelion) August 3, 2026 The Army’s Fiscal Year 2027 budget documentation indicates that this effort is moving toward increasingly representative hardware. Among the milestones listed for FY2027 is a live-fire launch of a “production representative” Blackbeard GL and launcher pod. Castelion has already released extensive imagery of Blackbeard test vehicles, and the company formally unveiled the weapon’s current external configuration earlier this year . Those images showed a two-stage arrangement with a booster and an upper vehicle that has characteristics consistent with a hypersonic glide or maneuvering payload. Compared to the air-launched version, seen below, the ground-launch model lacks the cruciform tailfins at the rear of the lower stage, but otherwise appears similar. The first official photo of the Blackbeard missile. Castelion The precise propulsion system and flight profile of the production weapon remain undisclosed. Little is known about its performance parameters, either. Castelion has previously hinted that the missile could strike targets at ranges of just under 500 miles, although its range would likely be reduced when launched from the ground, without the altitude and speed provided by an aircraft launch platform. The launcher appears to use a relatively compact enclosed container, consistent with the Army’s stated interest in leveraging the existing MFOM ecosystem and, eventually, HIMARS. The photograph doesn’t establish how many Blackbeards could be carried by a single launcher, although, based on the dimensions, at least two and perhaps as many as four missiles appears a feasible load. A mock-up of an ATACMS missile next to one of a standardized MFOM. U.S. Army Exactly how closely the pictured launcher corresponds to the eventual production Blackbeard GL pod is also not yet clear. Castelion has previously stressed that its test hardware is deliberately designed to support rapid development cycles and should not necessarily be interpreted as representative of the final weapon system. Castelion had previously shown Blackbeard-related test articles alongside palletized launch equipment, including launch hardware mounted on an Oshkosh MKR18 Logistics Vehicle System Replacement truck. The company has also said it was converting such a vehicle into a launcher for flight testing. That appears to be the vehicle shown in the new image, too. A test article that Castelion has used in previous testing related to Blackbeard in front of a palletized launcher loaded on a truck. Castelion Corporation The Army’s interest in Blackbeard GL is rooted in cost as much as performance. The service has described the weapon as an affordable, mass-produced hypersonic precision-fire capability intended to engage time-sensitive moving and hardened targets. The stated objective has been to obtain roughly 80 percent of the capability of the Army’s planned Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) Increment 4 while achieving a substantially lower cost per round. Existing U.S. hypersonic weapons such as the Army’s Dark Eagle Long Range Hypersonic Weapon use large, highly specialized launch equipment. Blackbeard is instead being developed around the idea that a hypersonic weapon can be sufficiently compact, inexpensive, and manufacturable to be treated more like a conventional tactical munition. The U.S. Army’s Dark Eagle Long Range Hypersonic Weapon assigned to Bravo Battery, 5th Battalion, 3rd Field Artillery (Long Range Fires Battalion), 1st Multi-Domain Task Force, participates in an exercise on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington. U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Brandon Rickert Staff Sgt. Brandon Rickert A containerized launcher compatible with an existing mobile fires ecosystem would reinforce that concept. It could allow the Army to introduce a new hypersonic effect without creating an entirely separate launcher, crew, transport, and reload architecture. The ground-launched version is only one part of Castelion’s broader Blackbeard effort. The company is also working with the Navy to integrate the weapon onto the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet . In April, Castelion received a $105 million Navy contract supporting integration and the transition toward an early operational capability, while a subsequent $23.4 million order covered 50 early-operational-capability pre-production missiles and associated storage and shipping containers. A pair of Blackbeard hypersonic missiles mounted on a Super Hornet during a developmental test flight on September 18, 2026. Edited photo from PAE(A) U.S. Defense Media Activity/Edited photo from PAE(A) The Navy has since moved into additional procurement, underscoring Castelion’s effort to establish Blackbeard as a weapon that can be produced in the quantities required. Blackbeard could also find its way onto Navy ships and submarines, as well as ground-based launchers, as we have discussed in the past . As for the Army, the next major milestone will be the planned production-representative Blackbeard GL and launcher-pod live-fire testing. An earlier Blackbeard-related test launch. Castelion “Once Castelion achieves testing and validation, the Department will award a two-year multi-year procurement contract for a minimum of 500 Blackbeard missiles annually, with options to extend for up to five years,” the Pentagon announced in May of this year. “To further encourage Castelion’s self-funded facility expansion, the Department is actively seeking the necessary authorizations and appropriations to purchase over 12,000 Blackbeard missiles over five years.” This reflects a broader and accelerating U.S. military push for lower-cost precision weapons that can be manufactured relatively simply and at scale, increasingly with help from non-traditional defense contractors . The goal is to build large stockpiles affordably before a major contingency, particularly a potential large-scale conflict with China in the Pacific, while ensuring production can keep pace with demand during a prolonged war. For now, Castelion has demonstrated what the Army’s Blackbeard launch system actually looks like when it fires, at least in its initial form. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Blackbeard Hypersonic Missile Shown Being Fired From Ground Launcher appeared first on TWZ .

title: FG announces 30-day petrol discount for transporters at NNPC filling stations
body: The Federal Government has announced a 30-day discount on petrol sold by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPCL, with public transport operators to receive priority under the arrangement. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed this on Thursday during a press briefing on petrol prices and subsidy-related issues in Abuja. Oyedele said the measure was not a return to petrol subsidy, explaining that the government would instead allow NNPCL to sell the product at cost during the period. He said the discount would initially run for 30 days, with public transport operators prioritised nationwide. “We are offering a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for the next 30 days in the first instance with priority for public transporters nationwide. So, it’s not a subsidy; the government is just saying we sell to you at cost,” Oyedele said. The announcement comes amid variations in petrol prices at NNPCL stations across the country. According to NNPCL’s latest reported price list, petrol sells for N1,355 per litre in Lagos and Rivers states, while the pump price in Abuja is listed at N1,370 per litre. The government’s latest intervention is expected to provide some relief to public transport operators and other beneficiaries during the 30-day period. title: Why I keep studying despite my football career – Taiwo Awoniyi
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria and Coventry City striker Taiwo Awoniyi has revealed that a promise he made to his father is the reason he has continued studying throughout his football career. Awoniyi made the revelation in an interview with BBC Sport after graduating from the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Business School. The 29-year-old striker, who recently graduated from the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Business School, said his latest qualification is his third, having previously obtained a degree in business management and another diploma. “I’ve got a degree in business management and another diploma, so this is my third qualification,” he told BBC Sport. Awoniyi said his father, Solomon, always placed strong emphasis on education, even while he was pursuing a career in football. “I say to people I’m a quiet dreamer. I always felt education was important. It was a promise I made to my dad that if I played football, I would keep studying. “That is what I’ve done and I am proud of it,” he said. Awoniyi, who joined Coventry City from Nottingham Forest this summer, has continued his studies alongside his professional football career. He said the ups and downs he has experienced in football have also reinforced the importance of developing himself beyond the sport. The striker suffered a serious injury in May 2025 after colliding with a goalpost during Nottingham Forest’s Premier League match against Leicester City. He was subsequently placed in a medically induced coma after rupturing his intestine. Awoniyi said footballers have enough time to pursue other interests despite the demands of their careers. “It’s not like a 9-5 job in football. We go in and sometimes finish quite early and, although it is challenging, I think every footballer has time in the evening for something like this business school. “Of course it demands a lot from you, so it is all about how willing you are to do it,” he said. The Nigeria international also stressed that football should not be seen as the entirety of a player’s life. “I say to people there are a lot of things that are bigger than football. Yes, football is our passion but we are normal human beings as well – and maybe that’s something the world doesn’t always see.” The PFA Business School course is designed to run alongside professional football, with seminars scheduled to minimise clashes with matches and training sessions while allowing players to study in their own time. For now, Awoniyi remains focused on his football career, but his latest qualification adds to an academic journey he says began with a promise to his father. title: Telecel Ghana launches CARE Month with customer rewards and community outreach
body: Telecel Ghana has launched its annual CARE Month for October 2026, with activities aimed at rewarding customers, supporting employees and extending educational and health services to communities. The programme coincides with Global Customer Service Week and adopts the global theCARE me, “The Extra Mile”, alongside the company’s own theme, “CARE That Counts”. Throughout October, customers will benefit from appreciation visits, surprises and rewards at retail outlets, loyalty redemption campaigns and service engagements for individual and business clients. Mercy Dawn Akude, General Manager, Customer Operations at Telecel Ghana, said the initiative seeks to translate customer appreciation into practical improvements in service delivery. “CARE Month reminds us that we are in business because our customers choose us every day. It is our moment to celebrate their loyalty and to empower our people to serve them even better,” she said. Activities began with the company’s observance of the International Week of the Deaf through its Super Care initiative, which supports accessible and inclusive customer service. Telecel will also organise customer experience training, engagements between frontline staff and management, peer recognition programmes, mental health and wellness sessions, and team-building activities. According to the company, these interventions are intended to equip employees to respond more effectively to customers’ needs and strengthen collaboration across its operations. The Telecel Ghana Foundation will lead two community programmes in the Volta Region as part of the celebration. Students at the Volta School for the Deaf in Hohoe will receive practical science, technology, engineering and mathematics training to help develop their digital skills and broaden their future opportunities. In Ho, the Foundation will organise free community health screening, including breast cancer education and screening, to encourage preventive healthcare. Ms Akude said the campaign’s success would be measured by the value its activities bring to customers, staff and communities. “This month challenges us to go beyond good intentions and deliver care that counts – actions that create real, measurable value,” she said. Telecel Ghana says the month-long programme forms part of its wider efforts to strengthen customer relationships through closer engagement, timely responses and practical community support.

title: ECOWAS swears in five new judges, demands judicial independence
body: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, has sworn in five new judges of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, with calls for judicial independence, impartiality and stronger enforcement of the Court’s decisions. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye of Senegal and Chairman of the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government administered the oath to the judges on Tuesday at the ECOWAS Commission headquarters in Abuja. The new judges are Désiré Henri Aihou of Benin, Justice Awa Bah of The Gambia, Charlyne M. Brumskine of Liberia, Henrietta Uzoamaka Didigu of Nigeria and Dr. Yaouza Ouro-Sama of Togo. They were appointed for a non-renewable four-year term by the ECOWAS Authority at its 69th Ordinary Session held in Lungi, Sierra Leone, on July 19, 2026. Speaking at the ceremony, Faye charged the judges to remain impartial and resist pressure in the discharge of their judicial responsibilities. He said the oath they took was a solemn commitment to serve the cause of law with loyalty, honour, impartiality and conscience. Faye urged the judges to examine cases according to their conscience and perform their duties without giving in to pressure, regardless of its source. He said the new judges were assuming office at a time when West Africa was facing serious political, economic, security and environmental challenges. According to him, the challenges require a strong commitment to the rule of law. Faye described the Community Court of Justice as a key institution for protecting rights and ensuring respect for ECOWAS legal instruments. He urged the judges to strengthen the Court and make community justice more effective and accessible to citizens. He said, “The oath you have just taken must guide your every action.” Also speaking, President of the ECOWAS Judicial Council, Justice Komba Kamanda, called for stronger implementation of decisions of the Community Court. Kamanda said the regional judicial system could only be effective when Member States and ECOWAS institutions respected and enforced the Court’s decisions. He also called for stronger cooperation between the Community Court and national courts. Kamanda said the different judicial traditions within the region should not be seen as a problem. He urged the new judges to uphold judicial independence, impartiality and integrity throughout their tenure. He said the protection of fundamental rights must remain at the centre of community justice. Kamanda also reminded the judges that they had inherited the work of their predecessors and must strengthen the Court for future generations. The President of the ECOWAS Commission, Birame Diop, said the swearing-in was more than a formal ceremony. Diop said the oath showed the judges’ commitment to put aside personal interests and external influence in the service of community law. He said the Court had become one of the most accessible ECOWAS institutions because individuals could approach it when they believed their rights had been violated. Diop disclosed that ECOWAS was considering the establishment of an Appellate Chamber for the Court. He said a committee made up of representatives of ECOWAS institutions had been set up to examine the proposal. The five judges were appointed by the ECOWAS Authority at its 69th Ordinary Session in Lungi, Sierra Leone, on July 19, 2026. They replaced Justice Ricardo Cláudio Monteiro Gonçalves of Cape Verde, Justice Sengu Mohamed Koroma of Sierra Leone, Justice Dupe Atoki of Nigeria, Justice Gberi-Bè Ouattara of Côte d’Ivoire and Justice Edward Amoako Asante of Ghana, whose four-year tenure had ended. The appointments were made under the December 2025 Supplementary Act on the Community Court of Justice. The Act provides that judges must be persons of high moral character with the qualifications required for appointment to the Supreme Court or a similar court. They must also have at least 20 years of professional experience. Before assuming office, each judge is required to take an oath of office before the Chairman of the ECOWAS Authority. The five judges are expected to elect a president and vice-president from among themselves for a two-year term. title: Outrage over video showing FRSC officers allegedly beating motorist in Nasarawa
body:
A video showing officials of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) repeatedly hitting and kicking a man during a roadside encounter in Lafia, Nasarawa State, has triggered outrage online.
The incident reportedly occurred at about 8 a.m. on Tuesday along Makurdi Road in Lafia, with the man identified by his family as Hassan Babalawal.
The footage circulating online shows at least four men dressed in FRSC uniforms confronting Mr Babalawal, who is seen on the ground as some of the officials appear to punch and kick him.
A person filming the incident can be heard questioning the officials’ actions and saying the man had not fought them.
The video has prompted criticism from Nigerians who questioned the use of physical force by officials responsible for road safety and traffic enforcement.
The reactions have largely focused on the apparent imbalance between the officials and the man, particularly the footage showing him on the ground while the confrontation continued.
But the video does not establish what happened before the recording began or what prompted the confrontation.
Mr Babalawal’s elder brother told SaharaReporters that an FRSC patrol team stopped his brother along Makurdi Road before the confrontation.
He alleged that the officers assaulted Mr Babalawal despite the family being unaware of any offence he had committed.
The family said the incident caused Mr Babalawal physical and emotional distress and called on FRSC authorities to identify the officers captured in the footage and investigate their conduct.
The family also said it was prepared to provide photographs, medical reports, eyewitness accounts and other evidence that could assist an investigation.
“We are not seeking to obstruct the lawful duties of the FRSC,” the elder brother said, according to SaharaReporters. “Our concern is simply that no citizen should be subjected to unjustified physical assault or harassment.”
The family has specifically appealed to the FRSC Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, and the Nasarawa State Sector Commander to investigate the incident and take appropriate action if the officers are found to have acted unlawfully.
The incident has renewed questions about the conduct of uniformed personnel during roadside enforcement and the limits of force that may be used when motorists or other road users resist or dispute enforcement actions.
The FRSC is responsible for road safety administration, traffic management and enforcement of relevant road-traffic regulations. Its personnel are expected to carry out those duties professionally and within the law.
The Corps has previously investigated viral videos involving alleged misconduct by its personnel.
In one such case reported by PREMIUM TIMES, the FRSC said it investigated a viral video involving a confrontation between its officers and a tricycle rider and said disciplinary measures had been taken against staff involved in the incident.
PREMIUM TIMES contacted the spokesperson of the FRSC in Nasarawa State for the Corps’ reaction to the incident. He said the Sector Commander would issue a statement on the development.

title: Nicolas Maduro and wife charged with torturing US citizens in new indictment
body: Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were charged with conspiring to torture US citizens and others in a new indictment released on Thursday. Mr Maduro, who served as Venezuela 's president for about 13 years, and his wife were captured by US soldiers from the presidential compound in Caracas in early January, after they were indicted by Washington on drugs and weapons charges. Ms Flores was expected to appear in court on Thursday. The new indictment accuses Mr Maduro and Ms Flores of presiding over “a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention and the torture of detainees”. “That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families, including children,” it said. Victims of their alleged abuse included US citizens “believed to pose a threat” to Mr Maduro. “One particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles and forced injections,” the indictment said. The former Venezuelan president and his wife have been in custody awaiting trial in New York in the months since their capture. Both pleaded not guilty to the original indictment against them , under which they are accused of narco-terrorism, conspiracy to import cocaine, and possession of machine guns and destructive devices. Mr Maduro came to power in Venezuela in 2013, after the death of long-time leader Hugo Chavez. During his time in office, critics accused him and his administration of political repression, corruption and criminal activity, amid the country's economic collapse.

body:
